articleTitle: Optimal partitioning method among heterogeneous edge nodes in CNN models
abstract: In recent years, addressing the challenges of edge computing in executing complex CNN models has become crucial, with a focus on constructing lightweight models. While model compression can lead to accuracy degradation, model partitioning offers a method to reduce model size without compromising accuracy. This paper studies optimal partitioning methods between heterogeneous edge nodes, verifying the effectiveness through experiments.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation Metric for Rectangle Extended Object Tracking Based on Minkowski Distance
abstract: This paper aims to develop a new tracking performance evaluation metric for rectangle extended object tracking (REOT) methods, providing a more comprehensive and accurate performance assessment. Specifically, firstly, we introduce five indicators to assess the similarity between ground truth and the tracking results output by different REOT methods. Then, to more effectively evaluate the tracking performance of different REOT methods, we propose a novel evaluation metric. It simultaneously considers multiple indicators including angle, length, width, generalized intersection over union, and kinetic indicators. Then, it leverages the Minkowski distance for comprehensive performance evaluation. Moreover, it is capable of more holistically evaluation on the tracking performance of REOT methods, including many aspects such as shape changes and kinetic characteristics, which provides a powerful evaluation tool for the research of REOT methods.

articleTitle: Deep-TransVOD: Improved Video Object Detection with Low-Rank Tensor Decomposition
abstract: This study advances Video Object Detection (VOD) through optimization of the TransVOD Lite framework. Our enhancements utilize a Transformer Encoder to improve equivalent mapping and integrate low-rank matrix factorization, thereby eliminating the need for manual post-processing. This upgraded framework, named Deep-TransVOD, is detailed in this paper. It highlights improvements in feature extraction and the implementation of multi-frame input, resulting in a substantial advancement in real-time automated anomaly detection within industrial environments.

articleTitle: AgriGlow: An IoT Multi-Spectral Light Sensing Device for Distributed In-Greenhouse Monitoring
abstract: There is a need to reduce the operational costs of commercial greenhouses equipped with supplemental environmental controls. An effective method to achieve this is to create and deploy a set of distributed sensors that precisely measure the light received at different points in a greenhouse to determine if plants are receiving enough light, and only turning the lights on above those plants that are in deficit. This paper presents the AgriGlow IoT sensing device which is designed to measure the light spectrum and intensity for extended periods of time in a greenhouse scenario. This device is standalone, battery powered, and combines an 18-wavelength spectrum sensor, with a system on a chip for sensor integration and cloud connectivity. The fabrication details of this sensing device are presented as well as a set of experiments which are used to evaluate the potential effectiveness of the device in the required setting. The results clearly show that the device can operate for more than 11 days while measuring the intensity of 18 wavelengths of light spectrum every 15 minutes. This is a significant achievement that could lead to great improvements in greenhouse efficiency and productivity.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotional Understanding through Multimodal Fusion: A Dual Channel Approach with Self-Attention Mechanism and Transfer Learning
abstract: The understanding of emotions plays a pivotal role in a multitude of fields, including human-computer interaction, affective computing and human behaviour analysis. The intricacy and subtlety of emotional states are often challenging to capture with traditional single-mode approaches. With the advent of eye tracking technology and facial expression recognition, eye tracking and facial expression can be employed in conjunction with one another, collectively offering insights into emotions. The integration of these two types of information can provide a more comprehensive and accurate description of an individual’s emotional experience. A data collection experiment was designed using emotion theory in psychology. Three types of emotionally activated images (positive, neutral, and negative) were selected from the Chinese Emotion Image System (CAPS). In order to better capture the correlation and importance between different modal information, a system was designed to dynamically adjust the weights of different modal features through feature fusion using Self-Attention mechanism. A two-channel multimodal emotion recognition model based on Residual Neural Network (ResNet) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed. The network was initialised and trained on a large dataset using a transfer learning approach, and then tested by fine-tuning on the collected data. Finally, the model achieved an accuracy of ${9 6 . 2 8} \%$. The combination of eye movement signals and facial features improves the accuracy and robustness of emotion recognition compared to modality-based emotion recognition methods.

articleTitle: Identity Recognition through Anthropometric Feature Analysis of mmBody Data
abstract: With the development of biometrics, human feature recognition has become the focus of research. Traditional methods such as facial recognition and fingerprint recognition face challenges in low-light and non-contact environments. This study introduces a method for identification using human features extracted from mmBody data. The study focuses on extracting features from the upper body, such as head and neck length, upper body length and arm length. These measurements are combined to form feature sets. The validity of these features was verified experimentally and the feature pattern with the highest recognition rate was identified. For model training, algorithms such as feature matching and converter models were explored and evaluated through crossvalidation to ensure the robustness of the approach. The study utilized the mmBody dataset for experiments. The method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional biometric methods and provide a reliable alternative for authentication in challenging environments such as low-light conditions or where contactless identification is required.

articleTitle: Simulating a Multi-Agent UAV System Coordinated by State Machines Using Godot
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles have advanced quickly and are now a dominant force in several domains, including military, security, and even logistics. 3D simulations with virtual environments are cost effective tools for assessing feasibility and costs of developing new systems or upgrading current systems. This is especially true for multiagent or swarm systems that require many agents working in concert. The total costs can be much higher when only physical prototypes are used for testing and analysis. There are existing 3D libraries for aiding with UAV simulations, but they’re too specialized; it is difficult to create highly customized virtual environments with these packages. A simulation development framework needs to be capable and stable for accurate simulations yet generalized enough that any types of simulations can be developed without exhausting efforts. This paper explores the feasibility and ease of using Godot, an open-source game engine, to develop a simulation that can assess the function of a multiagent UAV system. It is found that the Godot engine is a powerful tool that is both accurate and generalized enough to develop highly customizable UAV simulation. This allows verification and testing of UAV designs and control algorithms in highly customizable and flexible virtual environments, using a free open-sourced tool.

articleTitle: A Load Balancing Mechanism Based on Non-Cooperative Game in Traffic Environment
abstract: Multi-controller resource scheduling problem is crucial in the edge computing. Nonetheless, since the network has to be constantly scaled up to match the increasing application’s diversity and complexity, the original SDN with single controller suffers from the problem of lower processing capacity of the control plane in the edge computing environments. The currently popular solution in the literature tends to deploy multiple controllers to form a distributed control plane, while this method may lead to the load imbalance among controllers, bringing about the large network latency and low resource utilization. In this paper, to balance the load among controllers, we propose ATS-NCGT, which is an Adaptive Traffic Scheduling algorithm based on the Non-Cooperative Game Theory. We consider the load balancing problem of multi-controller as a non-cooperative game according to the interaction characteristics between the switches and the controllers. We also design a hybrid genetic algorithm based on simulated annealing to improve the optimization accuracy and convergence speed in the solving process. The simulation results demonstrate that our scheme is effective in terms of improving the load-balancing rate and lowering the controller response delay, even in the case of high request rate.

articleTitle: Exploring Environment and Behavior Logic in Virtual Space Through MMOG game map design
abstract: Contemporary MMOG game map is comparable to urban and architecture design due to the increasing size and complexity. To enhance the possibility of social interaction, the spatial layout of buildings its surrounding areas in the MMOG map are resemble to the real world. This paper introduces a design studio of 4th year architecture student of BJTU. Using space syntax theory and method, the social logic of spatial distribution of NPC in capital cities and the synchronized “quest-NPC-place” network in World Of Warcraft are analyzed as an example. Students select games based on their own interest. They are encouraged to conduct similar analysis and do one area map design. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the analytical method, and the forementioned logics in WOW could also be found in other games.

Author Keywords: Environment and Behavior in Virtual Space

articleTitle: The Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolution Network for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification
abstract: Static Functional Brain Networks (FBNs) capture the functional connectivity patterns of the brain, which have proven to be highly discriminatory in identifying brain diseases. However, static FBNs overlook temporal variations that can potentially impact classification performance. To address this limitation, we propose a grey and white matter dynamic FBN approach that utilizes spatially independent component analysis and sliding window techniques to capture temporal changes in fMRI data for Alzheimer’s disease classification. By extracting spatial topological features and global information through a graph-attentive convolution mechanism and a temporal convolution residual module, we are able to comprehensively represent the dynamic nature of the brain’s functional connectivity. Experiments conducted on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that our proposed method, which fuses grey and white matter dynamic FBN features, outperforms most existing techniques, highlighting its potential for improving the accuracy of Alzheimer’s disease classification.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin for Pest Population Monitoring
abstract: An improved understanding of pest population dynamics is critical for more informed and effective management of agricultural pests. A Digital Twin (DT) that spatially visualises pest population dynamic modelling and monitoring, has great potential for facilitating effective and collaborative pest management. We have developed a proof-of-concept DT of agricultural pest monitoring that provides dynamic and real-time estimates of pest population throughout an agricultural landscape, while accounting for weather, land-use and pest control methods being applied. This proof-of-concept DT demonstrates both the viability and suitability of the DT framework for agricultural pest monitoring and management; it also showcases the potential of DTs as valuable decision-support tools in the agricultural landscape.

articleTitle: Real-time Determination and Correction of Multi-source Multi-modal Heterogeneous Data Quality
abstract: With the rapid development of industrial informatization, digital twins have achieved comprehensive dynamic simulation in the production and manufacturing processes in digital form. They cover the entire product lifecycle and the entire industrial chain, which is of significant importance in promoting the development of future intelligent manufacturing. Digital twin workshops measure the multidimensional attributes of the production process by deploying multiple independent heterogeneous data sources, resulting in multi-source, multi-modal heterogeneous perception data. However, due to inherent limitations of equipment and environmental noise, perception equipment inevitably encounters issues such as missed reads, multiple reads, and incorrect reads, leading to common data quality problems. Therefore, this paper focuses on the twin workshop as the main subject and multi-source, multi-modal heterogeneous perception data as the object.It explores critical technologies such as real-time data collection and data quality control during the production process. These technologies enable the assessment and optimization of real-time data quality, ensuring the generation of high-quality digital twin models.This allows the workshop to operate accurately and efficiently, providing a reference for advancing the research and application of digital twin technology in future manufacturing industries.

articleTitle: Creating and preserving the architectural heritage and environment of ancient towers in the game space based on digital measurement and computing technology: Fangshan Ancient Pagoda, Beijing
abstract: The application of digital technology in the field of architectural heritage conservation allows real world scenes to be quickly transformed into game assets. This paper takes the ancient pagoda in Fangshan District of Beijing as the research object. Through case analysis, data collection, data processing and other methods, three-dimensional reconstruction technology is used to transform the ancient pagoda architectural heritage into a virtual scene that can be used in games. The purpose is to summarize the work flow of data collection and processing in the digitization of heritage, carry out virtual restoration of ancient pagoda and backup protection of real heritage environment with the help of virtual space. We find that the scientific and efficient heritage image acquisition strategy guarantees the efficiency and accuracy of 3D reconstruction. Immersive heritage environments combined with interactive games can be both an excellent heritage preservation method and an effective educational and cultural communication strategy.

articleTitle: Identification of Starch Types by Using Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy Combined with SG-KNN
abstract: The terahertz (THz) spectra of four different types of starch were investigated by terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS). Subsequently, standard normal variate (SNV) and savitzky-golay (SG) were used to remove the interference of spectral noise, and then a K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) method was applied to identify the four types of starch. The results showed that the samples were identified with average accuracy, Kappa, and F1 scores for the test set were $0.9375,0.9158$, and 0.9383, respectively. This method was also contrasted with logistic regression (LR). The comparisons demonstrated that SG-KNN surpassed the other methods and indicated that the integration of THz technology with SG-KNN was an effective approach for identifying starch types.

articleTitle: A Data Grading Privacy Preservation Method for Intelligent Connected Vehicle
abstract: During the design, development, and operational phases of intelligent connected vehicles (ICVs), an increased amount of data is required to be published. This raises privacy concerns for drivers, as ICV data contain rich sensitive information, such as mileage, battery energy information, and fuel level. To address these concerns, local differential privacy techniques have been developed. These techniques aim to balance data utility and privacy preservation and have shown positive results in the big data domain. Building on these techniques, this paper introduces a data grading privacy preservation method to enhance the privacy preservation of vehicle data published. This method employs the $\mathbf{k}$-anonymity mathematical framework and information entropy to grade data attributes into different levels. It then integrates the sensitivity into the differential privacy budget. It achieves adaptive privacy preservation of data attributes in multiple aspects. Differential privacy based on the Laplace noise mechanism is employed to safeguard data security. Experiments show that the method proposed in this paper excels in reducing error and re-identification risk.

articleTitle: A Grasping Posture Selection Method Based on Large Language Model
abstract: Large Language Models exhibit excellent generalization capabilities, particularly in their ability to semantically analyze and perceive new concepts. This potential can be harnessed to enhance the cognitive abilities of robots in tasks such as grasping decision-making. However, despite the semantic understanding LLMs provide, the process of transitioning from text-based instances generated by LLMs to actual item instance grasping decisions is fraught with challenges. These challenges include multi-instance selection and the absence of a unified framework paradigm that allows for modular and interchangeable decision-making processes related to grasping gestures. In this paper, a layered architecture is proposed that addresses these challenges by incorporating hot-swappable modules. This architecture integrates LLMs, visual perception, and grasping gesture decision-making to enable embodied intelligence to perform grasping tasks effectively. By utilizing the current pretrained foundation models, our approach benefits from the advantages of requiring no fine-tuning and permitting hot-pluggable modules. The feasibility of our architecture has been validated through real photo experiments, demonstrating its practical applicability.

articleTitle: Evaluate the Winter Wheat GVMI and NDMI correlations with the Rainfall
abstract: With the recent application of digital twin systems in smart agriculture, the intricate relationships between different data types have become increasingly significant, particularly the correlation between satellite data and weather data. This correlation is a critical aspect of advanced agricultural monitoring. This study examined the relationship between two satellitederived indices, GVMI and NDMI, which reflect leaf moisture content, and rainfall. Our analysis reveals a strong correlation between GVMI and NDMI, with a coefficient as high as 0.97, while their correlation with rainfall is minimal. Consequently, future research will further explore the impact of rainfall on these indices. Specifically, we investigated whether substantial increases in these indices are linked to rainfall and examined the correlation between their growth rates and rainfall. Our findings indicate that approximately 70% of significant increases are attributed to rainfall. Additionally, due to the inherent lag in satellite data’s response to rainfall-—here substantial changes may not be immediate but require some time to manifest—we explored the time lag needed for significant changes in NDMI and GVMI to occur after rainfall. The results demonstrate that NDMI is more sensitive and reacts more quickly to rainfall, with $\mathbf{9 2 \%}$ of the data showing significant increases or decreases within two days following rainfall, compared to $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ for GVMI.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis of Rendering Optimization Methods in Unity Tuanjie Engine, Unity Global and Unreal Engine
abstract: In the field of computer game development, Unity Technologies’ game engine has a Chinese version called Tuanjie, developed by Unity China and officially released in January 2024. Tuanjie customizes with exclusive rendering optimization techniques such as a Nanite-like Virtual Geometry (VG) for geometric complexity optimization. While the VG system has garnered global attention, comprehensive performance comparisons with other Level of Detail (LOD) systems remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by constructing a benchmark scene with ten 3D mesh models (each containing 3 million polygons) to analyze the VG system’s performance thoroughly. We conducted performance tests comparing the built-in LOD system of Unity Global, the VG of the Tuanjie engine and Nanite of Unreal Engine 5 (UE5). The data of GPU, CPU, and RAM usage along with FPS was collected and analyzed every 100 milliseconds over 4 minutes, yielding 2400 data points per engine. The comparative studies were conducted at five viewing distances (i.e. $0 \text{m}, 100 \text{m}, 200 \text{m}$, $300 \text{m}, 400 \text{m}$) and with an empty scene. The results validate that UE5’s Nanite system remains superior performance compared to both Tuanjie’s VG and Unity Global’s LOD systems. Moreover, Tuanjie’s VG system outperforms Unity Global’s LOD system in rendering distant objects while underperforming when rendering close objects. This comprehensive comparison highlights the strengths and weaknesses of each LOD system in our scenario. We hope the results can shed some light for researchers and game developers in the fields of game design and computer graphics development.

articleTitle: Research Progress and Challenges in Grain Storage Temperature Detection
abstract: The grain storage temperature has a significant impact on the grain quality and safety. Thus, reliable and accurate detection of storage temperature forms an essential aspect of scientific grain management. Substantial progress has been made in grain storage temperature detection methods due to continuous advancements in sensor technology and microcomputer technology. This paper reviews the current state of traditional contact-based and emerging non-contact grain storage temperature detection technologies. It summarizes various detection methods and analyzes their strengths and drawbacks. Furthermore, it provides an outlook on the future development of grain storage temperature detection technologies, aiming to offer new research directions and a foundation for advancements towards higher precision, faster detection times, and broader adaptability in grain storage temperature monitoring.

articleTitle: Exploring Physiological and Psychological Responses to Different Types of Green and Blue Spaces through Two Virtual Media
abstract: The rapid urbanization of modern society has led to various physiological and psychological public health problems. Numerous theoretical and empirical studies have demonstrated that exposure to natural environments benefits public health and well-being. The recent emergence of digital media, such as virtual reality (VR) and digital images (DI) that simulate green and blue spaces, allows individuals to experience “virtual nature” without extensive travel. However, more evidence is needed to understand better the physiological and psychological health impacts of different virtual green and blue spaces presented by different virtual media forms. This study aims to explore physiological and psychological responses to three kinds of natural green spaces (NGS), natural blue spaces (NBS), and artificial green-blue spaces (AGBS) through two media forms, namely, DI and immersive VR in a controlled lab environment. We recruited 38 participants for our experiment. During the experiment, wireless sensors were used to measure their stress levels by monitoring skin conductance levels. At the same time, their psychological responses were collected using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory and Perceived Restorativeness Scale Questionnaire. The results showed that experiencing virtual blue and green spaces could provide physiological and psychological health benefits regarding stress recovery, but the benefits were stronger in the psychological aspect. We also found that NBS resulted in a significant decrease in the skin conductance level compared with NGS and AGBS. Our findings open new avenues for nature-based interventions and urban policies to promote health and well-being.

articleTitle: Locally Private Estimator for Degree Distribution with Laplacian Mechanism
abstract: Local differential privacy (LDP) provides a solution such that an untrusted server can achieve privacy-preserving data analysis. Node degree is one of the most fundamental metrics in graph data analysis. Existing LDP-based methods can not balance degree distribution estimation and degree distribution characteristic estimation. In this paper, we propose a local private estimator for degree distribution with Laplacian mechanism (LEDL), which uses elastic net regression to estimate the degree distribution, selects the regularization weight to prevent overfitting or underfitting. We can aslo adopt the existing method to calculate degree distribution characteristics according to data with Laplacian noise. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of LEDL in degree distribution and Laplacian mechanism in degree distribution characteristic estimation, six metrics are applied across four datasets.

articleTitle: Meta-Path-Based Multiple Instance Learning with Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for lncRNA-disease Association Prediction
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (IncRNAs) are involved in the development and progression of numerous diseases. Predicting associations between IncRNAs and diseases is crucial for uncovering their molecular mechanisms and devising new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. However, conventional biological methods are time-consuming, expensive, and frequently produce inadequate outcomes. Thus, there is an urgent requirement for a predictive approach that comprehensively captures associations between entities and delves into network topology for IncRNA-disease prediction. We present a method called HGCNMRD, utilizing a heterogeneous graph neural network and meta-pathcentered deep multi-instance learning. This method builds a heterogeneous network by incorporating similarities between IncRNAs and diseases along with established associations. Instances are generated through meta-path creation, and attention mechanisms are applied to assess various meta-paths, yielding interpretable association probabilities. We performed 5 -fold and $\mathbf{1 0}$-fold cross-validation experiments on the IncRNA-Disease 2.0 dataset, illustrating HGCNMRD’s superior performance over alternative models and its ability to identify potential IncRNA-disease associations. We conducted case studies on breast and lung cancers on benchmark datasets, and as a result observed that authoritative databases all confirmed the top 10 ranked IncRNAs.

articleTitle: Shape Topology-Driven Network for Unsupervised Keypoint Detection
abstract: 3D keypoints provide an intuitive abstraction that facilitates the shape representation and plays a fundamental role in various downstream tasks. Although the existing methods tend to detect reliable and repeatable points, they only take the spatial relations between points into account and overlook the underlying topological structures of diverse shapes. Thus, we propose an unsupervised framework that leverages the skeletal outline of a shape to guide the detection of salient points. The skeletal representation enables the proposed network to capture the intrinsic topology of the point cloud. We first employ a DGCNN-like encoder to extract the point-wise features and then form a mask to predict the locations of keypoints. To take advantage of the neighboring information in skeletonization, we introduce a local topology construction strategy that associates the detected points with the regional structures. Finally, the skeletal outline is constructed by rationally connecting the keypoints and applied to refine the keypoint detection. Extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework in detecting keypoints and producing expressive skeletal representations keypoints labels and are robust to noise.

articleTitle: Task Allocation for Heterogeneous UAV Swarms under Communication Constraints
abstract: This paper investigates the task assignment problem in the collaborative reconnaissance and strike processes of UAV swarms. Addressing challenges such as limited communication distance and heavy communication load, a consensus-based contract net allocation algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a distributed task allocation model for UAV swarms is established, and a manager UAV selection method based on set covering theory is proposed to achieve information consistency in the local communication network. Secondly, by introducing the consensus algorithm, the problems of repeated UAV invocation and task assignment in multi-manager allocation schemes are solved, achieving conflict resolution among UAVs. Simulation results show that this algorithm can solve the task allocation problem of UAV swarms under communication constraints, outperforming classic contract net algorithm and auction algorithm with fewer communication times.

articleTitle: MCSFF: Multi-modal Consistency and Specificity Fusion Framework for Entity Alignment
abstract: Multi-modal entity alignment (MMEA) is essential for enhancing knowledge graphs and improving information retrieval and question-answering systems. Existing methods often focus on integrating modalities through their complementarity but overlook the specificity of each modality, which can obscure crucial features and reduce alignment accuracy. To solve this, we propose the Multi-modal Consistency and Specificity Fusion Framework (MCSFF), which innovatively integrates both complementary and specific aspects of modalities. We utilize Scale Computing’s hyper-converged infrastructure to optimize IT management and resource allocation in large-scale data processing. Our framework first computes similarity matrices for each modality using modality embeddings to preserve their unique characteristics. Then, an iterative update method denoises and enhances modality features to fully express critical information. Finally, we integrate the updated information from all modalities to create enriched and precise entity representations. Experiments show our method outperforms current state-of-theart MMEA baselines on the MMKG dataset, demonstrating its effectiveness and practical potential.

articleTitle: Structure tensor based multi-exposure images fusion in gradient domain
abstract: A multi-exposure image fusion algorithm is proposed. The algorithm is developed for color images and processed in YCbCr space, and the luminance and chromatic components are processed respectively. For processing the luminance components, the structure tensor representation is first utilized to blend the gradients of the luminance components from the input images. The fused luminance is then derived by solving a Poisson equation on the fused gradient field. Finally, it is refined through gamma correction and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization to yield the final luminance component. In processing the chromatic components, the fused chromatic components are obtained by weighted blending of the chromatic channels. Experimental results show that the method not only captures details in both bright and dark areas but also displays the colors of the observed scene excellently and naturally.

articleTitle: A Speech Dataset for Snoring Detection in Sleep Based on Deep Learning
abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Hypopnea Syndrome (OSAHS) is a common sleep disorder that affects the health and quality of life of millions of people worldwide. Traditional methods for diagnosing OSAHS, such as polysomnography (PSG), are widely recognized but have drawbacks such as high cost, operational complexity, and inconvenience to patients. Snoring sound detection methods based on deep learning offer a low-cost and convenient alternative for OSAHS diagnosis. However, these methods often require large amounts of data for training, and the lack of datasets severely hinders the development of snoring recognition. In this study, we aim to construct a comprehensive snoring audio dataset to support research and diagnosis of OSAHS. This dataset includes four categories: non-snoring, normal snoring, abnormal snoring, and breathing sounds. We utilize four signal processing algorithms—Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), and Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC)—to extract features from the audio. These extracted features are then evaluated using 12 state-of-the-art (SOTA) classification models. Experimental results demonstrate that this dataset can achieve high accuracy across most classification models. We believe this dataset can provide valuable reference and support for related research.

articleTitle: Motifs-Based Multi-Scale Graph Convolution Learning Framework for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Classification
abstract: Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder. Recent studies suggest functional brain networks could provide crucial insights for diagnosing ADHD. However, most of these studies primarily focus on functional connections, often overlooking complex higher-order spatial topological relationships among brain regions. To address this limitation, a Motifs-based Multi-scale Graph Convolution (MMGC) model is proposed to enhance feature representations by aggregating spatial features from neighboring nodes across various higher-order relationships. Our experiments indicate the effectiveness of the proposed network, achieving an average accuracy of $\mathbf{7 2. 0 4} \%$, thereby outperforming traditional brain network classification methods.

articleTitle: An Elastic LatticeKrig Generative Model for Non-ideal Spatial Datasets
abstract: When datasets have missing parts, we typically use data characteristics to select a suitable model to generate these missing parts. However, the poor quality of real data often affects the fitting accuracy of the ideal model, leading to lower-thanexpected results. In this paper, we improve the LatticeKrig model by using local basis function spanning. This enhancement aims to improve the model’s fitting ability and robustness to poor quality data while avoiding potential overfitting. In our experiment, we demonstrated the model’s fitting ability with ideal data and used it to fit the missing parts of garbage collection data from the Norwegian coast. The results show that our improved model achieves better fitting performance with non-ideal data.

articleTitle: A Study on Classification of Tor Encrypted Traffic Based on Mamba
abstract: Network traffic classification is an important and fundamental work to ensure network security and network management in an orderly manner, and traffic classification of darknet encrypted traffic with high degree of encryption mainly in Tor network has always been a very challenging task, the most mainstream Transformer as the core model is often inefficient although the classification effect is very good, in the text, we try to use the Mamba as the core model to perform the Tor network encrypted traffic classification task by by pre-training and fine-tuning, A small improvement in classification results and an improvement in performance on the ISCX-Tor dataset.

articleTitle: An adaptive weight mechanism for recognizing unknown samples in remote sensing scene images
abstract: Recognizing unknown classes enables the model to distinguish between samples of categories that exist in the test set but not in the training set, which is a crucial skill for open-set domain adaptation and other open-set deep learning tasks. These tasks better aligns with real-world application needs. However, research on remote sensing image scene classification is less prevalent compared to natural images. This paper designs an adaptive weight mechanism to help identify samples belonging to unknown classes in remote sensing scene images. Specifically, we fully utilize global and local features, employing two classifiers to analyze the similarity of samples and known categories from the perspectives of the overall category space and individual categories. The higher the obtained weight, the more likely the sample is to be recognized as an unknown class. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for remote sensing scene image classification compared to other open-set domain adaptation methods.

articleTitle: Vessel Trajectory Prediction Based on Context-Assisted Information
abstract: In this paper, aiming at the problem of vessel trajectory prediction, a Context-Assisted Long Short-Term Memory Network (CA-LSTM) is proposed to process historical trajectories of vessel navigation as well as contextual information such as water depth, water temperature, wind speed, wind direction, wave height, and wave direction to solve the problem of high accumulated errors and low accuracy of ship trajectory long-term prediction results caused by differences in navigation strategies. The method first utilizes the water depth data, which directly affects vessel navigation, to establish a depth penalty function that constrains the area of vessel trajectory prediction. Subsequently, for other contextual information like water temperature et al that indirectly affects vessel navigation, an encoder-decoder architecture is constructed to extract the implicit features that influence the vessel's trajectory. Finally, experiments conducted on actual AIS datasets have demonstrated that the proposed method possesses superior predictive capabilities compared to other representative vessel trajectory prediction methods.

articleTitle: Trajectory and Communication Resources Planning for Dual-UAV Data Collection
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be utilized in communication uncovered areas for data collection. This paper studies two UAVs collaborating to collect data from sensors, with one UAV relaying the data to an information center through the other UAV. To shorten task completion time for UAVs, a particle swarm optimization-based method for task allocation and initial trajectories planning of UAVs is first proposed in the paper. Building upon this, this paper proposes a joint planning of communication resources for all sensors and UAVs, as well as trajectories for two UAVs. Due to the complex nature of the proposed problem, an algorithm based on block coordinate descent algorithm is proposed. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm shortens the task completion time compared to other algorithm.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models for Activity Recognition and Fall Detection Using FMCW Radar
abstract: Activity recognition and fall detection play a pivotal role in ensuring the health and safety of elderly individuals and patients. Traditional monitoring methods, such as wearable devices and camera-based systems, present inherent drawbacks, including user discomfort and privacy concerns. In contrast, Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar offers a non-intrusive and privacy-preserving solution for human activity monitoring. This paper proposes a deep learning-based framework for activity recognition (including fall detection) utilizing FMCW radar data. Data were collected using the Texas Instruments IWR6843AoP radar sensor, and the performance of six different models—VGG16, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, Efficient-NetB0, DenseNet121, and a custom CNN—was evaluated. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach achieves high accuracy in distinguishing between various activities. Notably, the ResNet50 model outperformed the others, particularly in subject-independent validation settings. These findings highlight the potential of radar-based contactless methods for reliable and efficient activity monitoring.

articleTitle: Multi-Step ENSO Forecasting Using Kolmogorove Arnold Networks
abstract: ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation) is a global climatic phenomenon that affects weather, agriculture, water supplies, and economies worldwide. Effective planning and mitigation need accurate ENSO forecasts. This study introduces the Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Time Series Forecasting (KAN-TSF), which improves multi-step ENSO forecasting by combining KANs with LSTM networks’ gating mechanism. We present a multi-step time series forecasting model to capture detailed temporal patterns and manage non-linearity of time series data. The model is tested using ENSO dataset for ONI patterns from January 1950 to June 2024. KAN-TSF was compared to CNN, RNN, LSTM, and CNN-LSTM. The findings shows that KAN-TSF can successfully forecast ENSO trends over numerous time steps with the greatest R-squared value (0.902), lowest Loss (0.003), MAE (0.043), MAPE (12.220), and RMSE (0.056) among the other models, thereby demonstrating its superior capacity to accurately predict ONI patterns over multiple time steps.

articleTitle: Modeling of All Mutant and Wild Protein Structures Using Metaverse ESM: Surface Area Analysis and Implications
abstract: The integration of virtual reality and advanced modeling platforms in the Metaverse has revolutionized the way biochemical data is visualized and analyzed. Specifically, the Evolutionary Scale Modeling (ESM) within the Metaverse provides an innovative environment for simulating and examining protein structures, allowing for both mutant and wild type analyses. Traditional bioinformatics tools often require substantial computational resources and can be limited in interactive capabilities, posing challenges in rapidly modeling variations in protein structures, especially for educational and research purposes in the Metaverse. This study exploits the capabilities of the Metaverse ESM to generate and analyze surface area models of all mutant and wild protein structures. We applied logistic regression, a robust machine learning method, to classify residues based on their surface area characteristics such as total, apolar, backbone, and sidechain areas. This approach facilitated a streamlined analysis directly within the Metaverse platform, enhancing accessibility and interactive learning. Our model achieved perfect classification metrics-accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of 1.0—highlighting the effectiveness of combining Metaverse ESM tools with machine learning. The ROC curve further demonstrated the model’s exceptional discriminative ability with an AUC of 1.0, supported by a clear and accurate confusion matrix. The successful implementation of logistic regression for protein surface analysis within the Metaverse showcases the potential for these technologies to simplify and enhance biochemical education and research. This paves the way for broader applications of virtual reality in scientific studies, making complex molecular biology concepts more accessible and engaging through immersive experiences.

articleTitle: Efficient and Verifiable Federated Learning Based on Blockchain
abstract: Federated learning (FL) breaks the data island crisis and enables a large number of users to collaboratively train a global model. The existing federated learning schemes have low efficiency in secure aggregation, and users have to trust a single server. To address the above issues, we propose an efficient and verifiable federated learning scheme based on blockchain. First, blockchain and smart contract are used to implement multi-user collaborative training without a trusted center. Second, double masking and homogeneous linear recursion based secret sharing are used to achieve the goal of protecting user privacy and improving aggregation efficiency. Finally, we verify the correctness of the aggregation results using vector homomorphic hashing and smart contract. Security analysis proves the confidentiality and verifiability of the scheme. Simulation results show that the efficiency is improved by about $47 \%$ compared with the existing scheme.

articleTitle: RFNet: A Redundancy-Reduced and Frequency-Aware Feature Fusion Network for RGB-T Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Traditional semantic segmentation approaches primarily utilize RGB images, which struggle in complex scenes. To address this challenge, the multi-modal solution that fuses RGB and thermal (RGB-T) images can exploit the advantages of these modalities to improve accuracy and stability of segmentation. However, how to effectively fuse multi-modal and multi-level features remains a significant challenge. To this end, a Redundancy-Reduced and Frequency-Aware Feature Fusion Network (RFNet) is proposed. The RFNet employs a dual-stream encoder-decoder architecture to separately handle the extracted features from two modalities. This network reduces redundancy in shallow feature fusion and integrates frequency-aware attention mechanisms in deep feature fusion, efficiently capturing complementary information from multi-modal and multi-level features. Experiments on the MFNet dataset indicate that RFNet outperforms the majority of current networks in terms of segmentation performance.

articleTitle: Basic study on improving the efficiency of pantograph slider inspection operations using SfM
abstract: In Japan, electric train inspections and maintenance involve workers climbing onto the roof and visually inspecting the wear of the pantographs' current collector strips. To conduct this work safely and efficiently, inspection methods using sensors are being developed. However, existing methods assume daytime inspections and face challenges related to sunlight conditions. Therefore, if measurements can be taken at night or indoors, where changes in sunlight conditions are minimal, it would contribute to the efficiency of inspections. In this study, we proposed a method to measure the wear of current collector strips at night by projecting patterns onto the strips and generating a point cloud from multi-view images of the projected patterns on the strips. In a demonstration experiment, we used current collector strips that were actually in use by the railway company to confirm the presence of wear. As a result, it was found that the proposed method can determine the wear amount of the current collector strips with an accuracy of about 1 mm when the vehicle is stationary.

articleTitle: Layered implementation of power grid connected renewable energy digital twin
abstract: As application services utilizing replication of virtual space expand in industrial technology areas such as energy, smart cities, manufacturing, and the environment, interest in digital twins is increasing day by day. The evolution of digital twin was classified into stages according to factors such as autonomy, federation. Recently, a method of classifying the degree of evolution according to the technical implementation layer was proposed. In this paper, we introduce a test bed of digital twin that composed of renewable energy sources linked to the power grid according to the layered implementation approach. The test bed is performing real-time monitoring and analysis through linkage with the weather environment, and aims to evolve to a higher level in the future.

articleTitle: Edge-Enabled Data-Centric Dynamic Node Trust Evaluation
abstract: Recent advancements in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) and Digital Twins (DT) offer significant benefits in smart cities and industrial automation. However, integrating these technologies with physical space introduces numerous security threats. Towards these challenges, we propose an edge-enabled data-centric dynamic trust evaluation model for perception nodes. This model integrates real-time metrics such as node interaction behaviors and quantified data accuracy with historical trust records, facilitating dynamic assessment of node reliability. Moreover, the model reduces the risk of misidentifying incidental anomalies as malicious nodes, thereby mitigating the impacts of inaccurate data and anomaly interaction behavior. Experimental validation using data from weather information system (RWIS) units along the Wuyu Highway in Shanxi Province demonstrates the model’s effectiveness in detecting anomalies like packet loss, replay attacks, data modification, and on-off attacks, ensuring system integrity.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin System for Predictive Maintenance of Complex Equipment
abstract: Predictive maintenance of equipment is a very important task in the Industrial Internet and plays an important role in maintaining the safety of industrial production. Digital twins are an important tool and technical basis for predictive maintenance. However, the continuous changing in the operational status of equipment pose a challenge to predictive maintenance based on digital twins, because most methods do not consider the evolution of digital twin systems. Therefore, this paper proposes a digital twin system framework for predictive maintenance of equipment. This framework achieves high-precision and adaptive monitoring of equipment with changing working conditions through highly generalized modeling, AI-based data generation for unknown scene perception, and dynamic evolution of prediction models based on continuous learning. Finally, the future directions of predictive maintenance is outlooked.

articleTitle: Consideration of Road Feature Extraction Using Low-Cost LiDAR Mounted in a Vehicle
abstract: Surveying by mobile mapping systems (MMS), terrestrial laser scanners (TLS), and portable laser devices is widely used in public works projects in Japan, resulting in the accumulation of vast amounts of point cloud data in various locations. A point cloud is a collection of three-dimensional points and is increasingly being used as the base data for the digital twinning of roads and urban spaces. However, since each point does not retain the attributes of the road features, a structured semantic point cloud for each road feature is required. Therefore, the authors have developed semantic point clouds that can be used for the maintenance and inspection of road features using road drawings, road maps for autonomous driving, and deep learning techniques. Conversely, continuous measurement of roads and urban spaces by laser scanning is necessary to monitor changes in the road features. While MMS, the mainstream laser measurement method, can capture highdensity point clouds, it is expensive to deploy and requires frequent measurements. In this study, we employed a low-cost LiDAR, which can easily measure point clouds, to generate area data of road features and extract these features from the point clouds. Consequently, we were able to extract road features with an average F-measure of 0.800 or higher, indicating that the point cloud data measured by the low-cost LiDAR can be effectively structured according to the road features.

articleTitle: Effective Human Intervention in AI and Beyond: A High-Level Framework
abstract: Computing plays a critical role in today’s world, making it essential to ensure its safe, beneficial, responsible, and morally sound design and use. This is especially true for AI applications. This paper presents a framework outlining four preconditions for effective human intervention in complex systems: epistemic access, self-control, causal power, and fitting intentions. Together, these elements enable individuals to increase the likelihood of achieving a given desideratum. The framework is applied to various normative domains, such as law, morality, and rationality. We also discuss the role of explainability using the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Object Detection In Complex Background Based In Heterogeneous Information Fusion
abstract: With the rapid development of UAV technology, UAVs will play a pivotal role in the future of warfare and commercialisation, making the rapid and accurate detection of UAVs an important and challenging problem. However, due to the small size of UAVs and the presence of natural environments or building obstructions in complex backgrounds, or poorly lit nightt me conditions, detection using only a single visible light is not efective. Unlike visible light mages, infrared images can distinguish the radiation differences between different objects, thus helping the detector to better distinguish different objects from the background, which can solve the problem of not detecting UAVs in complex backgrounds. Therefore, based on the deep learningframework, thispaper combines the advantages of visible images rich in UAV texture details and infrared images rich in thermal radiation information to carry out research on visible and infrared non-aligned image fusion detection under complex backgrounds, and in response to the use of a single visible light to detect UAVs subject to the limitations of the background light and other limitations that lead to the target leakage detection, this paper proposes a method based on joint infrared-visible light detection. On the basis of the classical algorithm YOLOv5 for target detection, the backbone network is improved, and a two-channel multi-source input detection network R-IDC YOLOv5_1 containing a featurefusion module is designed, which introduces a new infrared information input channel under the premise of the original single visible light information input, and increases the feature splicing module to achieve the fusion of infrared and visible light data in the feature layer, making it possible for the detector to be used for UAV detection. The accuracy of the detector on UAV detection is improved compared to a single source.

articleTitle: Development of a speech dataset for emotion recognition and analysis
abstract: In recent years, with the development of technologies such as signal processing, machine learning, and deep learning, speech emotion recognition has found wide applications in mental health, educational training, and social media analysis. However, current methods for speech emotion recognition mostly rely on data-driven models, and the lack of emotional speech datasets significantly hinders their progress. To address this issue, this paper proposes an emotional speech dataset consisting of 6,447 audio clips for emotion recognition and analysis. The dataset includes five emotional categories: happy, sad, surprised, fearful, and angry. In addition, four speech signal processing algorithms including Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), and Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) are utilized for feature extraction, resulting in the creation of four emotional feature image datasets. Furthermore, eleven state-of-the-art (SOTA) classification models are selected to establish a benchmark. Experimental results show that most classification models achieve accurate recognition performance on the proposed emotional speech dataset. It is believed that the proposed dataset and benchmark can promote the research and development of emotion recognition and analysis.

articleTitle: Harnessing Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentiment Analysis of Tweets on the Metaverse
abstract: In the digital era, understanding public sentiment towards emerging technologies such as the Metaverse is crucial for businesses and developers. Traditional sentiment analysis methods often struggle to accurately interpret the nuances of digital communication, particularly when assessing rapid technological advancements. This study harnesses the power of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to address this challenge, focusing on sentiment analysis of tweets related to the Metaverse. By employing advanced preprocessing techniques including tokenization and vectorization, and by using a CNN model, we have analyzed a dataset of tweets to discern public opinion with high precision. The CNN demonstrated remarkable effectiveness, achieving an overall accuracy of ${9 7 \%}$ with precision, recall, and F1-scores exceeding 0.96 for both positive and negative sentiments. These results underline the potential of CNNs in extracting meaningful insights from social media data, which can be pivotal for shaping marketing strategies and understanding consumer behavior towards new technologies like the Metaverse. The findings suggest that leveraging such deep learning models could significantly enhance the accuracy and depth of sentiment analysis in digital communication landscapes.

articleTitle: Human Interface Design in Mobile Apps: Managing Information for Effective Evacuation Strategies
abstract: Mobile applications have become essential tools for information dissemination and task execution, particularly during emergencies like evacuations. The design of these applications, guided by Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) and User-Centered Design (UCD) principles, can greatly enhance user safety and performance in such critical scenarios. This paper investigates the application of HCI and UCD methodologies in developing a mobile app specifically for emergency evacuations. We propose various interface strategies, such as dynamic maps with real-time updates versus static maps with pre-determined routes, to assess their effectiveness in aiding user decision-making during evacuations. Additionally, we emphasize iterative prototyping, usability testing, and real-time feedback to refine the application and improve the user experience and evacuation strategy. Furthermore, we address the challenges of deploying these systems in diverse indoor environments, including infrastructure constraints, real-time data accuracy, and privacy concerns. Our research provides valuable insights into creating intuitive, accessible, and effective evacuation apps, with the ultimate goal of improving evacuation strategies and ensuring user safety during emergencies.

articleTitle: Effects of virtual reality blue-green spaces on human mental health: A systematic review
abstract: Despite the rapid urbanization and societal advancements, many urban residents confront stress and high pressure in their daily lives, giving rise to pressing public health concerns. Recent studies emphasize the positive effects of exposure to blue-green spaces. Further research is needed to determine if blue-green spaces in virtual reality (VR) technology also positively impacts human psychological well-being. This review conducts the comparative analysis of VR versus real-world environments, highlighting the merits of leveraging virtual blue-green spaces to investigate mental health outcomes. The results show that virtual blue-green spaces have a positive impact on mental health in general. For the heightened mental stress and recurrent public health threats, VR technology emerges as a promising tool for mental health enhancement. Notably, highly immersive VR technology amplifies the effects on mental health. Therefore, exploring the influence of virtual blue-green spaces on mental health holds substantial practical value, offering invaluable insights and guidance for future studies and implications.

articleTitle: Integrating Digital Twin Instance into Blockchain-Based Access Control governed by Smart Contracts
abstract: Digital twin instances are gaining popularity due to their ability to provide a novel way to operate, design, and maintain physical assets. These virtual replicas offer real-time insights into their real-world counterparts’ performance, condition, and potential issues. Organizations can optimize processes, predict failures, and make informed decisions by analyzing data from sensors, simulations, and historical records, ultimately saving costs, reducing downtime, and enhancing overall efficiency. However, the data streams, models, and connected physical assets of a digital twin instance are of considerable value to the owners of the digital twin and, thus, need to be protected from potential abuse and attacks. This paper focuses on the need for access control when deploying digital twin instances. We present and evaluate a solution integrating digital twin instances into a smart-contract-governed blockchain solution.

articleTitle: Experiments on Compression and Restoration of Point Clouds Using Voxels
abstract: In Japan, point clouds of vast areas of land measured by instruments such as MMS and airborne LP are being stored. Because of the huge amount of data, these point clouds are managed in index maps based on the national large-scale maps. With this method of managing point clouds, data management becomes more complicated as the number of divided point clouds increases as the measurement area expands. In recent years, measurement technology has been developed and high-density point clouds have been acquired. Therefore, even a divided point cloud consists of large-sized data, which often imposes filtering loads when using it in difference analysis and other applications. The ability to compress a point cloud in text format and restore it to a point cloud with a spatial resolution appropriate for the application contributes to efficient point cloud management. The objective of this study was to propose a compression and restoration method for point clouds according to the application. The proposed method compresses the point cloud by recording the presence or absence of points in voxels defined with five spatial resolutions ranging from a maximum of 1.00 m to a minimum of 0.0625 m. As a result of the verification, the data volume of the compressed point cloud was less than one-sixth of the original point cloud. Furthermore, in the difference analysis use case, point clouds restored from the compressed point cloud at 1.00 m and 0.0625 m spatial resolution were used to identify the location of the deformation and to quantitatively calculate the difference. This indicates that the proposed method can recover point clouds with a spatial resolution suitable for the application, and that the method is useful.

articleTitle: AI in Sustainability:Assessing its Functions and Environmental Impact
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has fundamentally transformed various industries, including healthcare, transportation, agriculture, energy, and media. However, while AI’s impact is widely recognized, its sustainability remains a critical concern due to significant computational and environmental costs, as well as ethical issues such as biased systems and misinformation. This paper explores the dual dimensions of AI’s impact on sustainability: its potential to promote sustainability across sectors and the sustainability of AI systems themselves. Using a comprehensive review of existing literature, we address both the benefits and challenges associated with AI in achieving sustainable goals and the need for a more integrated approach to understanding its environmental, social, and economic impacts. Our analysis of the “AI Global Index” dataset, which evaluates AI capabilities across 62 countries, highlights key trends and disparities in AI development. The findings underscore the need for a holistic approach to AI sustainability that encompasses its full range of effects and interactions with various dimensions of sustainability.

articleTitle: Application and development of OPM-MEG technology
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of science and technology, Magnetoencephalography (Meg) has been widely used in neuroscience and clinical medicine because of its high spatial and temporal resolution. As an important branch of MEG technology, the MEG system based on Optically Pumped Magnetometers (OPMs) is emerging with its unique advantages. However, the high cost, large SQUID and stringent requirements for environmental conditions limit the use of SQUID in clinical applications. By contrast, Optically Pumped Magnetometer (OPM) Meg is becoming a hot research and potential clinical tool in MEG field because of its portability, wearability and high sensitivity. This paper reviews the recent progress of OPM-MEG technology, including its research and application in signal processing, multi-source detection, bad channel recognition, coregistration, pattern recognition and clinical application.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Stackelberg Game for Energy Trading in Power Grid Metaverses
abstract: Metaverses are a virtual space that has revolutionized many fields, such as healthcare and education. By integrating metaverses with power grids, power grid metaverses are regarded as a digital representation of the power grid infrastructure, giving rise to some potential applications, such as visualization and monitoring of energy trading. Energy balancing is essential to ensure that the supply of electricity matches the demand. Power grid metaverses can be used to identify potential imbalances between supply and demand and execute energy trading in real time, ensuring the proper functioning of smart grids. However, without reliable incentives, energy trading may not be conducted effectively. Considering the energy trading between EVCOs (EVCOs) and EMs (EMs), we propose a Stackelberg game model where the EM acts as the leader, setting the electric energy price, while EVCOs follow. We utilize a soft actor-critic algorithm to identify the Stackelberg equilibrium, addressing non-stationary challenges through the design of a partially observable policy, definition of the action space, and formulation of the reward function. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm effectively achieves the Stackelberg equilibrium, indicating the robustness of our approach.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Deep Learning Model for Efficient and Accurate Anti-Cancer Peptide Identification Surpassing Traditional Machine Learning Methods
abstract: Anti-cancer peptide (ACP) classification is crucial for developing new cancer therapies. However, traditional machine learning methods often struggle with both accuracy and efficiency in the task of ACP classification. To address these challenges, we utilized DistilBERT, which is a variant of BERT designed to reduce size and computational requirements while maintaining performance, to capture complex relationships and patterns in ACP sequences, by leveraging its ability to learn deep language features from large amounts of unlabeled data. DistilBERT’s knowledge distillation approach compresses the large BERT model into a smaller one, thereby reducing storage needs and accelerating inference speed. Our results demonstrate that DistilBERT significantly outperforms traditional machine learning models in ACP classification tasks, achieving an accuracy of 0.8957, precision of 0.9068, recall of 0.9012, and $F 1$-scores of 0.9045. This improved performance, combined with DistilBERT’s efficiency, makes it a promising tool for ACP classification, potentially accelerating the discovery and development of new cancer treatments, even in environments with limited computational resources.

articleTitle: FMCW Radar-based Sleep Posture Recognition with Transfer Learning and Range-Aware Dataset
abstract: Sleep posture recognition is crucial for understanding sleep quality and diagnosing sleep-related disorders. In this paper, we propose a fine-tuned VGG16 model for classifying four fundamental sleep postures—Supine, Prone, Right side, and Left side—using data collected from Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar. Radar signals are processed into range-time images and fed into the deep-learning model for training and classification. We evaluate the impact of varying window sizes, radar distances (1.5, 1.7, and 1.9 meters), and subject independence on the model’s performance. Our fine-tuned VGG16 model achieves an average accuracy of over 96% across different distances and demonstrates superior performance compared to a basic CNN. However, the model struggles to generalize to unseen subjects, indicating the need for further research to address subject-dependent challenges. This study highlights the potential of radar-based systems for contactless sleep monitoring and suggests future improvements to enhance model generalization.

articleTitle: Dive into the Long-Term Effects Autonomous Vehicles Have on Transportation
abstract: Self-driving cars have garnered significant attention and debate in recent years, with many viewing their widespread adoption as inevitable, despite several unresolved technological and legal challenges. However, the long-term impacts of this technology are rarely explored in the literature. The effects—both direct and indirect, positive and negative—are diverse, and predicting the overall societal impact is challenging. This study aims to identify and analyze some of these potential outcomes, exploring the conditions under which autonomous vehicles could benefit or harm the broader transportation system. Specifically, it examines how self-driving technology might influence the attractiveness of car travel, how that might affect mode choices, and how changes in these choices could reshape the transportation network. The study outlines two theoretical scenarios based on different behavioral responses to the introduction of autonomous vehicles, using a well-established system dynamics model to illustrate the key factors. Various policy interventions are explored, and a wide range of potential consequences are considered.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering Optimization for Massive Data
abstract: Hierarchical agglomerative clustering is one of the iconic data processing methods. It runs slow, let alone massive datasets, compared to other clustering methods, due to its fundamental algorithm. However, it has unreplaceable value in a few fields, such as statistics, biology, and image processing. The MapReduce framework seems to be the way out with its parallel computing and low hardware cost. Unfortunately, the performance might be worse using MapReduce since there might be too much data transferring back and forth without a proper design. Considering that the most time-consuming step is to find the required one distance from all pairs of observations between two clusters, we first design an optimization method to filter the observations based on their distances with the centroids. We only keep the relative marginal observations which are with way higher probability to be selected than relative central ones. Then we design and implement the corresponding MapReduce functions and test it using two datasets. In the experiments, our method can reduce the amount of calculations greatly and also can decrease the volume of shuffle data in MapReduce. It can achieve 9% to 82.3% running time reduction for different volumes of datasets while maintaining the accuracy more than 90%.

articleTitle: Neuro-Humanoid-Twin: Empowering Neurodiversity in Teams and at the Workplace Through Digital Twins and Digital Human Models
abstract: This vision paper explores the potential of digital twins (DTs) and digital human models (DHMs) for designing inclusive workplaces. To address the growing trend of companies hiring neurodivergents to tackle the skills shortage, the concept of the neuro-humanoid-twin is introduced. Workshops and surveys were conducted with neurodivergents to identify their specific needs and create a comprehensive database for the DT. The neuro-humanoid-twin is designed to support managers by providing valuable insights into the neurodivergent perspective, ultimately enhancing social interaction and empowering inclusivity in the workplace.

articleTitle: An optimization method for accelerating TCP convergence in metaverse scenarios
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of virtual reality (VR) technology has brought the concept of the metaverse from science fiction to reality. VR devices have made significant progress in the consumer market, with new hardware and technologies constantly emerging. However, the initialization time for VR application software is quite long, severely impacting user experience. We closely examined the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) connection behavior during software startup and found that current congestion control algorithms take a long time to converge to the maximum available bandwidth in highbandwidth networks after the slow start phase. This is because the internal parameters of widely used congestion control algorithms, including CUBIC, are fixed within the kernel, leading to prolonged convergence times in high-bandwidth environments. In this paper, we propose FWMB, a dynamic parameter adjustment method based on CUBIC that optimizes parameter settings using the current network’s maximum available bandwidth. We implemented this algorithm in a Linux environment, and comprehensive experiments show that compared to the default CUBIC algorithm, FWMB reduces the convergence time to maximum bandwidth by $11.2 \%$ to $19.7 \%$.

articleTitle: MPSI: A Cross-layer Multi-path QUIC Approach for Mobile Video Streaming Services
abstract: The deployment of multipath transmission protocols has brought opportunities for the development of data-intensive network applications such as mobile ultra-high-definition video and provides solutions for maximizing the utilization of diverse and long-coexisting network resources like Wi-Fi, 4G, etc., under 5G scenarios, as well as for achieving network load balancing. However, most research on multipath scheduling mainly focuses on improving the performance of wired networks, and the importance of Multipath QUIC (MPQUIC) path-scheduling strategies for wireless transmission has not been given sufficient attention. This paper proposes MPSI; by combining mechanisms such as Signal Interference Noise Ratio (SINR), Round-Trip Time (RTT), and weighted freshness, it not only significantly optimizes the transmission efficiency and stability of web video streams under wireless networks but also ensures fair resource allocation among substreams during multipath transmission. It provides an effective solution to the challenges of multipath wireless transmission in weak network environments. Experimental results indicate that compared to traditional multipath scheduling algorithms, MPSI demonstrates significant improvements in throughput and robustness.

articleTitle: The right to explanation in the European AI Act
abstract: The European AI Act is the first extensive legal regulation of AI systems and is therefore of great importance for developers and users of AI systems. From the perspective of Explainable AI, the right to explanation according to Article (Art.) 86 AI Act is of particular interest. This article provides a brief overview of the AI Act and analyses the subject and content of the right to explanation.

articleTitle: Real-time Respiratory Apnea Detection Using mmWave Radar
abstract: Sleep Apnea Syndrome (SAS) is a sleep disorder characterized by repeated pauses in breathing during sleep, leading to potential health problems such as high blood pressure and heart disease due to oxygen deprivation. While home-based SAS tests like simplified polysomnography (PSG) exist, they require the attachment of equipment, prompting a demand for a more simple, non-contact method of apnea detection for SAS. This research is focused on real-time apnea detection using a radar with frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW). To evaluate the apnea detection results, Spirometer as a reference device that measures air volume in respiration is adopted and its data are used for precise apnea detection. The second derivative is applied for both Spirometer-based and radar-based apnea detection. Three methods have been proposed for apnea detection, one is based on peaks found the second derivative, another is based on states of the Hidden Markov Model (HMM), and the last one is based on judgements on if the normalized absolute radar phase values exceed a threshold or not. All the three proposed methods exhibit relatively high accuracy in detecting apnea events and parameters as compared with the ground truth obtained from the reference device.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Intelligent Accelerator Experiment Platform for Ship Information Infrastructure
abstract: This paper combined the requirement easily use demand of ship information infrastructure in the scenarios of heterogeneous artificial intelligent (AI) accelerators in the ship user system, and established a benchmark for heterogeneous intelligent accelerator for ship information infrastructure. In order to achieve the benchmark test of multiple AI accelerators in parallel area in ship information infrastructure and improve the convenience and intuitiveness of heterogeneous task management, an experiment platform for heterogeneous AI accelerators based on container technology was designed in this paper. This experiment platform implemented resource management, dataset management, model management, synchronization testing, models evaluation, and operation of multiple servers in the cluster, through which the ship users could view heterogeneous resource status and task execution progress at one glance.

articleTitle: Addressing Non-IID Data in Federated Learning with Dual Attention Mechanism for Edge Computing Applications
abstract: In edge intelligence scenarios, Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a preeminent method for ensuring privacy preservation and fostering collaboration among end devices. This is primarily due to its ability to train a global model in an edge computing environment without compromising the data privacy of end devices. However, challenges arise in the form of non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) issues, such as heterogeneous graph data distributions, stemming from heterogeneity in end device data. These issues notably impede the convergence speed of the federated model and escalate communication costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce a novel edge computing based FL framework with a Dual Attention mechanism, termed FedDAD. Specifically, FedDAD integrates a Graph Attention Network (GAT) within the local model training process, which is designed to capture the variety of relationships across diverse client data distributions. Concurrently, FedDAD employs an attention mechanism across different client models to fuse key features from various client models into the global model. The efficacy of FedDAD is evaluated through extensive experiments on three heterogeneous graph datasets, demonstrating its superior performance over representative FL baselines.

articleTitle: WhoAmIOn: A Technique To Determine Whether All Devices Are Being Used By The Same Person
abstract: Wearable devices, with a plethora of sensors, can measure physical and physiological signals from various on-body locations, and log the information against a device owner’s profile. However, when another person uses the same wearable device, the other person’s activities and health-related information are also logged into the owner’s profile, causing mis-logging.
