One approach to prevent mis-logging is by enabling the owner’s wearable devices to communicate amongst themselves to determine if the same person is using them. In this work, we also explore the possibility of using heart rate and inertial sensor data from multiple devices to determine their co-existence with the same user. We developed the WhoAmIOn system that uses machine learning techniques (as compared to correlation approaches that are currently used) to determine whether the same person is using the devices. Overall, we observed that with the inertial sensor, we achieved an accuracy of 52%, while with a heart rate sensor the accuracy increases substantially to 85% in determining whether the same user is wearing or using the devices at the same time instant in a freeliving setting. This demonstrates that, it is indeed possible to use heart rate sensors to determine if devices are on the same body.

articleTitle: Joint Semantic and Spatial Feature Learning for Audio-Visual Speaker Tracking
abstract: Audio-visual speaker tracking, as a fundamental task in the field of multimodal perception, has broad application prospects in the domain of human-computer interaction. However, existing approaches primarily focus on spatial localization cues within audio-visual data, often utilizing only single-level features, which neglect the complementarity between semantic and spatial information. This creates challenges for current technologies in complex environments, such as occlusions, background interference, and environmental noise. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel Audio-Visual Tracker based on Semantic-Spatial feature fusion (AVSS-Tracker). First, a semantic feature encoding method based on an audio-visual keyword spotting network is designed, capable of extracting semantic information related to the target from audio-visual signals. Then, a two-stage semantic-spatial feature fusion mechanism is introduced, which leverages a cross-attention mechanism to explore the correlations and complementarities of features across different levels and modalities, significantly enhancing feature representation capabilities and tracking accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AVSS-Tracker performs exceptionally well in complex scenes and under interference conditions, with the fusion of semantic and spatial features notably improving the performance of audio-visual speaker tracking.

articleTitle: Camera-Based HRV Prediction for Remote Learning Environments
abstract: In recent years, the widespread use of online facial videos has brought increasing attention to remote photoplethys-mography (rPPG) in affective computing. Recovering blood volume pulse (BVP) signals from facial videos is a complex task, involving multiple stages of preprocessing, image analysis, and postprocessing to accurately reconstruct waveforms. Not only is the heart rate metric utilized for affective computing, but the heart rate variability (HRV) metric is even more significant. The challenge in obtaining HRV indices through rPPG lies in the necessity for algorithms to precisely predict the BVP peak positions. In this paper, we collected the Remote Learning Affect and Physiology (RLAP) dataset, which includes over 32 hours of highly synchronized video and labels from 58 subjects. This is a public dataset whose BVP labels have been meticulously designed to better suit the training of HRV models. Using the RLAP dataset, we trained a new model called Seq-rPPG, it is a model based on one-dimensional convolution, and experimental results reveal that this structure is more suitable for handling HRV tasks, which outperformed all other baselines in HRV performance and also demonstrated significant advantages in computational efficiency. The RLAP dataset is open source: https://github.com/KegangWangCCNU/RLAP-dataset

articleTitle: Urban Area Detection Based on Cross-Domain Lightweight Parallel Fusion Network for Orbita “Zhuhai-1” Hyperspectral Satellite
abstract: In order to ensure the stabilization issues of efficient deployment in orbit and cross-domain real-time detection. In this paper, a lightweight domain adaptation parallel fusion network (LAPNet) for urban detection of Orbita “Zhuhai-1” (OHS) remote sensing data has been proposed. Point convolution and dynamic convolution are employed to fully exploit spatial-spectral fusion features from local-global and pixel-semantic perspective. At the same time, cross-scene domain alignment from the public dataset to the target dataset is achieved by the adversarial domain adaptation strategy. Based on the hyperspectral remote sensing data from the “Zhuhai-1” satellite, we created three urban detection datasets for the experiment, where the public dataset and the dataset generated by hyperspectral reconstruction algorithm as the pre-training datasets for urban area detection. To verify the effectiveness of LAPNet for domain adaptation, we evaluate the LAPNet for the urban area detection task on the target domain “Zhuhai- 1 “ hyperspectral dataset. Compared to related comparative algorithms, the LAPNet improves the urban detection performance and efficiency for hyperspectral remote sensing satellite on each dataset with effectively reducing the number of model parameters.

articleTitle: Modeling Larval Tumbling Locomotion Based on Differentiable Material Point Method
abstract: Tumbling locomotion enables Drosophila larvae to rapidly reposition themselves to evade predators. Owing to the complex spatial postural changes involved, studies on this phenomenon are relatively scarce. Neuromechanical models can simulate sequences of biological locomotion postures and synthesize long-term multimodal movement behaviors, facilitating the analysis of the mechanisms linking the nervous system and locomotion. However, constructing neuromechanical models of larval tumbling presents significant challenges due to the extensive deformations resulting from tumbling. Here, we developed a model based on the material point method (MPM) that reflects the biological structure of Drosophila larvae, controlling muscle contractions in response to received signals. By integrating deep learning, we created an artificial neural network-based controller to generate these signals. We built this framework using differentiable physics and leveraged efficient gradient calculations for gradient-based optimization of the neural network controller. Our framework supports both straight and offset tumbling and achieves closed-loop control of a complex 3D soft-bodied neuromechanical model. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized neural network controller enables the larval model to perform tumbling actions effectively, providing new insights into understanding and simulating larval locomotion behavior.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Networks with Fine-Tuned Word Representations for Visual Question Answering
abstract: Recent advances in graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have demonstrated their effectiveness in vision-language tasks such as visual question answering (VQA), primarily due to their ability to capture both spatial and semantic relationships. However, through a series of experiments applying GCNs to VQA tasks, we observe that the performance of GCNs is highly sensitive to various subtasks, often resulting in unstable outputs. This variability can be attributed to factors such as the size of the training and testing datasets, evaluation metrics, and the selection of hyperparameters. To ensure fair evaluations of GCN-based VQA models, it is essential to implement consistent evaluation schemes across these factors. In this study, we propose a GCN framework for VQA that leverages fine-tuned word representations from the GloVe model, specifically tailored to address reasoning-based questions. We comprehensively assess the performance of our framework using multiple evaluation metrics on both the GQA and VQA 2.0 datasets. Our experimental results demonstrate significant improvements over existing methods, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed approach in evaluation setting.

articleTitle: Sound of Reason: Using AI to build a Digital Twin after the Kanon of Pythagoras in school settings
abstract: This paper presents ongoing work on kanON, an AI-driven EdTech tool designed to foster interactive learning and support Digital Cultural Heritage (DCH) preservation. kanON facilitates the digital reconstruction of the infamous Pythagorean monochord, by allowing users to seamlessly manipulate parameters such as origin (location and epoch), materials, and shape/dimensions. Through the integration of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, the tool predicts missing archaeological data and generates real-time 3D renderings based on user input, accompanied by corresponding confidence metrics. A mixed-methods (pilot) study was conducted in classroom environments to evaluate its educational impact via quantitative Likert scale assessments and qualitative content analysis of educator feedback. Preliminary results demonstrate high levels of student engagement and reflect positive educator responses, highlighting its potential to enhance the in-class accessibility and understanding of complex historical concepts, as well as to enable the preservation and exploration of cultural artifacts through digital means. Future work will focus on refining kanON and expanding its applicability within both educational and DCH contexts, by introducing the capability of outputting a fully operational digital twin, that integrates mixed reality functionalities. The idea is to enable users to later engage with their (personalized) model dynamically (e.g., readjusting string length and tension), thus allowing them to produce different soundscapes in real-time. This advancement aims to deepen the pedagogical impact by merging tactile interaction with visual and auditory feedback, further enhancing the educational experience via immersive, experiential learning.

articleTitle: Driving Toward Safety: A Personalized Approach to Traffic Risk Assessment Leveraging Driver Behaviour Data
abstract: In this paper, we propose a three-phase framework for personalized traffic risk assessment leveraging driver behavior data. Firstly, we extract temporal features and create spatial cluster zones using a clustering algorithm. Subsequently, we extracted drivers’ driving behavior such as speed differences, acceleration, jerk, aggressive braking, and turning rate, and then analyzed drivers’ behavior statistically, computing trip means and standard deviations. We also cluster trajectories using the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). For risk classification, we employ a Self-Organizing Map (SOM) and compute risk scores using an autoencoder-based RNN to address the challenge of insufficient labeled data. We validate our model using the real-world CityTrek-14K dataset from the US, achieving low MSE and MAE values of 1.3 and 0.8, respectively, demonstrating the model’s effectiveness in predicting personalized traffic risk.

articleTitle: VIDF-SR: A Multispectral Super-resolution Method Based on Visible-infrared Difference Feature Maps
abstract: Multispectral super-resolution aims to recover a high-resolution image from low-resolution images of two modalities. The primary challenges are the poor quality of visible light images under low-light conditions and the inherently low resolution and insufficient structural information in infrared images. There are relatively few approaches dedicated to multispectral super-resolution so far as most methods focus on single-image super-resolution. The existing methods on multispectral super-resolution typically rely on simple convolution and upsampling techniques, resulting in suboptimal performance. To address these issues, we propose a multispectral super-resolution method based on visible-infrared difference feature maps (VIDF-SR) in this study. Specifically, to effectively utilize the superior structural information from the visible light modality and the clearer texture and edge information from the infrared modality during the reconstruction process, we introduce the Modal Information Complementary Module (MICM), which generates fused features based on the difference feature maps between the two modalities, retaining key information from both. Furthermore, to produce clearer multispectral super-resolution images, we design the Feature Map Super-Resolution Module (FMSR), incorporating a diffusion model into our framework to achieve superior performance. Experiments on the M3FD dataset show that our method surpasses current approaches, with ablation studies providing additional confirmation of the effectiveness of each component.

articleTitle: Droflysim: A Collective Behavior Analysis and Evaluation Tool
abstract: The collective behaviors of various organisms exhibit complex patterns and statistical characteristics, especially evident within large populations. The complexity of these behaviors necessitates in-depth analysis of extensive trajectory data to reveal underlying dynamics and patterns. Current methods fall short in quantitative analysis and multi-angle assessment of collective behaviors, particularly in terms of the limitations of macroscopic indicators and the singularity of evaluation methods. This study introduces Droflysim, an efficient computational platform for analyzing and assessing large-scale trajectory data of collective behavior. Droflysim enhances data processing speed through parallel processing technology and integrates a variety of simulation models and multi-angle evaluation methods, overcoming the limitations of traditional tools. Notably, Droflysim emphasizes the statistical analysis of trajectories under environmental disturbances, providing a new perspective and deeper understanding of the complexity of collective behavior by establishing a trajectory fitting model. The design of Droflysim includes an intuitive interactive interface, modular architecture, and parallel processing capabilities, enhancing the efficiency and scalability of data analysis. By quantitatively analyzing trajectories, Droflysim lays the foundation for precise model calibration and authentic reproduction of behavior, offering a powerful tool for the study of collective behavior.

articleTitle: Multi-Concept Interactive Representation Learning for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge Representation Learning (KRL) enhances the completeness and utility of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) by embedding entities and relations into low-dimensional vector spaces for link prediction and completion. However, existing KRL methods often fail to address the complex multi-concept issues hidden in triplets. This paper proposes a Multi-Concept Interactive Representation Learning method (MCIRL) that captures the complex conceptual variations in entities and relations from two different informational perspectives: interactive steady-state information and shared semantic information. Specifically, interactive steady-state information focuses on the unique interaction patterns between entities and relations in their current combinations, while shared semantic information focuses on the common features of entities and relations across different interaction contexts. We designed three modules to perform different tasks: (a) GAERT module (Gated Attention Entity-Relation Transformer) to extract interactive steady-state information; (b) SWVD module (Semantic Weave Variational Decoder) to extract shared semantic information; (c) MsAPFE module (Multi-Scale Attention Pyramid Feature Extraction) to combine these two types of information and generate specific contextual information. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that MCIRL significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art KRL methods across various evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Trans-EffNet: A Hybrid Model for Brain Tumor Detection Using EfficientNet and Transformer Encoder
abstract: Accurate classification of brain tumors from MRI is critical for effective diagnosis and treatment. In this study, we introduce Trans-EffNet, a hybrid model combining pre-trained EfficientNet architectures with a transformer encoder to enhance brain tumor classification accuracy. By leveraging EfficientNet’s deep CNN capabilities for localized feature extraction and the transformer encoder for capturing global contextual relationships, our model improves the identification of intricate tumor characteristics. Fine-tuned with ImageNet-derived weights and utilizing extensive data augmentation, Trans-EffNet was validated on both multi-class and binary datasets. Trans-EffNetB1 achieved $99.49 \%$ accuracy on the multi-class dataset, while Trans-EffNetB2 recorded $99.83 \%$ accuracy on the binary dataset, with perfect precision, recall, and F1-Score. These results underscore Trans-EffNet’s robustness and potential as a significant advancement in brain tumor detection and classification.

articleTitle: A Self-attention Spiking Neural Network for Human-to-Human Interaction Recognition Based on Wi-Fi Signals
abstract: Leveraging Wi-Fi signals for human activity recognition (HAR) enables efficient deployment, cost savings, and enhanced privacy protection. Channel State Information (CSI) has become central in recognizing human-to-human interactions (HHIs) within HAR research. Traditional Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models, although widely used for HHIs recognition, suffer from high system overhead and suboptimal recognition accuracy. To address these limitations, we introduce an innovative Self-Attention Spiking Neural Network (SASNN) model, named HHIs-SASNN, specifically designed for recognizing HHIs. This model leverages the robust spatio-temporal processing capabilities of Spiking Neural Networks (SNN), augmented with a self-attention mechanism, to effectively extract and process spatio-temporal information from Wi-Fi signals. Our model exhibits superior performance in both accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional ANN-based methods. Our experimental results show that the proposed approach achieves an average accuracy of over 96% in recognizing 13 distinct types of human-to-human interaction behaviors, including steady-state activities, nearly a 1% improvement over conventional ANN methods. Additionally, the experiments indicate that our model achieves lower system overhead.

articleTitle: A Federated Class Incremental Learning Framework for Edge Intelligence
abstract: With the advancement of deep learning, artificial intelligence has garnered significant attention in the field of edge computing. However, the characteristics of edge devices present two major challenges for the application of deep neural networks: the conflict between high accuracy and strong data privacy requirements, and the conflict between the high consumption of computing resources and the low performance of edge devices. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a federated class-incremental learning framework for edge intelligence. Based on the varying consumption of computing and storage resources, the scheme divides the training process of the complete federated class-incremental model into three stages, which are executed at different locations. The pre-training of the basic model and the aggregation of global parameters are carried out on the central cloud server with strong computing power, while analytic incremental learning is introduced on the edge server to reduce the computation and storage load during model updates. This scheme offers three advantages: continuous updating capabilities of the model, low resource consumption on edge devices, and a robust data privacy protection mechanism for edge devices. Performance analysis results from experiments demonstrate the reliability of this method.

articleTitle: EPIC: Ensembled Poisoning Identification and Classification for LLM Backdoor Defense
abstract: In the realm of artificial intelligence, Large Language Models (LLMs) stand as titans of natural language understanding and generation, driving innovations across diverse applications. However, their ascendancy brings forth challenges, notably vulnerability to data poisoning attacks; malicious alterations designed to compromise model integrity. This work introduces a novel approach to safeguard LLMs against these malicious threats. This paper delineates a two-pronged methodology: initially deploying an ensemble of traditional machine learning models to detect discrepancies in predictions between clean and poisoned models, followed by an enhanced technique that trains models to discern the “poison status” directly from data inputs. Through meticulous experimentation, this work not only unveils the susceptibility of LLMs to poisoning but also demonstrates the efficacy of ensemble methods and poison detection in fortifying model defenses. Our research aims to improve security and robustness of AI systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing Collaborative Filtering via Structural Denoised and Scalable Graph
abstract: Collaborative filtering (CF) based on graph neural networks (GNN) has demonstrated excellent performance in recommender systems and has been widely adopted. However, real-world interaction graphs often contain noise, which significantly affects the effectiveness and robustness of GNN models. While existing studies have addressed data denoising, they either employ complex strategies or only focus on denoising semantic neighbors, failing to directly address the noise issue. To address this problem, this paper proposes SDGCF, a novel robustness-enhanced structural denoised CF model. SDGCF consists of two key modules: a graph denoising module and an enhanced graph fusion module. The graph denoising module removes noisy interactions by assessing structural similarity between users and items, creating two denoised enhanced graphs. These graphs, retaining high structural similarity interactions, improve message passing and model robustness. The enhanced graph fusion module facilitates information sharing during message passing, leveraging graph diversity for better generalization. By utilizing mutual information maximization (MIM) and the InfoNCE loss function, SDGCF ensures consistency across the denoised graphs, further reducing noise impact. Our extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that SDGCF consistently outperforms existing baseline methods, confirming its superior performance in handling noisy interactions and providing accurate recommendations.

articleTitle: Road Damage Detection Across Borders: Federated Learning Insights from Japan, China, Norway and the USA
abstract: This study explores the application of federated learning (FL) techniques to road damage detection across diverse geographical contexts, including Japan, Norway, China, and the USA. Federated learning, a decentralized machine learning approach, facilitates collaborative model training without sharing raw data, sharing only model parameters, thereby preserving privacy and enabling data synergy. While previous studies have been conducted on a smaller scale, using nearly similar datasets with consistent image capture methods, resolutions, and road views, our proposed work presents an extensive study of 4 countries (Japan, China, Norway, and the USA) demonstrating FL’s effectiveness on a broader scale with diverse and heterogenous data addressing variations in road conditions, infrastructure, inspection methods, and environmental factors. The insights from the study reveal that the collaboratively trained model using FL outperforms the individual country’s centralized models by a large margin. Leveraging YOLOv81 and the Flower framework with FedAvg strategy, our federated model garnered an mAP50 of 0.49 on a multi-country test dataset curated from these four participating countries, surpassing Japan’s centralized model by 2.4% and outperforming models from Norway, China, and the USA approximately by about 20% and more.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin Framework for Robot Grasp and Motion Generation
abstract: Digital twin technology has demonstrated significant potential across various domains. In the field of robotics, manipulation, particularly robotic grasping, is fundamental to many applications. While artificial intelligence and deep learning methods have been employed to enhance grasp detection through visual perception, challenges such as data collection, the simulation-toreality (sim2real) gap, and motion planning safety still persist. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a comprehensive framework for digital twin-based robotic grasping and motion generation. Firstly, a digital twin synthetic data generation and domain randomization framework for robot manipulation is proposed to generate large-scale data to support deep learning training. Then, a hybrid training strategy combining synthetic and real data is proposed to reduce sim2real gap and enhance model performance in real-world perception. Finally, a dynamic digital twin working environment construction framework is proposed for motion generation and collision avoidance in changing environments. The proposed framework is widely applicable to various robotic tasks, offering a robust solution to the challenges faced in robotic manipulation. By leveraging digital twins, the efficiency, safety, and reliability of robotic operations will be enhanced across multiple robotic applications.

articleTitle: Adversarial Attacks on Influence Maximization in Homogeneous Hypergraphs
abstract: Adversarial strategies targeting influence maximization within homogeneous hypergraphs is an essential area with applications in viral marketing, rumor control, and epidemic prevention. We define the Adversarial Influence Maximization Problem (AdvIMH) and propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning-based algorithm ADV-DRL for selecting attack nodes. Additionally, we introduce a hypergraph embedding algorithm HyperVec to obtain vector representations of hypergraphs. By modeling real-world high-order relationships in datasets such as Music and Restaurant hypergraphs, we demonstrate the effectiveness of ADV-DRL through extensive experiments. Results show that ADV-DRL significantly outperforms baseline algorithms in reducing influence spread, highlighting its potential to identify vulnerable nodes and strategically diminish information propagation in hypergraphs. This work not only broadens the scope of influence maximization applications but also offers an innovative approach for tackling adversarial scenarios in networked systems.

articleTitle: Quantifying and Analyzing Speculative Execution Risks: A Quantitative Security Framework
abstract: The disclosure of Spectre and Meltdown vulnerabilities has significantly challenged processor security, exposing inherent flaws in microarchitectural design and revealing the limitations of existing countermeasures. Despite extensive mitigation efforts, completely preventing information leakage resulting from speculative execution continues to pose a significant challenge. A significant gap remains in the lack of a quantitative evaluation framework that rigorously assesses the effectiveness of these mitigation strategies. In this research, the SPECTECTOR analytical framework is utilized to introduce two novel quantitative metrics: Relative Leakage Entropy (RLE) and Normalized Conditional Entropy (NCE). These metrics are designed to evaluate the relative information leakage between speculative and non-speculative execution traces, providing distinct insights on leakage quantification. By utilizing these metrics to assess 15 example programs compiled with Intel ICC and CLANG compilers across different optimization levels and mitigation strategies, the analysis reveals that compiler optimization strategies markedly affect the magnitude of information leakage. The results indicate that, despite advanced mitigation techniques, substantial information leakage persists, highlighting the need for more effective security architectures in future processors and software systems.

articleTitle: Trans-Mamba: The Cross-network of Transformer and Mamba for Traffic Flow Prediction
abstract: Traffic flow prediction is a crucial aspect of intelligent transportation systems. It holds significant importance in optimizing traffic management and enhancing road safety. However, the task of traffic flow forecasting remains a significant challenge due to its inherent complexity, dynamic nature, and the presence of long-range dependencies. Existing graph neural network methods exhibit two primary limitations. Firstly, when static graphs are employed to capture spatial dependencies, they fail to account for the dynamics in these dependencies. Secondly, these methods struggle to effectively capture long-range spatial dependencies. Furthermore, attention-based methods, while potentially addressing some of these issues, require substantial computational and memory resources, leading to inefficiencies. We design a cross-network model that combines Transformer and Mamba architectures for traffic flow prediction, which efficiently captures dynamic long-range spatio-temporal dependencies. The model architecture is composed of three main components: a learnable spatio-temporal embedding layer that adaptively captures the unique features of different nodes and time; stacked spatio-temporal blocks, which include two temporal blocks and one spatial block arranged between them to effectively capture spatio-temporal dependencies; and a fully connected output layer that generates the final predictions. Experiments on three public real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of TransMamba. Specifically, the model improves the mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) by 2.59% and 4.14%, respectively, on the PeMS08 dataset. Additionally, ablation studies confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of each component of the model.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Causal Reasoning for Emotion Recognition in Conversations
abstract: Emotion recognition in conversation (ERC) has always been a research highlight in human-computer interaction (HCI). Existing models, including large-scale language models (LLMs), exhibit their advantages in capturing semantic correlations in utterance embeddings. However, they do not consider the causal relationship between utterances, which can be directly located to the cause and avoid unnecessary noise interference. Causal relationships are powerful in seizing the generation and evolution of emotions, and are also important for understanding the spread and changes of emotions in dialogue. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Multi-Level Causal Reasoning Model (MLCRM), which explores how to distinguish different causal relationships of a simulation embedding by independent conditioning. Specifically, we put forward a novel causal graph architecture to deal with unstructured conversation data, aiming to reveal causal links between sentences in a conversation. We not only focus on causal relations at the local level, but also on semantic embedding analysis at the global level. We commit to achieving comprehensive capture of causal relationships in conversation data by devising a coarse-grained semantic embedding module to assist the fine-grained causal inference. Furthermore, we raise a mix of experts module to enhance the exchange of information between the coarse-grained and fine-grained modules and to ensure the effective fusion of information for both. We conduct extensive experiments on four benchmarks, and the experimental results show that our model exhibits competitive results in the task of ERC.

articleTitle: deepV:PPO-driven Task Latency Minimization in Volunteer-supported Edge Computing
abstract: Although the emergence of edge computing has greatly enhanced the efficiency of data processing and reduced latency by bringing computation closer to the data source, one significant drawback of edge computing is the lack of processing capabilities of centralized cloud servers. With the rapid development of Internet of Things (IoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, the computational demand on edge servers is increasing exponentially. To address such shortage of resources at edge servers, this paper proposes deep V, a volunteer-supported edge computing framework. We also formulate a long-term multiobjective problem for joint optimization of resource allocation and volunteer employment. First, driven by deep reinforcement learning (DRL), a novel PPO-based algorithm is designed to configure the volunteer to IoT (V2I) device matching as well as uplink bandwidth allocation; Second, an efficient resource allocation and data partitioning algorithm is proposed utilizing the block coordinate decent (BCD) method. Through extensive simulations, we demonstrate the schedulability and scalability improvements of our work over other related algorithms.

articleTitle: TSCN-ELF: Feature Fusion of Two-Stream Convolutional Neural Networks for Action Recognition
abstract: Action recognition, which identifies the action performed by a person from a given video, is an important research topic in computer vision. Most existing action recognition methods rely on single-modal data, which suffers from problems such as limited feature representation and insufficient feature expression, affecting the action recognition performance. A novel framework called two-stream convolutional neural network for action recognition with early and late fusion (TSCN-ELF) is proposed to address this problem. This framework uses the lowcost separable hybrid 3D residual network (LCSH-3DResNet) to extract features from skeleton and RGB modalities, respectively. The skeleton feature extraction stream captures more spatiotemporal structural information, complemented by the RGB feature extraction stream, which captures more spatial appearance information. The features of the two streams are fused by early and late fusion methods to achieve efficient action recognition. Moreover, the dynamic similarity frame aggregation (DSFA) module is incorporated into the model to obtain better results. Our TSCN-ELF model efficiently learns spatiotemporal features that are more robust against pose estimation noise compared to single-stream networks, enhancing both action recognition accuracy and contributing to improved decision-making processes. The proposed method improves the performance compared to previous state-of-the-art methods on NTU RGB+D 60, NTU RGB+D 120, UCF101 and HMDB51 datasets.

articleTitle: Generate Unrestricted Adversarial Examples by Diffusion Model Based on Labels
abstract: The conventional method in adversarial examples research involves setting a fixed limit on the magnitude of perturbations, which fails to consider how humans perceive these perturbations in reality. Recent research has been directed towards creating natural unrestricted adversarial examples (UAEs) that surpass $L_{p}$ perturbation bounds while still preserving semantic plausibility. However, earlier attack methods often depend on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which lack theoretical provability and thus generate unrealistic examples, especially when applied to large-scale datasets like ImageNet. Lately, there has been a shift towards employing diffusion models for generating UAEs. Although diffusion models generate highquality adversarial examples, many of them still show notable deviations from the original samples. This paper presents a novel method called Conditional Sampling Optimization (CSO), which utilizes diffusion models to craft unrestricted adversarial examples targeted at specific class labels. In the process of generating UAEs, the class labels are iteratively used to adjust the prediction noise, guiding the UAEs towards misclassification by the target models. Extensive experiments conducted on ImageNet demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method in generating UAEs. Our approach delivers enhanced attack performance while preserving exceptional generation quality.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Approach: Boosting IoT Sensor Network Security with Visual Secret Sharing
abstract: This research paper is based on the issue of protecting the sensor networks in the era of IoT because the data is very sensitive and huge, and is collected in resource-constrained environments. We put forward a new approach to the enhancement of the security of IoT sensor networks by applying VSS on visual data. Our approach is based on the implementation of the VSS approach which implies that no single node will contain full information about the visual input which will be divided among the nodes. Furthermore, this approach also increases the security of the data, and at the same time is appropriate for the IoT environments since it does not require a large amount of computational power and network bandwidth. In addition, we explain how this method can be used, discuss its features, and based on the data from the experiments, prove the effectiveness of the suggested approach. The results of the research show that data security and the ability to counteract attacks can be resist if VSS is used in systems of IoT sensor networks.

articleTitle: A Method for Efficient Heterogeneous Parallel Compilation: A Cryptography Case Study
abstract: In the era of diminishing returns from Moore’s Law, heterogeneous computing systems have emerged as a vital approach to enhance computational efficiency. This paper introduces a novel MLIR-based dialect, named hyper, designed to optimize data management and parallel computation across diverse hardware architectures. The hyper dialect abstracts the complexities of heterogeneous computing by providing a unified compilation framework that efficiently schedules tasks and manages data communication. To demonstrate its capabilities, we present HETOCompiler, a cryptography-focused compiler prototype that implements multiple hash algorithms and enables their execution on heterogeneous systems. The proposed approach achieves performance improvements over existing programming models for heterogeneous computing (OpenCL), offering an average speedup of 1.93 x, 1.18 x, and 1.12 x for SHA-1, MD5, and SM3 algorithms, respectively. Our findings highlight the potential of the hyper dialect in harnessing the full computational power of heterogeneous devices, advancing the field of compiler design for heterogeneous systems.

articleTitle: Reasoning Semantic Augmentation for Long-Tailed Recognition
abstract: Long-tail recognition has garnered widespread attention due to the significant challenges posed by extremely imbalanced data. This imbalance causes models to heavily focus on learning head classes, neglecting tail classes and resulting in a decline in overall model performance. Recently, classifier retraining methods decoupling feature learning and classifier training have emerged. In the classifier retraining stage, using balanced sampling ensures an equal quantity of head and tail samples. However, it overlooks the gap in semantic richness between head and tail classes. In this paper, we conduct experiments to analyze classifier retraining methods, revealing that semantics scarcity is a crucial factor contributing to the underperformance of tail classes. To address this issue, we propose a novel semantics augmentation method based on two sampler branches named Reasoning Semantics Augmentation (RSA). Specifically, in the instance-wise branch, we use activation maps and gradients to distinguish important semantics and non-important semantics. Then, in the class-wise branch, we integrate non-important semantics from semantically rich classes into semantically scarce tail classes. This augmentation significantly enhances the richness of tail class semantics, improving the overall performance of the model. Additionally, our method can be seamlessly incorporated into other approaches as a semantic augmentation module. We validate the effectiveness of our method on three widely used datasets and achieve almost a 9.25% gain in CIFAR-10-LT (IF=200). At the same time, we conduct a large number of experiments to verify the adaptability and effectiveness of our method on different backbones and data augmentation.

articleTitle: Efficient Design of Prefix Adders Based on Relational Graph Convolutional Network
abstract: Due to the complex topological structure of prefix adders, a set of design solutions typically contains a large number of non-dominated solutions. Commonly, to identify the dominated solutions, the conventional design process involves performance evaluation of the design outcomes, a procedure that consumes a significant amount of time. To address this, this paper proposes a new prefix adder design process based on graph neural networks, aimed at increasing the proportion of dominated solutions in the design outcomes. By utilizing Relational Graph Convolutional Networks (RGCN) to train existing prefix trees and create predictive models, we modify the feature matrices of known prefix graphs to generate new prefix trees that potentially offer improved performance. Experimental results indicate that our method has increased the proportion of dominated solutions in the generated solutions to 0.7%, while reducing the number of evaluations for adder performance by 47.8%. This approach adheres to the rigorous standards expected of high-level research in the fields of neural networks and circuit design.

articleTitle: Enhanced Small Target Detection via Multi-Modal Fusion and Attention Mechanisms: A YOLOv5 Approach
abstract: With the rapid development of information technology, modern warfare increasingly relies on intelligence, making small target detection critical in military applications. The growing demand for efficient, real-time detection has created challenges in identifying small targets in complex environments due to interference. To address this, we propose a small target detection method based on multi-modal image fusion and attention mechanisms. This method leverages YOLOv5, integrating infrared and visible light data along with a convolutional attention module to enhance detection performance. The process begins with multi-modal dataset registration using feature point matching, ensuring accurate network training. By combining infrared and visible light features with attention mechanisms, the model improves detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results on anti-UAV and Visdrone datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of our approach, achieving superior detection results for small and dim targets.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Objective Optimization Approach for Low-Interference UAV Communication Based on Collaborative Beamforming
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in the field of wireless communications due to their inherent advantages such as easy deployment and low cost. Employing collaborative beamforming techniques to form a UAV-based virtual antenna array (UVAA) is a promising solution to achieve remote and low-cost communications. Owing to the nature of electromagnetic waves, UVAA may cause interference to unaffiliated users when deployed in densely populated areas. To address this issue, UAVs must identify the most suitable positions to achieve optimal beam patterns. However, considering their limited energy capacity and the increased power consumption associated with excessive flight, a multi-objective optimization analysis is necessary to balance these factors. Thus, we formulate a low-interference communication multi-objective problem (LIMOP), aiming to maximize transmission rate, minimize interference, and reduce energy consumption through the optimization of UAV positions, excitation currents, and the selection of target BS. Given the complexity of LIMOP, we introduce multiple improvement strategies to propose an improved swarm intelligence method. According to simulation results, the proposed IMOAHA is effective in addressing the formulated LIMOP and is superior to other algorithms.

articleTitle: A PUF-Based Mutual Authentication Protocol for Trustless Fog Computing Environments
abstract: Fog computing extends cloud capabilities to the edge of the network, addressing the latency and bandwidth issues inherent in the management of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Yet, this extension introduces new security challenges, particularly in the authentication of endpoints and fog nodes that are susceptible to physical attacks. Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) are pivotal for enabling lightweight, energy-efficient, and secure authentication of resource-constrained devices in traditional IoT networks. However, existing PUF-based authentication protocols, which rely on external trusted third parties or the storage of Challenge-Response Pairs (CRPs) within the verifier, are incompatible with the fog computing setting. To address this problem, this paper proposes a PUF-based authentication scheme that requires no storage of CRPs and is well-suited for trustless fog computing environments, achieving mutual authentication and key exchange between devices and fog nodes without the need for a trusted proxy server. The protocol incorporates a dynamic secret parameter update mechanism to ensure Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS), offering a more convenient and lightweight alternative compared to traditional solutions based on periodic re-registration or elliptic curve multiplication. We formally prove the security of the protocol using the Real-OrRandom (ROR) model and provide a comparative analysis of its performance, demonstrating its superiority in terms of security features, computational efficiency, and communication cost.

articleTitle: Summit Vitals: Multi-Camera and Multi-Signal Biosensing at High Altitudes
abstract: Video photoplethysmography (vPPG) is an emerging method for non-invasive and convenient measurement of physiological signals, utilizing two primary approaches: remote video PPG (rPPG) and contact video PPG (cPPG). Monitoring vitals in high-altitude environments, where heart rates tend to increase and blood oxygen levels often decrease, presents significant challenges. To address these issues, we introduce the SUMS dataset comprising 80 synchronized non-contact facial and contact finger videos from 10 subjects during exercise and oxygen recovery scenarios, capturing PPG, respiration rate (RR), and SpO2. This dataset is designed to validate video vitals estimation algorithms and compare facial rPPG with finger cPPG. Additionally, fusing videos from different positions (i.e., face and finger) reduces the mean absolute error (MAE) of SpO 2 predictions by $\mathbf{7. 6 \%}$ and $\mathbf{1 0. 6 \%}$ compared to only face and only finger, respectively. In cross-subject evaluation, we achieve an MAE of less than 0.5 BPM for HR estimation and $\mathbf{2. 5 \%}$ for SpO 2 estimation, demonstrating the precision of our multi-camera fusion techniques. Our findings suggest that simultaneous training on multiple indicators, such as PPG and blood oxygen, can reduce MAE in SpO 2 estimation by $\mathbf{1 7. 8 \%}$.

articleTitle: Visually Impaired Assistance with Large Models
abstract: Visually Impaired Assistance (VIA) is designed to facilitate the autonomous execution of daily activities for individuals with visual impairments through automated support. The progress in VIA technology is intrinsically linked to advancements in Computer Vision (CV) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) via Large Models (LMs). To investigate the possibility of current state-of-the-art (SOTA) LMs in VIA scenarios, we conduct a comprehensive study titled Visual Impaired Assistance with Large Models (VIALM). This study focuses on a task where a photo depicting the reality and linguistic question from a visually impaired user are provided to generate elaborate guidance aimed at assisting the user in fulfilling their request within that specific context. Our study, Visual Impaired Assistance with Large Models (VIALM), examines the application of SOTA LMs in VIA by providing an image and a textual request from a visually impaired user to generate detailed, context-specific guidance. Through benchmarking experiments and a review of recent LM advancements, our research indicates that while LMs have significant potential for enhancing VIA functionalities, they exhibit limitations such as insufficient environmental grounding (e.g., $\mathbf{2 5. 7 \%}$ failure rate in GPT-4) and inadequate detail in instructions (approximately $\mathbf{3 2. 1 \%}$ deficiency rate in GPT-4).

articleTitle: A Method for User Identification Across Multiple Transportation Systems Using Trajectories
abstract: This paper investigates a method for identifying users based on trajectories collected by different public transportation systems, where a user has different IDs in different systems. Identifying users is crucial for completing their trajectories and optimizing or recommending travel routes. The problem is similar to calculating the similarity between two trajectories from two data sources. Existing trajectory similarity methods based on trajectory point alignment or travel pattern similarity primarily focus on scenarios where trajectories are spatiotemporally synchronous. These methods are not applicable to here, as the trajectories collected by different public transport systems for same user are asynchronous. To address the issue, this paper proposes a user identification method (GLDT) for the scenario based on global semantic rationality and local contributions of co-occurrence points (e.g transfer point). Specifically, the method first filters out impossible pairs of trajectories by considering the uniqueness of a user in certain spatiotemporal contexts from a global perspective. Then it calculates the similarity of two trajectories by aggregating the novel defined local similarity of each co-occurrence point, which considers multi-view attributes of a co-occurrence point helpful to uniquely identify a user (e.g., individual and group visit frequency at a location, rationality of transfer routes, and so on). We validated our method using real-world data from Shenzhen, China, the results show that the matching accuracy improves by at least 10% compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: EmotionPass: Unobtrusive Emotion-based User Authentication on Glasses
abstract: Wearable devices are increasingly prevalent, necessitating reliable user authentication to mitigate privacy risks. Glasses, as a prominent category of wearable devices, have traditionally employed methods such as iris recognition, depth cameras, and electrooculography (EOG) for authentication purposes. However, these solutions are usually only applicable for bulky VR/XR goggles and are often impractical for emerging lightweight smart glasses due to the need for additional hardware modules. Thanks to their compact size, low cost, and privacy-preserving capabilities by capturing muscle movements, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) offer a promising alternative for user authentication. This study introduces EmotionPass, a novel system embedding IMU sensors in a pair of lightweight glasses for passive user authentication via facial expressions. Utilizing a Knowledge-Aware Network (KAN) and Supervised Contrastive Learning, our system extracts distinctive features from IMU signals. Experiments with 23 participants performing seven facial expressions demonstrated a high average accuracy of $99.22 \%$ and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 0.0154 in user attack scenarios. We compared various baseline algorithms and proved the reliability and stability of our algorithm. The system maintained $92.51 \%$ accuracy for unseen expressions, with long-term usability confirmed. EmotionPass thus offers a non-invasive, cost-effective, and efficient solution for continuous user authentication in wearable settings.

articleTitle: Influence Maximization on Dynamic Social Networks with Conjugate Learning Automata
abstract: The problem of identifying an optimal subset of nodes to serve as seeds for influence maximization in social networks has been a major focus of extensive research. Numerous approaches have been proposed to identify influential nodes in static networks. However, the application of these methods to dynamic networks, in which the network topology changes over time, presents significant challenges. The evolving nature of such networks complicates the direct application of static models, leading to a clear distinction between algorithms designed for static and dynamic influence maximization. In this paper, we demonstrate that conjugate learning automata, a specialized form of reinforcement learning, can be effectively applied for influence maximization in dynamic networks. The network dynamics are represented through fluctuations in the influence spread, which are incorporated into the learning process. Our approach efficiently models the impact of network evolution: as variations in the influence spread become more pronounced, the probability of needing to relearn the seed nodes from scratch increases. Experimental results from both synthetic and real-world networks validate the superior performance of our approach compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: A Privacy-Preserving Decentralized Federated Learning Framework Based on Differential Privacy
abstract: Federated learning allows machine learning models to be trained by local clients without sharing data directly, providing a degree of privacy protection. However, existing studies reveal that traditional federated learning is prone to issues like gradient leakage and model poisoning, which can compromise user privacy and negatively impact the performance of the global model. In this paper, we propose a Decentralized Differential Privacy Federated Learning (DDPFL) framework that strengthens privacy protection in federated learning by integrating decentralized design with differential privacy. First, we incorporate differential privacy noise through the Laplace mechanism, applying noise via a hierarchical processing scheme. Additionally, we control the noise addition by employing an adaptive gradient pruning strategy. Then, we develop a decentralized federated learning framework that employs a committee scoring mechanism. The core of this mechanism is a scoring system that determines which clients are eligible to contribute to the aggregation of the global model. Theoretical analysis confirms that the proposed DDPFL framework meets differential privacy requirements, with the level of privacy protection adjustable by selecting different $\epsilon$ values. Experimental results show that DDPFL exhibits strong resilience to model poisoning attacks, and that performance degradation can be managed effectively by selecting an appropriate privacy protection budget.

articleTitle: Verifiable and Byzantine-robust Private Information Retrieval over Distributed Database
abstract: Private Information Retrieval (PIR) protocols enable a user to retrieve a specific data item from a database while ensuring that no information about the requested item’s identity is revealed. To defend against Byzantine attacks in multi-server scenarios, we present a new Verifiable and Byzantine-robust Private Information Retrieval scheme (VBRPIR) on a database stored on n servers. Specifically, the database consists of m files of size l, which are encoded and stored, respectively, among n servers that may be colluding, Byzantine, and unresponsive. Differently from the erasure code-based scheme, we propose a new scheme based on a hash function and linear equations to verify answers and reconstruct the desired file from wrong answers, even in the extreme situation where all servers are Byzantine or unresponsive servers. Concretely, hash function is used to generate commitment of data stored on servers in offline stage, and the commitment is used to verify Byzantine server, based on the one-way property of hash function. Linear equations are also generated in the offline stage, used to reconstruct file when exists Byzantine or unresponsive server. The scheme achieves a download rate of $\frac{l}{2 n}$ for any number of files. We provide theoretical analysis and experimental results to illustrate the efficiency of our work. In the experimental setup of this paper, the time to retrieve a single file is within 1ms when there is at least one responsive and honest server. Even in the extreme case where all servers are Byzantine servers, the file can be retrieved within 2s.

articleTitle: Graph Contrastive Learning via Cluster-refined Negative Sampling for Semi-supervised Text Classification
abstract: Graph contrastive learning (GCL) has been widely applied to text classification tasks due to its ability to generate self-supervised signals from unlabeled data, thus facilitating model training. However, existing GCL-based text classification methods often suffer from negative sampling bias, where similar nodes are incorrectly paired as negative pairs. This can lead to over-clustering, where instances of the same class are divided into different clusters. To address the over-clustering issue, we propose an innovative GCL-based method of graph contrastive learning via cluster-refined negative sampling for semi-supervised text classification, namely ClusterText. Firstly, we combine the pre-trained model Bert with graph neural networks to learn text representations. Secondly, we introduce a clustering refinement strategy, which clusters the learned text representations to obtain pseudo labels. For each text node, its negative sample set is drawn from different clusters. Additionally, we propose a self-correction mechanism to mitigate the loss of true negative samples caused by clustering inconsistency. By calculating the Euclidean distance between each text node and other nodes within the same cluster, distant nodes are still selected as negative samples. Our proposed ClusterText demonstrates good scalable computing, as it can effectively extract important information from from a large amount of data. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of ClusterText in text classification tasks.

articleTitle: Efficient Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks via Optimized Weight Sampling and Pruning
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have revolutionized various fields, especially in applications like image and speech recognition, medical image analysis, and autonomous driving. However, their performance can degrade under uncertain conditions or when trained on small datasets, posing challenges in safety-critical applications. Bayesian Convolutional Neural Networks (BCNNs) address these issues by introducing uncertainty at the model level through weight distributions, enhancing robustness and mitigating overfitting. Despite these advantages, BCNNs suffer from high computational overhead due to the repeated sampling required for each inference, limiting their practical deployment. In this study, we propose X-BCNNs, a novel approach to optimize the weight sampling process in BCNNs. Our method simplifies the computational process by delaying sampling and instead convolving the distribution parameters directly, specifically the mean and variance, which maintains the Gaussian nature of the distribution. This significantly reduces the number of required convolutions from s to two, thereby decreasing the computational load. Additionally, we introduce a pruning strategy based on the distribution of sampled weights, which further reduces complexity by skipping the sampling process for weights below a certain threshold. Our approach not only enhances network sparsity but also improves the efficiency of BCNNs, leading to faster inference times and reduced resource requirements.

articleTitle: Leveraging Middleware to Support Digital Twin System Development
abstract: Digital twin (DT) systems encompass virtual counterparts of physical entities that enable advanced monitoring, simulation, and decision-making processes. Despite their transformative potential, DT systems face significant challenges due to the heterogeneity of technologies and data and the complexity of maintaining synchronized interactions between physical and virtual elements. A middleware solution, with its capability ofoffering standardized development interfaces and runtime services, can abstract these complexities and promote interoperability among diverse components of a DT system. This paper addresses these concerns by proposing MidDiTS, a middleware designed to support the development and operation of DT systems. MidDiTS aims to meet essential requirements for DT systems by providing services for storing DT models, managing DT instances, maintaining causal connections between physical and virtual entities, and integrating with third-party applications. This paper focuses on demonstrating how middleware can facilitate the development of DT systems via a proof of concept involving a DT-powered smart house.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Compression and Reconstruction Based on VQ-VAE-2
abstract: Due to the low bandwidth of underwater acoustic communication, large-sized color images cannot be transmitted in a timely manner. In response to this problem, this paper uses the deep learning-based VQ-VAE-2 model to propose two other finetuning model structures, NVQ and VQI, to encode, compress, transmit, reconstruct and generate large-information original images through convolutional networks. The NVQ model reduces the characteristics of the bottom quantization, and the VQI model re-quantizes the bottom quantization result, which significantly reduces the amount of data transmitted. The picture compression rate of the VQ-VAE-2 model is $13: 1$, and the picture compression rates of NVQ and VQI are 32:1 and 60:1. SSIM (Structural Similarity) of VQ-VAE-2, NVQ and VQI are 0.94, 0.91 and 0.87, respectively. In contrast to previous work, 1) we obtain visually pleasing reconstructions that are perceptually similar to the input, and 2) our approaches have short encoding time and decoding time, generate character strings directly without adding additional overhead, so have shorter transmission time compared with other methods.

articleTitle: Collaborative Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Based Resource Allocation in Clustered IoV Networks
abstract: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) necessitates efficient resource management to meet the growing demands for high data rates, low latency, and real-time communication in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS). This paper presents a novel multiagent reinforcement learning framework based on the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm for optimizing resource allocation in clusters of cells within IoV networks. The framework dynamically allocates transmission power and bandwidth across base stations, each acting as a collaborative agent. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the multi-agent PPO approach outperforms other reinforcement learning algorithms, including Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), regarding throughput, power efficiency, dynamic bandwidth allocation, and overall network performance.

articleTitle: Automated Grading Hemifacial Spasm Using Smartphone Cameras
abstract: Hemifacial spasm is a chronic neurological condition characterized by involuntary facial muscle contractions caused by nerve compression. While familiar to specialists, it is less known to the public and general practitioners, which can lead to difficulties in diagnosis and severity assessment, and even misdiagnosis. Consequently, patients are common to have a long medical history. However, long-term patients tend to have poorer outcomes following surgery, and one-third of patients experience a delayed cure during postoperative rehabilitation. Moreover, $4 \%$ of patients experience recurrence, highlighting the importance of early and accurate diagnosis as well as postoperative monitoring. In this paper, we collected a video dataset of 50 hemifacial spasm patients and 9 healthy adults. We identified three facial features from the videos to establish a novel grading system closely aligned with the medical standards, specifically the Cohen-Albert Grading System. We also developed algorithms capable of automatically grading hemifacial spasm using smartphone cameras based on facial keypoint detection. These algorithms were evaluated on the dataset, achieving an accuracy of $88 \%$ for detection and a mean absolute error of $\mathbf{0 . 4 2}$ for grading.

articleTitle: Language-based Audio Retrieval with Co-Attention Networks
abstract: In recent years, user-generated audio content has proliferated across various media platforms, creating a growing need for efficient retrieval methods that allow users to search for audio clips using natural language queries. This task, known as language-based audio retrieval, presents significant challenges due to the complexity of learning semantic representations from heterogeneous data across both text and audio modalities. In this work, we introduce a novel framework for the language-based audio retrieval task that leverages co-attention mechanismto jointly learn meaningful representations from both modalities. To enhance the model’s ability to capture fine-grained cross-modal interactions, we propose a cascaded co-attention architecture, where co-attention modules are stacked or iterated to progressively refine the semantic alignment between text and audio. Experiments conducted on two public datasets show that the proposed method can achieve better performance than the state-of-the-art method. Specifically, our best performed co-attention model achieves a 16.6% improvement in mean Average Precision on Clotho dataset, and a $\mathbf{1 5. 1 \%}$ improvement on AudioCaps.

articleTitle: A Visualization Approach to Enhance Maintenance in Electric Power Communication Networks
abstract: The electric power communication network is vital for enhancing modern power grids’ efficiency, reliability, and resilience. A critical aspect of maintaining this network is planning physical routes, especially when existing routes are damaged. Currently, this process is mainly manual, involving extensive surveys and analysis, making it time-consuming and prone to errors. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a visualization approach that automates the planning of physical routes for electric power communication networks. Our system provides a comprehensive overview of damaged and potential new routes. By framing route generation as an image inpainting task and employing a GAN-based model, our approach effectively generates appropriate physical routes within specified areas. The effectiveness and usability of this visualization system have been validated by domain experts, confirming its potential to significantly enhance the maintenance and management of electric power communication networks.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Distributed Digital Watermarking effort on Federated Learning: Innovating Intellectual Property Protection
abstract: Federated Learning with Digital Watermarks (FLDW) have been recognized as a promising solution for property protection. However, the existing FLDW-related technologies neglect the requirements of decentralized settings, leading to recurrent issues such as discrepancies in distributed client data. This paper introduces a Blockchain Federated Learning Intellectual Property Protection Framework (BFLIPR), to address the data security and model validation challenges in decentralized federated learning environments. BFLIPR merges blockchain, digital watermarking, and federated learning technologies. By harnessing the blockchain’s tamper-proof properties, digital watermarking’s concealment capabilities, and federated learning’s distributed feature, the framework offers a solution that aligns with intellectual property protection mechanism, to bolster data security and property safeguarding. Experimental findings demonstrate its high feasibility and robust for data privacy and model security in the federated learning.

articleTitle: Ambient IoT in 3GPP Release 19: A Survey
abstract: The ambient Internet of Things (IoT) that utilizes harvest energy is gaining recognition as an innovative technology in the wireless communication industry. The devices associated with this technology, known as Ambient IoT devices, are characterized by being battery-less, low-cost, maintenance-free, smaller size, and low hardware complexity. Recently, the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) has initiated a study on integrating Ambient IoT with the cellular network, to provide widespread and flexible connectivity, meeting the massive deployments of these class ultra-low power Ambient IoT devices. This paper outlines a timely survey of the Ambient IoT within 3GPP Radio Access Network (RAN) Release 19. It presents the technical foundations of Ambient IoT, encompassing representative use case, connectivity typology, service requirement, and device type. Furthermore, it delves into an analysis of the essential protocol functions and gives the signaling procedures for the Ambient IoT. In addition, the paper explores several potential considerations for Ambient IoT that might be explored in the future.

articleTitle: Virtual Keyboard Based on IMU
abstract: The development of sensors and artificial intelligence have promoted human-computer interaction. However, as the most widely used human-computer interaction, traditional typing keyboard, has not undergone fundamental changes in the past few decades. In this paper, a system based on the inertial measurement unit and long short term memory network algorithm are designed to recognize keyboard finger movements and achieve efficient text input. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme achieves over $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$ recognition accuracy for both traditional QWERTY layout keyboards and phone numeric keypads. The proposed virtual keyboard scheme not only saves space but also improves the input convenience for mobile device, which offers the valuable exploration in the smart typing and the interaction with virtual world.

articleTitle: LC-SID: Developing a Local LLM-based Chain-of-thought Framework for Enhanced Sensitive Information Detection
abstract: The detection of sensitive personal information has long been a significant area of research. However, existing methods have inherent limitations. For instance, rule-based matching requires substantial human involvement in the design process and is not well-suited for unstructured documents. Additionally, algorithms based on neural networks, such as LSTM, are limited by the type and size of the training dataset, which restricts their versatility and applicability across diverse domains. Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate robust language comprehension capabilities, making them promising candidates for detecting sensitive personal information. However, directly using mature commercial models on the network may risk leaking sensitive information. This paper proposes an LLM-based framework for identifying sensitive information, which can be deployed locally using open-source LLMs. Our proposed LCSID framework divides the recognition of sensitive information into three subtasks, utilizing a chain-of-thought (CoT) approach. To optimize resource consumption and scalability, each subtask can be handled by its own model. Ultimately, the detection rate for personal sensitive information was $91.9 \%$.

articleTitle: Scalable and Efficient Support Vector Regression Model in Power Systems
abstract: Support Vector Regression (SVR) is a crucial tool for modeling complex relationships in power systems and is widely applied to tasks like demand and load forecasting. SVR, rooted in statistical learning theory and the principle of structural risk minimization, operates by mapping input space to a high-dimensional feature space and constructing an optimal separating hyperplane therein to achieve non-linear regression. In power systems, SVR effectively captures complex non-linear relationships among multidimensional variables such as load, weather, and economic factors, thus excelling in areas like short-term load forecasting and renewable energy generation prediction. However, the high computational cost of SVR presents significant limitations for its practical applications in real-world scenarios, especially in the era of smart grids with their everincreasing data volumes. Traditional SVR algorithms have a time complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(n^{3}\right)$, where n is the number of training samples. This implies that as data scale increases, training time rises dramatically, becoming impractical for large-scale realtime applications. To address this problem, we propose two scalable acceleration algorithms, ALM-SVR and ADMM-SVR, to improve the efficiency of SVR. Both algorithms have linear time complexity and thus are able to be scalable to large-size datasets. We further discuss their extensions and provide theoretical proofs of their boundedness and convergence. Experimental results on benchmark and real power system datasets show that our methods significantly outperform conventional SVR solvers in terms of running time and are therefore suitable for large-scale applications in power systems.

articleTitle: A Priority-Aware Task Offloading Method with Knowledge Distillation in Edge Computing
abstract: With the swift proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, offloading tasks efficiently is essential for enhancing system performance. Numerous strategies for task offloading in edge computing environments have been introduced. They often fall short of effectively managing task prioritization and latency requirements. To address this issue, this paper introduces a priority-aware task offloading approach that integrates Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Knowledge Distillation (KD). The method employs a Dueling duDeep QNetwork (Dueling DQN) model coupled with a priority-weighted reward mechanism to refine task offloading decisions. By incorporating a pre-trained teacher model, we facilitate the learning process of the DRL agent and bolster its performance. The experimental outcomes demonstrate that our proposed approach outperforms four comparative benchmark methods, achieving notable improvements in average latency, the ratio of overdue tasks, and the priority-weighted average delay.

articleTitle: CPIMAC: MEC-assisted Message Dissemination Based on Traffic Prediction at Intersections
abstract: The Internet of Vehicles (IoV) is gaining increasing attention for its ability to improve traffic safety and efficiency by providing situational awareness and detecting potential hazards beyond the visual range. Time division multiple access (TDMA) based communication protocol effectively prevents transmission collisions in IoV. However, road intersections pose challenges for the implementation of TDMA-based MAC protocols, as vehicles converge from different directions, leading to severe communication access and merging collisions. To address this issue, we propose a distributed MAC protocol named slot collisions prediction based MAC at intersection (CPIMAC). Specifically, We combine mobile edge computing (MEC) with a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention neural network model to predict potential transmission collisions and propose corresponding collision avoidance algorithms. In addition, we design the head-tail beacon (HTB) algorithm to reduce slot collisions during vehicle waiting periods at intersections by adjusting beacon frequency. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments to evaluate the proposed protocol. The results show that transmission collisions can be reduced by $58.1 \%$ compared to the existing protocols.

articleTitle: Multistage Disturbances Label Mixing for Weakly-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Weakly supervised medical image segmentation with scribble annotation has witnessed great progress. Using pseudolabels to assist scribble annotations is a crucial technique. Most previous methods involve mixing predictions from different outputs to generate pseudo-labels, producing more completed supervision. However, these mixing methods often ignore to produce distinguished region-level pseudo labels, resulting in increasingly similar predictions, which further suppress the quality of pseudo labels due to the ineffective prediction mixing strategy. In this paper, we propose a Multistage Disturbances Label Mixing method to build a new label mixing strategy by mining discriminate regional predictions. Specifically, we randomly crop the same regions in different predictions generated by the dual-branch network and bi-directionally exchange them. After that, predictions are mixed up to generate discriminative pseudo labels. In addition, to produce more distinguished region-level pseudo labels, we incorporate disturbances in both the input and network structure. Experimental results on the public ACDC dataset demonstrate that our method performs better than the current weakly-supervised medical image segmentation methods. The code will be released.

articleTitle: Large Model Based Crossmodal Chinese Poetry Creation
abstract: Generating Chinese poetry is a complex task with significant potential for large models. However, most current systems only support single-model of input and the output lacks interpretability. This paper proposes a large model based system that supports cross-modal input of text and image, provides interpretable annotations for generated Chinese poems, and supports multiple rounds of iterative optimization. First, it analyzes images with CLIP and MiniGPT-4 and generates descriptive text from analysis with ERNIE-4.0. Then, it generates Chinese ancient poems from the input text and descriptive text by ERNIE-4.0, using our devised prompts based on CRISPE. Finally, it evaluates and then optimizes the created poems with prompts based on few-shot. Preliminary evaluations have validated the efficacy of our poetry scoring criteria and demonstrated the superior performance of the system when utilizing the conjunction of text and imagery as cross-modal inputs.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Real-Time Forensic Evidence Collection System for a Secure Metaverse
abstract: Metaverses have evolved beyond mere avatar-based games and entertainment into complex environments where social, cultural, and economic activities mirror those in the real world. This development has led to the emergence of not only offline threats but also cybercrimes within virtual spaces, highlighting the need for effective measures to ensure safety in the metaverse. Traditional forensic methods, which focus on collecting and analyzing evidence after an incident, often fall short in real-time environments like the metaverse. Additionally, the diverse nature of data in the metaverse and the associated privacy issues pose further challenges in evidence collection. To address these needs, this paper introduces a specialized Forensic Evidence Collection System, FECS, designed specifically for the metaverse. This system operates through three core stages: evidence caching, evidence recording, and evidence submission. By employing lightweight recording methods, data compression, and selective recording technologies, the system efficiently manages storage and ensures accurate event timelines. Hash values and watermarking technologies are utilized to verify the integrity and authenticity of video evidence, protecting against tampering and unauthorized alterations.
