This approach aims to significantly enhance the efficiency and reliability of forensic processes within virtual environments. Additionally, evidence management is supported by permissioned blockchain. This blockchain model restricts participation to verified nodes, safeguarding the confidentiality and privacy of sensitive data from a large number of users. Through this controlled and secure environment, the system maintains high standards of data protection while facilitating robust forensic investigation.

articleTitle: Modeling and analyzing approach for safety-critical cyberattacks effects on connected autonomous vehicles
abstract: The open-access perception and communication environment makes the connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) vulnerable to cyberattacks, causing concerns on traffic safety and security. Cyberattacks on cyber layer in the CAV can threaten the behavior of physical subjects at the vehicle layer. Scholars have typically used improved car-following models or control models to explore CAV behavior under cyberattacks. However, the complexity and diversity of cyberattacks make modelling of CAV status challenging. Moreover, these models lack quantitative evaluation metrics. This paper proposes a modeling framework to support a comprehensive analysis of CAV performance under cyberattacks. Firstly, we categorize potential safety-critical cyberattacks faced by CAVs into false data attack and delayed message attack based on their consequence. Secondly, we develop a generalized vehicle dynamics model that accounts for the cyberattack effects on safety of CAVs. Finally we propose four metrics for describing the change in state of the CAV when it is under cyberattack. Experimental results shows that the effects of different safetycritical cyberattack on CAV varies. This research contributes to the understanding of CAV status under cyberattacks and provides a foundation for enhancing the cybersecurity of CAV.

articleTitle: EM-Mamba: An Edge-Mix Enhanced Long-Range Sequential Modeling Mamba for Kidney Segmentation in CT Scans
abstract: Manual delineation of the kidney region in CT scans is a laborious process. Although existing models have achieved remarkable success in the realm of automated segmentation, they still encounter challenges in effectively modeling both the global and local information. To address this, we introduce Edge-Mix enhanced Mamba (EM-Mamba) for kidney segmentation, which is designed to capture global and local information from multi-scales. EM-Mamba leverages SegMamba as its backbone, utilizing Mamba’s efficiency in extracting long-range dependencies. To further enhance the model’s integration of local and global information, we introduce the Edge-Mix module, which captures edge information from the shallow layers of the network during the encoding phase and merges it with multi-scale features during the decoding phase. Additionally, a Multi-Scale Convolution (MSC) module is designed to enhance the capability of extracting effective information from 3D medical images, achieving a fusion of rich local and global information across multiple scales. The innovation of the EM-Mamba model lies in its integration of detailed and global information, as well as its robust feature extraction ability in 3D medical image analysis, offering a new solution for precise kidney segmentation. The experimental results show that our framework achieving a Dice score of $\mathbf{9 1 . 9 5}$ % on the KiTS21 dataset and 86.35 % Dice score on our proprietary dataset called Kidney Parenchyma Segmentation (KPS).

articleTitle: Proof of Similarity: Searchability-enhancing Blockchain Consensus for Industrial Digital Twins
abstract: Recently, industrial digital twins have been widely adopted to create a digital replica of the industrial sites for real-time simulation, intelligent decision-making, and automatic feedback control. However, the bi-directional information flows between the physical twin and digital twin are facing unique challenges in guaranteeing data authenticity and improving data searchability. Existing studies propose employing blockchain-empowered industrial digital twins to authenticate the information flow. They also consider improving data security and privacy and deploying blockchain-empowered industrial digital twins on emerging 6G and edge networks. However, they neglect the provision of high-efficiency data query services. This work is the first to consider the searchability issue in blockchain-empowered industrial digital twins. We propose a general system architecture of blockchain-empowered industrial digital twins applicable for various applications. The key novelty of this work lies in the proof-of-similarity blockchain consensus mechanism that significantly improves the search efficiency of industrial digital twins data. More specifically, proof of similarity guarantees that the generated block contains semantically similar data and a block summary. Then, the blockchain queries will be compared with the block summaries before entering the transactions in the blocks. In this way, up to $\mathbf{9 2. 0 \%}$ of the blocks can be skipped during blockchain query, resulting in an 87.4% reduction of the average query completion time.

articleTitle: RetNAS: Reinforce Evolutionary Trend in Lightweight Neural Architecture Search
abstract: Neural architecture search (NAS) based on zero-shot proxy evaluation assesses neural networks using mathematical metrics without requiring actual network training, resulting in the fastest evaluation speed in the NAS field and can greatly reduce the cost of neural network development on portable environment. However, the commonly used evolutionary-based search strategies in such algorithms often suffer from slow convergence and require numerous iterations, limiting their performance advantages. In this paper, we demonstrated diversity within the population and the number of iterations for dominant individuals as key efficiency factors in Evolutionary NAS tasks. Based on this, we propose a novel evolutionary algorithm-based lightweight neural architecture search method called RetNAS. RetNAS uses a low-cost method to explicitly model the probability distribution of operators and hyperparameters of dominant individuals in neural architecture search, thereby guiding the random architecture search process. It accelerates convergence speed and improves search results through a gradual mixing and iterative process. Experimental results show that compared to baseline algorithms, RetNAS achieves equivalent evaluation metrics with only 50% of the search steps, substantially expediting the search process. Furthermore, RetNAS can be easily integrated into other NAS algorithms, providing similar performance improvements.

articleTitle: MERIT: Multimodal Wearable Vital Sign Waveform Monitoring
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death and premature mortality worldwide, with occupational environments significantly influencing CVD risk, underscoring the need for effective cardiac monitoring and early warning systems. Existing methods of monitoring vital signs require subjects to remain stationary, which is impractical for daily monitoring as individuals are often in motion. To address this limitation, we propose MERIT, a multimodality-based wearable system designed for precise ECG waveform monitoring without movement restrictions. Daily activities, involving frequent arm movements, can significantly affect sensor data and complicate the reconstruction of accurate ECG signals. To mitigate motion impact and enhance ECG signal reconstruction, we introduce a deep independent component analysis (Deep-ICA) module and a multimodal fusion module. We conducted experiments with 15 subjects. Our results, compared with commercial wearable devices and existing methods, demonstrate that MERIT accurately reconstructs ECG waveforms during various office activities, offering a reliable solution for fine-grained cardiac monitoring in dynamic environments.

articleTitle: A Meta-learning-based Domain-invariant Method for Cuff-less Blood Pressure Estimation
abstract: Cuff-less blood pressure estimation methods usually require personalized fine-tuning to achieve better estimation accuracy due to significant inter-individual data variability. The emerging domain generalization methods can extract blood pressure-related knowledge from diverse individuals and estimate readings for unseen subjects; however, these existing methods are less effective in aligning distributions for regression tasks on highly individual physiological time-series data. In this paper, we present a meta-learning-based approach for domainin-variant blood pressure estimation (MetaDIBP), which optimizes a temporal invariant representation learning module with a twostage meta-learning strategy. Specifically, we minimize differences between a prospective target domain and the rest of the source domains in the meta-training stage; update the model utilizing all source domains to ensure consistent and robust performance across various unseen target domains in the successive metatesting stage; and incorporate deep feature extraction, Correlation Alignment loss, and Maximum Mean Discrepancy loss into a temporal invariant representation learning module to serve as the network architecture for feature distribution discrepancy reduction. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional domain generalization and deep-learning-based blood pressure models, achieving a mean absolute error of $12.989 \mathbf{~ m m H g}$ for systolic blood pressure and 7.391 mmHg for diastolic blood pressure. With personalized finetuning, the mean absolute error further improves to 7.464 mmHg for systolic blood pressure and $4.509 \mathbf{~ m m H g}$ for diastolic blood pressure, showing advantages over existing methods.

articleTitle: Document Information Extraction Framework Based on Graph Enhanced Language Model
abstract: During the process of intelligent transformation and digital upgrading in the industry, a large amount of document data containing both structured and unstructured information has been generated. Efficiently and accurately extracting valuable information from these documents has become a pressing issue for both industry and academia. Traditional document information extraction models primarily focus on document pre-training models that emphasize entity feature representation within the documents. However, combining the structural information of entity pairs in unstructured documents can help improve the accuracy of information extraction. This paper proposes a Visual-Rich Document Information Extraction Framework based on Graph Neural Network Enhanced Language Model (GELM). This method leverages the document reconstruction capabilities of pre-trained models enhanced by graph neural networks. It uses the visual, textual, and structural aspects of documents as inputs to the graph neural network and integrates the outputs of the graph neural network and the pre-trained model through a biaffine attention mechanism, thereby extracting entities and their relationships from the documents. Comparative experimental results show that the proposed method improves the performance by ${1 \% - 2 \%}$ compared to the baseline pre-trained models, validating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: LDQN: A Lightweight Deep Reinforcement Learning Model
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) integrates Reinforcement Learning (RL) with Deep Learning and has made remarkable strides in several domains, such as gaming, robotic control, autonomous driving, and natural language processing. Yet, in real-world applications, many deep learning models utilizing Deep Q-learning Networks (DQN) continue to encounter issues like slow training times and significant computational expenses. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a lightweight deep reinforcement learning model based on DQN, called Lightweight Deep Q-learning Network (LDQN). LDQN incorporates design concepts from the lightweight convolutional neural network MobileNet, adapting the first two standard convolutional layers into depthwise separable convolutions to minimize computational costs and model size. Additionally, the network employs the efficient and high-performance H-Swish activation function to boost image feature extraction abilities while minimizing computational overhead. A series of experimental results demonstrate that the proposed LDQN model not only reduces computational costs and model parameters but also delivers exceptional performance in Atari games.

articleTitle: MoodCam: Mood Prediction Through Smartphone-Based Facial Affect Analysis in Real-World Settings
abstract: MoodCam introduces a novel method for assessing mood by utilizing facial affect analysis through the front-facing camera of smartphones during everyday activities. We collected facial behavior primitives during 15,995 real-world phone interactions involving 25 participants over four weeks. We developed three models for timely intervention: momentary, daily average, and next day average. Notably, our models exhibit AUC scores ranging from 0.58 to 0.64 for Valence and 0.60 to 0.63 for Arousal. These scores are comparable to or better than those from some previous studies. This predictive ability suggests that MoodCam can effectively forecast mood trends, providing valuable insights for timely interventions and resource planning in mental health management. The results are promising as they demonstrate the viability of using real-time and predictive mood analysis to aid in mental health interventions and potentially offer preemptive support during critical periods identified through mood trend shifts.

Author Keywords: Empirical study that tells us about people

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Honeynet Technology Based on Machine Learning
abstract: In order to change the passive situation of the defender in the industrial control system security confrontation, honeypot honeynet as a typical deceptive defense technology has received wide attention. The static characteristics of traditional honeynet technology make it limited when dealing with complex network environments, for this reason, artificial intelligence technology was introduced to propose a threat trapping technology based on machine learning algorithms for industrial control systems. Aiming at the problems faced by the power industrial control system, such as the complexity of the type of anomalous traffic and the high dimensionality of the characteristics, the Random Forest algorithm is introduced to design the data detection module of the dynamic honeynet system, which improves the accuracy of the anomalous traffic identification. Meanwhile, the DQN algorithm of deep reinforcement learning is utilized to help the honeynet system make dynamic adjustment of strategies when facing different attack behaviors. Based on the typical network security dataset CIC-IDS-2017, the feasibility and effectiveness of the above design were verified. The experimental results show that the technique can effectively improve the network security protection capability of industrial control systems.

articleTitle: Efficient and Atomic Cross-blockchain Transaction Processing for Decentralized Web3 Applications
abstract: Web3 has received considerable attention from industry and academia due to its groundbreaking revolution to decentralize the current centralized web. As a fundamental building block, blockchain provides web3 with the ability to rebuild trust in the trustless decentralized web. More and more blockchain-based web3 applications are taking place and becoming successful. Many web3 applications generate coupled data and transactions from multiple blockchains and demand efficient and atomic cross-blockchain transaction processing; however, existing approaches rarely consider transaction atomicity, and the processing efficiency is inferior. In this work, we formally model multi-blockchain systems and formulate the cross-blockchain transaction processing problem. Then, we propose a novel consensus mechanism, namely proof of credible contributions, to solve the efficiency and atomicity issues in cross-blockchain transaction processing. Inside, we define credible contributions as a measure of blockchain nodes’ credits and workload, so as to make nodes compete to handle as many cross-blockchain transactions as possible. Furthermore, we propose the flag-referenceconfirm protocol to guarantee transaction atomicity. Extensive experimental results indicate the efficiency and effectiveness of proof of credible contributions.

articleTitle: A Survey of Machine Learning-based TLS 1.3 Encrypted Traffic Analysis
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet technology has elevated the importance of encrypted communication protocols in network security. As transport layer security (TLS) becomes the predominant encryption protocol, its latest version, TLS 1.3, introduces enhanced security features that challenge conventional traffic analysis approaches. This survey examines how machine learning techniques are being adapted to analyze TLS 1.3 encrypted traffic effectively. Specifically, this paper describes the broad application scenarios for TLS traffic analysis at first, and highlight their importance. Next, we introduce the key modifications of TLS 1.3 and analyzed the significance of these modifications. Then, we also review the latest developments in machine learning methods specifically designed for TLS 1.3 traffic analysis. Finally, the major challenges currently facing the field and future research trends are introduced in this paper, providing a roadmap for researchers in this evolving field.

articleTitle: Anti-Spoofing Detection on Zero-Shot Synthetic Audios With Self-Supervised Representation Learning
abstract: Synthetic speech spoofing attacks maliciously use machine-synthesized speech to impersonate individuals and bypass speaker verification systems, posing security risks to people’s privacy. In this paper, we propose an enhanced anti-spoofing detection module, which utilizes self-supervised representations to differentiate between synthetic and bona fide speech, especially on the advanced zero-shot synthetic speech. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method, achieving a 65% reduction in the equal error rate metric for detecting zero-shot spoofing, and a 79% enhancement in generalizing against unknown attacks compared to baseline systems. Extensive experiments also validate the efficacy of applying pre-trained models in zero-shot spoofing detection, and demonstrate the value of using state-of-the-art zero-shot synthetic speech data to enhance anti-spoofing datasets.

articleTitle: FireInvestLLM: Leveraging Large Language Models for Improved Fire Investigation Inquiries
abstract: Fire incidents occur frequently worldwide, and reliable fire investigations are crucial for uncovering the causes of fires, assessing damages, and improving prevention and control measures. To enhance the efficiency and accuracy of fire investigations, we propose an automated inquiry simulation pipeline based on LLMs, named FireInvestLLM. Specifically, we firstly performed Supervised Fine-Tuning on the model using our custom fire investigation instruction dataset, equipping it with domain knowledge. Secondly, we optimised the prompt design by retrieving historical similar case inquery templates, thus improving the model’s capabilities in role-playing, event comprehension and instruction execution. Finally, we enhance the dialogue flow through a question validation and self-reflection to ensure that the model maintains consistent professionalism and consistency across multiple rounds of dialogue. We utilized a custom fire incident dataset to evaluate our method. Experimental results show that FireInvestLLM significantly enhances the quality of inquiry dialogues in fire investigations, showcasing its substantial potential in practical applications and providing fire departments with an efficient AI assistant.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Approach for Effective Visual Question Answering
abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) presents a multifaceted challenge, requiring models to process and integrate both textual and visual data. The Transformer architecture, with its self-attention mechanism, has proven highly effective in managing global dependencies, making it a popular choice for many VQA models. However, a key challenge lies in achieving an optimal balance between global and local dependency modeling within conventional Transformer frameworks. Addressing this issue, our research introduces an innovative Transformer-based approach that employs region-specific self-attention for VQA. In contrast to models that concentrate exclusively on global dependencies, our method concurrently executes intra and inter-window attention operations to effectively capture contextual information from images. By utilizing regional windows for visual feature processing, our model eliminates redundancy in global self-attention while still preserving rich contextual details. The efficacy of our proposed technique, which relies on the utilization of visual features, has been extensively evaluated through experiments. These assessments were conducted using widely recognized VQA benchmark datasets, specifically VQA 2.0 and CLEVR. Our findings demonstrate that the model outperforms existing benchmark alternatives across various performance metrics. Notably, it achieved superior test results of $\mathbf{7 1 . 9 3 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 8 . 6 2 \%}$ on the VQA 2.0 and CLEVR datasets, respectively, underscoring its effectiveness in tackling complex VQA tasks.

articleTitle: ASD classification framework based-on temporal neural features
abstract: In recent years, more and more studies have begun to focus on the association between brain activity and disease, and functional magnetic resonance imaging(fMRI) of the brain has provided new perspectives for these studies.However, the high complexity of fMRI data and the fact that feature extraction has to capture temporal changes while reducing dimensionality have posed new challenges to temporal feature extraction methods.To address the above problems, this paper takes the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange(ABIDE) dataset as an example and proposes a temporal feature extraction method for fMRI data of the brain, which is able to reduce the complexity of MRI data and retain the time-varying information, and to extract the dynamic network features with the help of graph theory to identify the correlation situation and the change of connectivity pattern among brain network regions.

articleTitle: Make It Easy: Action Quality Assessment of Cyborg Animals Based on Spatial-Temporal Pose Inference
abstract: Assessing the action quality of cyborg animals helps to adjust control strategies, guide the development of control algorithm, and enhance the efficiency of navigation and military applications. However, existing research is limited in control algorithm and ignores the assessment of movement smoothness. In this paper, we first propose EASY, an effective assessment framework, which is able to (i) evaluate the action quality of cyborg animals of various sizes and motion patterns; (ii) obtain assessment results directly based on keypoints. Specifically, EASY first captures keypoints sequences through a small object pose estimation module. It employs the convolutional block attention module (CBAM) and depthwise over parameterized convolution (DOConv), allowing more accurate feature recognition with fewer parameters. Then, EASY employs multi-field fusion strategy that merges commonalities and differences, enabling a comprehensive and accurate assessment of fluency. We tested EASY on both CyborgRat-MFA dataset and CyborgBee-MFA dataset. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the assessment results are consistent with human expert scores, which prove that our proposed EASY is reasonable, effective, and interpretable.

articleTitle: Distributed Inverted List Indexes Technology Based on Virtual Data Space
abstract: Inverted index list technology is a common feature of modern full-text search systems. It uses keywords as query conditions to retrieve all documents containing the specified keywords. Indexing is crucial for achieving fast queries in virtual data spaces. Previous research has focused on data sharing and data migration. However, for virtual data spaces, where storage resources are widely dispersed and autonomously isolated, distributed management of inverted indexes to overcome the I/O bottlenecks of single processors remains a challenging problem. In this work, we design an efficient distributed inverted index for virtual data space and conduct experiments using customized retrieval algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on AR target recognition algorithm for mobile based on YOLOv8
abstract: In this paper, the latest YOLO series algorithm YOLOv8 is studied in depth, and based on it, an improved target detection algorithm, designed for mobile, is proposed to realize an AR system for real-time recognition of industrial elements. Aiming at the problems of large number of model parameters, large computation, not easy to deploy, as well as recognition errors and instability due to light changes and viewpoint movement that occur in the deployment of target detection models on mobile, YOLOv8 is improved and YOLOv8-PDS is proposed. In this paper, a new structure SPC is proposed based on Partial Conv, which is used to replace the C2f in the network. module, this innovation significantly reduces the amount of computation and the number of parameters, and at the same time effectively improves the speed of the network as an efficient inference of the convolution. In addition, the article introduces an ultra-lightweight and efficient dynamic upsampling technique, DySample, and incorporates a spatial context-aware module, SCAM, to further improve the detection accuracy. These improvements ensure a significant reduction in the number of parameters, computation, and model size without compromising accuracy. With the lightweight improvements, the YOLOv8-PDS model reduces the computation by 22.2%, the number of parameters by 17.8%, and the model size by 17.5% compared to YOLOv8, making it easier to be deployed on AR devices, while achieving $\mathbf{9 0. 0 \%}$ accuracy and $\mathbf{0. 8 \%}$ recall improvement. In order to verify the ease of deployment and stability of YOLOv8-PDS, this paper designs an AR interactive system that converts YOLOv8-PDS models to ONNX format and implements the interactive mode through the Unity3D platform, so as to develop a mobile AR application with integrated target detection function.

articleTitle: Smart DCU Digital Twin: Towards Autism-Friendly Universities
abstract: Digital Twins are one of the emerging technologies which facilitate the creation of a digital replica of physical assets and infrastructure. The majority of initial use-cases of digital twins for smart cities and smart universities has focused on creation of the 3D representation of the infrastructure. However, with the maturity of technology, digital twins are nowadays used to build use-cases for smart applications which involve multiple sources of information including geographical information, IoT sensors and use-case specific knowledge bases. Smart DCU Digital Twin is one of the initiative towards achieving a smart university status for Dublin City University (DCU). Across the globe and in Ireland many universities including DCU are working on providing additional support to students with ASD (Autism Spectrum Disorder). The primary focus of these initiatives is on improving social interactions, and reducing academic and sensory barriers for the students. In this paper, we present our work on using digital twin technology to assist DCU in achieving its objective of becoming a fully inclusive and an Autism-Friendly university, with a particular focus on the reduction of sensory barriers for its students.

articleTitle: ARR: An Attention-Based Robust Residual Network Architecture
abstract: As controllers of safety-critical systems, the robustness of feedforward neural networks is crucial. Although current research mainly focuses on developing adversarial training methods, the impact of network structure on robustness cannot be ignored. In this paper, we propose a novel robust deep network, AttentiveRobustResNet(ARR), which integrates the residual network architecture and the multi-head self-attention mechanism to effectively improve the model’s robustness in the face of adversarial samples without increasing additional model parameters. By using the multi-head self-attention mechanism to replace part of the convolution operation for feature extraction, the global information capture ability of the network is improved. By adjusting the sub-components of the network (activation function, data augmentation), the impact of abnormal phenomena such as gradient disappearance and global information loss in adversarial training on the robustness of adversarial training is alleviated. Based on adopting various adversarial training methods, this paper conducts extensive experimental validation of different adversarial attacks on multiple datasets. The results show that AttentiveRobustResNet significantly improves adversarial robustness compared with other neural network models under the same parameter scale. In particular, compared to the baseline network ResNet50, our model achieves an ${8 \%}$ improvement in clean accuracy and a 5% improvement in adversarial robustness (AA) under the TRADES adversarial training framework.

articleTitle: A Survey on Digital Twin: From Industrial Applications to Cybersecurity
abstract: Digital twin technology is swiftly advancing due to its transformative potential to reshape various sectors. However, despite its vast possibilities, a full understanding of its applications remains limited. Digital twins involve creating virtual representations of physical assets, different systems, or processes, allowing real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and performance optimization. These digital replicas enable dynamic interaction between the physical and virtual worlds, supporting continuous data exchange and feedback loops. By utilizing advanced technologies such as sensors, IoT, and AI, digital twins can simulate and analyze real-world conditions, forecast future scenarios, and optimize operations with realtime insights. Industries use digital twins to simulate production processes, validate designs, and accelerate product development cycles. While existing research primarily focuses on the physical aspects of digital twins and their role within Industry 4.0, this survey aims to showcase the broader transformative potential of digital twins across diverse sectors, including manufacturing, IoT, 5G, blockchain, AI devices, healthcare, and energy. Additionally, it is the first survey to explore digital twin applications in cybersecurity, specifically in securing smart energy systems and cyber-physical systems. The study further examines the growing role of digital twins in boosting operational efficiency and driving innovation.

articleTitle: A Dirty Data Identification Method in Mechanical Equipment Condition Monitoring
abstract: The rise of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIOT) has brought new opportunities for the mechanical equipment condition monitoring. The trend towards intelligent and automated production of mechanical equipment has become mainstream. However, in the actual operational environment, mechanical equipment is often mixed with a large amount of dirty data unrelated to equipment failures, which seriously affects equipment fault diagnosis and wastes maintenance resources. To improve the reliability of mechanical equipment health status analysis, this paper proposes a new method for dirty data identification suitable for mechanical equipment condition monitoring. First, utilizing the time-space position encoding (TSPE) to map positional relationships between sequences. Next, designing a time-dimension attention (TDA) mechanism to capture the correlation between multiple temporal attribute features and the temporal dependencies between preceding and subsequent data. Then, building a dirty data identification model using an improved Transformer network and Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). Finally, employing an adaptive thresholding method to dynamically set thresholds, determining the degree of data anomalies by comparing anomaly scores with the threshold. The effectiveness of the proposed method are validated through one simulation experiment and one real-world example. The F1 Score of this method on the simulated missing data and drifting data is 0.9874 and 0.9838. On the drive-end and fan-end is $\mathbf{0. 9 7 0 0}$ and 0.9882 at Case Western Reserve University (CWRU). Compared to other dirty data identification methods in the field, this method has better dirty data identification capability.

articleTitle: Exploring the Mental Health of Virtual Soundscape: A Systematic Review
abstract: This systematic review explores the application of virtual reality (VR) technology in soundscape research and its impact on mental health. It also compares virtual soundscapes with real-world soundscapes. We followed the PRISMA guidelines to examine publications in the Web of Science and Scopus databases, ultimately identifying 27 articles closely related to our research. Our review shows that the VR soundscape can provide restorative benefits similar to real-world natural settings. The VR technology enhances soundscape research by enabling precise manipulation of acoustic parameters and offers a more immersive experience than traditional monitors (e.g., complex and dynamic situations in reality). The review underscores the individual differences of virtual soundscapes on mental health, such as the restoration of older adults and patients. However, VR technology still falls short of fully replicating the multisensory richness of real-world environments, which may limit its restorative potential. Despite these challenges, VR technology presents valuable opportunities for the healthy environmental design of game space and short videos by enabling innovative soundscape simulations. Future research should focus on addressing technical limitations and implications of VR soundscape, such as real-time audio performance and sound transmission, which contribute to the realism and effectiveness of virtual soundscapes in enhancing mental well-being.

articleTitle: MAI-Unet: A Multi-Scale Attention Interactive Network for Multivariate Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
abstract: In recent years, Transformer models based on multiscale fusion have made significant progress in the field of multivariate long-term time series forecasting(MLTSF). Compared to traditional Transformer models, cross-scale models can better model long-term dependencies and extract multi-level features. However, they focus more on time dependencies at different scales and rarely consider the interrelationships between time series variables. Based on this issue, we propose a Mixed Pooling Spatio-Temporal Attention (MPSTA) module, aimed at efficiently extracting time dependencies and variable correlations in sequences. Moreover, this module can more accurately calculate attention weights while maintaining the relative spatial and temporal positions of multiple variables. Additionally, we propose a novel multi-scale attention interaction Unet network (MAIUnet), which can establish long-term and short-term dependencies in time series through cross-scale learning, addressing the traditional multi-scale model’s inability to fully utilize adjacent scale information. Through extensive experiments on eight public datasets, compared to the best Transformer-based model, MAIUnet achieved 31 optimal results and 25 second-best results in all test cases. In particular, on the Weather dataset, we achieved the best performance, with MSE decreasing by $\mathbf{1 0. 0 6 \%}$ and MAE decreasing by $\mathbf{5. 6 6 \%}$.

articleTitle: UbiPen:Digitizing Analogue Pens with a Finger-Mounted IMU
abstract: We present UbiPen, a novel mobile and wearable sensing technique that augments analogue pens at hand with digital input capabilities. UbiPen senses pen contacts on physical surfaces, 2D locations of pen tip, and various types of pen tips and surfaces. UbiPen requires only a single inertial measurement unit (IMU) mounted on users’ fingernail, which is lightweight as well as flexible, and able to preserve the nuanced analogue writing experiences with conventional pens. According to our evaluation, UbiPen reaches an average accuracy of 95.8% for pen contact detection on physical surfaces, 88.4% for surfaces recognition (six types) and 89.1% for pen tips recognition (three types). In a 2D Fitts’ Law and Steering Law study, we verified that our technique is capable of serving as a 2D pointing device. Finally, we illustrate the potential of UbiPen by presenting several applications. UbiPen blurs the boundary between analogue pens and augmented pens with digital functionalities, providing new interaction possibilities with analogue pens.

articleTitle: DACA: A Distributed Algorithm for Task Partitioning and Offloading in Mobile Edge Computing Networks Supporting Transformer
abstract: Recent studies have explored collaborative Transformer-based inference in edge computing (EC), but they often overlook the mobility of users and edge devices, leading to potential reliability issues. This paper aims to minimize inference latency in mobile edge computing (MEC) by considering heterogeneity in mobility, computation, and communication. We propose a task partitioning model utilizing the GPipe scheme for Transformer-based inference. The task partitioning and offloading problem is then formulated with constraints on computation resources and mobility, decomposed into a bin-packing problem and an integer optimization problem. To solve these subproblems, we introduce the Distributed Aggregated Competition Algorithm (DACA). Extensive simulations and testbed experiments demonstrate the high performance of our proposed algorithm in minimizing inference latency across heterogeneous mobile edge devices and networks.

articleTitle: Complementary Learning and Smooth Representation for Multi-view Subspace Clustering
abstract: Recent multi-view clustering methods have made significant progress in exploring the consistent and inconsistent features of multi-view data. However, existing methods either discard inconsistent features or directly fuse inconsistent features that contain corruptions, failing in making full utilization of complementary features contained in inconsistency. In addition, many methods fail to maintain the local neighborhood relationship between data in subspace learning, which inevitably loses information. To address these issues, we propose Complementary Learning and Smooth Representation for Multi-view Subspace Clustering (CLSRMC). Firstly, we differentiate the learned inconsistent features into complementary features beneficial for clustering and unfavorable corruptions, and impose different regularization constraints respectively. Secondly, we apply smooth regularization to the complementary features to supplement local structure information. Finally, a consensus graph containing complementary information of each view is obtained through graph fusion. An efficient iterative algorithm is designed to solve the optimization problem of CLSRMC. Extensive experiments on five real-world datasets validate the superiority of our method.

articleTitle: An Intelligent IoT Service Support Platform based on Cyber-Physical Space Convergence
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) connects more and more ubiquitous physical objects into cyber space to enable the cyberphysical space convergence. The ubiquitous access, uniform identification and comprehensive cognition of physical objects have become the basic challenges of IoT-enabled cyber-physical convergence space. In order to solve these three problems, we propose an intelligent IoT service support platform in this paper. Firstly, we propose an edge computing-based open IoT system architecture to satisfy the real-time process analytics and bandwidth requirements demanded by ubiquitous access of large-scale IoT objects. Then the enabling technologies of edge computing-based object identification and resolution are proposed to solve the uniform identification and identity consistency problems of IoT objects accessing into cyber space. Thirdly, the enabling technologies of knowledge graph-based object description modeling and discovery system are also proposed to realize the comprehensive digital twins modeling of physical objects, and discover suitable objects to meet application requirements. Finally, combining the Industrial IoT (IIoT) application, an illustrative use case is introduced. The proposed approach can improve the capacities of physical objects to be accessed, recognized and cognized by cyber space so that smart IoT applications and edge services can be supported.

articleTitle: GIN-LDP: A Graph Isomorphism Network-based Model for Loan Default Prediction
abstract: Loan default prediction is a key task in financial risk management, which directly affects the risk and return of financial institutions. To enhance the prediction accuracy, this study proposes a loan default prediction model GIN-LDP based on graph isomorphism network(GIN). First, based on the multi-source data, the lender’s historical credit behavior features, recent credit trend features and personal wealth soft information features are extracted respectively. Then, based on the above three kinds of extracted features, the graph structure is constructed with the lender as the node of each graph. In the multi-view graph structure, the random walk positional encoding(RWPE) is introduced to capture the global dependency features of the nodes, which are fused with the node features to perform a comprehensive characterization and through the GIN module, which aggregates adjacent and higher-order neighbor features. Finally, a fully connected layer is used for node classification prediction to discriminate whether the lender’s current loan application is at risk of default. Experiments conducted on home credit default risk dataset and lending club dataset validate the effectiveness of the GIN-LDP model.

articleTitle: Illumination-Aware Infrared and Visible Image Fusion for Nighttime Object Tracking
abstract: The change of illumination has a great impact on the imaging effect of visible image. In the tracking scene of bad illumination or weather conditions, visible image cannot effectively and comprehensively describe the imaging scene. It is important to consider the effect of illumination change in the process of feature extraction and fusion, and fuse complementary information from visible modality and thermal infrared modality to provide a comprehensive description of the scene. Aiming to enhance the performance of nighttime object detection and tracking, this paper designs an illumination-aware module, which utilizes the illumination information contained in the visible image. The module generates the fusion weights for the visible and thermal infrared images. Then the multi-modal fusion algorithm based on the module for object tracking is proposed. Extensive experiments have shown that the proposed illumination-aware multi-modal fusion effectively improves the performance of object tracking in the nighttime environment.

articleTitle: Intensify Knowledge Tracing for Learning Performance Prediction via Tensor-Based Self-Attention
abstract: The purpose of Knowledge Tracing (KT) is to model students’ mastery of Knowledge Concepts (KCs) and predict their future learning performance. Nevertheless, current attention-based methods focus exclusively on direct relationships among KCs and analyze these relationships using low-order attention weights. These methods neglect the indirect relationships among KCs and fail to incorporate multidimensional associations across different subspaces, ultimately leading to poor prediction performance. To address these challenges, we propose a novel tensorbased self-attention (TBSA) mechanism for better learning performance prediction in KT. We first propose TBSA, which captures both direct and indirect relationships among KCs. Then, we design tensor-based attention weights by utilizing tensor’s advantages to incorporate the multidimensional associations. Furthermore, we propose a TBSA-based KT model (i.e., TBKT) to enhance learning performance prediction. Finally, we conduct a series of experiments on four benchmark datasets to validate the effectiveness and innovation of the proposed TBKT. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that TBKT outperforms SOTA methods.

articleTitle: Policy-based Management of Human-Device and Device-Device Interactions in IoT Collectives: A Simulation-based Study
abstract: This paper examines a potential use-case of integrating human-device and device-device interactions in IoT collectives, specifically in a hospital setting. A simulation-based implementation was created and implemented in order to demonstrate how smart devices may behave in more human-centered ways by applying a set of policies from our proposed socio-ethical policy framework to their core functions. The implementation comprises Internet-connected robot(s) and multiple users. In order to minimise delays in job completion, the internet-connected robots cooperate with one another while they work. This enables each robot to carry out its duties successfully and with greater consideration for people. Robots are subject to a variety of rules, including those requiring them to avoid obstacles, make way for other robots, keep a safe distance, and more. This research has modeled complicated interactions, taking into account the implementation challenges of human-device and device-device interactions, and demonstrated, using a simulation-based implementation, the applicability of policy-based management of human-device and device interactions.

articleTitle: Multi-Stage Interaction and Multi-Scale Reconstruction: A Hybrid Attention Network for Skin Lesion Image Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesion areas is significant for the diagnosis and analysis of skin diseases. Due to the irregular and blurred boundaries between healthy skin and lesion areas and sometimes the interference of hair and pigmentation deposits, it is still a challenging task to accomplish accurate segmentation. To solve the above problems, a hybrid attention network (SISR-HANet) based on stage interaction and scale reconstruction is proposed. The network contains three main modules: The Multi-Scale Global Perception (MSGP) module perceives global features through multi-scale receptive fields, thus compensating for the lack of global contextual information. The Multi-Stage Spatial Reconstruction (MSSR) module utilizes the cross-mixing of features from different stages to adaptively generate feature masks corresponding to each stage for reconstructing the features in each stage, thus eliminating the semantic differences between feature maps at different scales. The Channel-Optimized Inter-Group Aggregation (COGA) module helps the model recover more detailed features during the up-sampling process by optimizing and regrouping the channel information. To evaluate the effectiveness of SISR-HANet, we conducted experimental validation on the public datasets ISIC2017, ISIC2018, and PH2. The experimental results show that the DSC scores of these datasets are improved by 1.58%, 1.53%, and 1.34%, respectively, compared with the suboptimal networks.

articleTitle: UAV-based Intelligent Information Systems on Winter Road Safety for Autonomous Vehicles
abstract: As autonomous vehicles continue to revolutionize transportation, addressing challenges posed by adverse weather conditions, particularly during winter, becomes paramount for ensuring safe and efficient operations. One of the most important aspects of a road safety inspection during adverse weather is when a limited lane width can reduce the capacity of the road and raise the risk of serious accidents involving autonomous vehicles. In this research, a method for improving driving challenges on roads in winter conditions, with a model that segments and estimates the width of the road from the perspectives of Uncrewed aerial vehicles and autonomous vehicles. The proposed approach in this article is needed to empower selfdriving cars with up-to-date and accurate insights, enhancing their adaptability and decision-making capabilities in winter landscapes.

articleTitle: Audio-Driven Talking Face Generation with Blink Embedding and Hash Grid Landmarks Encoding
abstract: Dynamic Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) have demonstrated impressive success in generating high-fidelity 3D models of talking portraits. Despite the progress in the rendering speed and generation quality, there are still challenges on accurately and efficiently capturing mouth movements in talking portraits. To tackle this challenge, we propose an automatic method based on blink embedding and hash grid landmarks encoding in this study, which can substantially enhance the fidelity of talking faces. Specifically, we leverage facial features encoded as conditional features and integrate audio features as residual terms into our model through a Dynamic Landmark Transformer. Furthermore, we employ neural radiance fields to model the entire face, resulting in a lifelike face representation. Experimental evaluations have demonstrated the superiority of our approach to existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: VRMAN: Variational Refined Multi-Head Attention Network for Intrusion Detection
abstract: With the continuous advancement of network technology, the complexity of network systems continues to increase, and at the same time they are also facing more security threats and risks. A well-designed intrusion detection method can significantly enhance network security. Over the past decade, various intrusion detection methods based on machine learning have been proposed. However, previous research typically relied on supervised learning, which requires high-quality data and labeling. The data collection and annotation are time-consuming and costly, particularly in industrial environments. Moreover, supervised learning models suffer from data imbalance and face challenges in real-world deployment, such as defending against unseen attacks. To address these challenges, we propose a semisupervised intrusion detection method named VRMAN. To alleviate data imbalance and noise interference, VRMAN first employs a prior estimation network. This network utilizes a small amount of labeled data as prior knowledge and integrates the computed prior anomaly scores into the loss function. Second, we introduce a variational attention network to capture potential intrusion features, showing better non-linear expression capabilities. Finally, an anomaly scoring network is trained to distinguish the anomaly scores between attacks and normal data. Experimental results show that VRMAN outperforms the state-of-the-art semisupervised intrusion detection methods, improving F1-scores by $\mathbf{3. 9 5 \%}, \mathbf{3. 3 9 \%}$, and $\mathbf{3. 2 9 \%}$ on three datasets respectively.

articleTitle: Enhancing AEB Systems with Digital Twin Evaluation in Urban Environments
abstract: Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB) systems are pivotal in preventing collisions. However, their effectiveness significantly diminishes in urban environments, where complex scenarios and adverse weather conditions complicate the estimation of distances to other road users and adaptation to variable road-tire friction coefficients. Therefore, it is critical to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the inaccuracies in distance and road condition estimations to enhance AEB performance. Traditional AEB testing methods, which involve reproducing critical traffic situations and altering road conditions, pose significant risks and challenges. To address these issues, our study introduces a digital twin-based evaluation methodology that replicates our test vehicle, complete with realistic driving dynamics and physical sensor models. Our testing protocols conform to the European New Car Assessment Programme (EU NCAP) standards for AEB Car-to-Pedestrian scenarios, with extensions to accommodate complex traffic and weather situations. Moreover, we adjust different roadway conditions from dry to icy in simulation. Our results determine the error tolerance and highlight the necessary precision for perception systems. Furthermore, our research illuminates the primary challenges associated with employing a digital twin in the development of autonomous driving functionalities and suggests possible implications.

articleTitle: Dynamic QoS Prediction for Edge Intelligence with Multi-Modal Data Fusion
abstract: Edge intelligence services encompass a wide range of offerings that often perform similar functions, making Quality of Service (QoS) a crucial factor for selecting and recommending the best services to users. QoS metrics can fluctuate over time due to varying network conditions and service demands, making dynamic QoS prediction essential for maintaining optimal user experiences. However, current dynamic QoS prediction methods are limited as they either extend static techniques without fully capturing temporal changes and considering contextual information, or rely on time series methods that fail to effectively represent hidden features. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel multi-view hybrid method for dynamic QoS prediction in edge intelligence services. This method integrates multi-modal data by capturing time-based dynamics with temporal dilated convolution, modeling contextual relationships with heterogeneous graph convolution, and uncovering latent feature interactions through temporal matrix factorization. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms several baseline techniques across multiple evaluation metrics, highlighting its effectiveness in dynamic edge intelligence environments.

articleTitle: Feature Rotation Invariance Learning for Point Cloud Analysis
abstract: While deep learning has significantly advanced point cloud analysis, extracting effective features from their disordered structure remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on complex network architectures or manual feature engineering to achieve rotation invariance, which increases inference latency. This paper offers a novel perspective on this challenge, showing that rotation-sensitive models can achieve performance comparable to rotation-invariant models when trained with rotation-augmented data. Given the significant differences in the feature distributions of rotation-sensitive and rotation-invariant models, we propose Feature Rotation Invariance Learning (FRIL), a framework that leverages Distance Metric Learning and rotation-based constraints to help rotation-sensitive models extract rotation-invariant features. This approach eliminates the need for additional modules, enabling robust performance against rotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FRIL consistently outperforms existing rotation-invariant methods across various visual tasks.

articleTitle: AcaPigeon: A Large Language Model-Based Academic Information Consultation Assistant
abstract: Academic Information Services are a crucial component of higher education, integral throughout the student’s learning journey. However, issues still persist regarding the convenience and intelligence of student information retrieval. To address these problems, we propose an academic information consultation assistant centered around a large language model, offering more convenient and intelligent services through natural language interaction. Specifically, we have designed a three-stage framework. Firstly, to identify the information sources to be retrieved, we utilize Few-Shot and other prompt engineering techniques with the large language model to analyze and annotate the queries. Secondly, based on the identified information sources, to enhance retrieval hit rates and thereby improve answer accuracy, different sources are equipped with customized retrievers suited to their unique characteristics. Lastly, we establish strict response standards, generating accurate answers through clear prompts and adhering to the principle of minimizing misleading information. Experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms baseline methods, with substantial improvements in hit rate and accuracy.

articleTitle: LLM-Enhanced Survival Model for Electric Device Lifespan Estimation
abstract: Scientific prediction of the lifespan of electrical equipment and the enhancement of refined management can facilitate the transformation and upgrading of power-related enterprises. In this paper, we conduct an enhanced survival analysis model based on Large Language Models (LLMs) for the lifespan estimation of electrical equipment. First, we employ association rule mining technology to extract key features. Subsequently, we introduce LLMs for deep optimization and feature selection to reduce data dimensionality and improve the accuracy of model predictions. Building on feature optimization, a survival analysis model is constructed, which defines survival functions and hazard functions to achieve precise prediction of the lifespan of electrical equipment. The final experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively improves the accuracy and robustness of lifespan estimation for electrical equipment, showing a significant enhancement in predictive performance compared to other methods on the dataset.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Anonymous Private Set Intersection Based on Obfuscation
abstract: As a key pre-step of vertical federated learning, private set intersection (PSI) technology finds the intersection of data from each participant without revealing their unique samples. However, the current PSI scheme incurs significant transmission costs, and participants can infer what data the other party possesses through the intersection set, violating anonymization requirements set by laws and regulations. To fill these gaps, we analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the existing PSI schemes based on the basic principles of different fundamental disciplines in the field of PSI research, and opt to construct a PSI scheme based on the oblivious transfer protocol and its extension, the oblivious pseudo random function. Subsequently, we improve the constructed scheme with cuckoo hash to address the transmission cost problem, reducing the complexity of communication transmission overhead from $O\left(n^{2}\right)$ to $O(n)$. Finally, in view of the lack of meeting the anonymization requirement in the field of PSI, we construct a bidirectional anonymization scheme by means of obfuscation expansion, and use the method of controlling variables to derive the effect of different variable variations on the final modeling accuracy through a large number of randomization experiments. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme can achieve bidirectional anonymous PSI while maintaining the performance of the federated model.

articleTitle: Integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enhanced Code Reuse: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Software Development
abstract: With the rapid development of ubiquitous computing, the demand for efficient software development is growing stronger. Code reuse is an effective means to enhance software development efficiency, significantly reducing the development cycle. Although existing large language models for code generation can assist developers in quickly writing code, they primarily aid in generating generic code and are unable to produce specific business code, making code reuse indispensable. In this paper, We propose a retrieval-augmented generation-based framework to streamline code reuse. This involves extracting reusable code units, generating natural language summaries, and matching queries with these summaries using search and reranking techniques. We conducted extensive experiments from both code search and code generation perspectives, the experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the efficiency and quality of code reuse.

articleTitle: Discovering Attacks against Smart Contracts Using Opcode Sequences with Feature Fusion
abstract: Smart contracts have revolutionized blockchain technology by enabling efficient, automated transactions without intermediaries. However, their increasing prevalence has made them attractive targets for malicious actors, highlighting the critical need for robust security measures. While significant efforts have focused on identifying vulnerabilities in smart contract bytecode before deployment, there still needs to be a substantial gap in detecting execution attacks post-deployment. This gap poses a severe risk to the integrity and security of blockchain transactions. To address this challenge, we introduce an innovative multi-dimensional feature fusion technique for detecting attacks during smart contract execution. Our method comprehensively analyzes opcode behavior across four key dimensions: target operation object, system resource utilization, category, and gas consumption. This multi-faceted approach allows for a more thorough and nuanced detection of potential threats. Our approach demonstrates exceptional performance, achieving a 97.21% detection accuracy and a 97.21% weighted F1-Score. These metrics indicate high precision and recall in identifying various potential attacks.

articleTitle: Generative AI-aided Reinforcement Learning for Computation Offloading and Privacy Protection in VR-based Multi-Access Edge Computing
abstract: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content (AIGC) services has led to increased mobile user participation in related computations and interactions. This development has enabled AI-generated characters to interact with Virtual Reality (VR) users in real time, making the VR experience more interactive and personalized. In this paper, we consider an MEC system where VR users engage in AIGC services, focusing on the Generative Diffusion Model (GDM)based image generation tasks. Specifically, VR users initiate requests for computing resources, while computation offloading distributes the processing load across the MEC system. To manage AIGC edge computation offloading and cloudlet-VR user connections jointly, a Data Center Operator (DCO) employs a centralized Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. To protect VR users’ privacy while preserving PPO functionality, we employ the Generative Diffusion Model (GDM), specifically the Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM), which first introduces noise to the PPO state, then conducts a denoising process to recover the state information. We further employ Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) to infer rewards for the recovered states, using expert demonstrations trained by the PPO. The similarity between PPO-generated rewards and IRL-inferred rewards is then computed. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed approach successfully achieves computation offloading while protecting VR users’ privacy within the PPO centralized management framework.

articleTitle: PointSaT: Structure-aware Transformer for Point Cloud Classification
abstract: As a basic task in point cloud analysis, classification is always challenging due to the irregularity and disorder of point clouds. Since the introduction of pointNet++, many point-based hierarchical networks have been proposed with excellent results. However, most of such networks use only point coordinates as geometric descriptions, and then go through multiple layers of sampling and learning in order to extract abstract and implicit structural features in high-dimensional space. To compensate for the lack of geometric information provided by coordinates, and to model the potential relationship between low-level structural channels and high-dimensional feature channels, we propose PointSaT. Specifically, we design the Explicit Structure Embedding Module (ESEM) to obtain explicit structural features of the original point cloud to complement the geometric cues. On the other hand, we propose the Structure-aware Transformer (SaT) module, which encodes and filters the channels of high-dimensional features to retain the channels faithful to the geometric space. Extensive experiments on ModelNet40 and ScanobjectNN datasets demonstrate the superiority and competitiveness of our network. The code of this paper is available at https://github.com/huangzhanhua02/PointSaT

articleTitle: OE-VI2: Occlusion Effect-based Narrow-Bandwidth In-Ear Voice Input Interface for Earphones
abstract: Nowadays, voice input on earphone sides has become one of the most paramount human-computer interaction approaches. However, airborne-channel input is noise-susceptible, decreasing the quality and intelligibility of input voice in noisy environments. In our work, we explore the feasibility of a noise-resistant but narrow-bandwidth in-ear channel as an alternative voice input interface. Although promising, directly taking the in-ear channel as voice input is non-trivial since the limited bandwidth of in-ear speech causes the timbre and content information to be lost. Thus, we propose $O E-V I^{2}$, an occlusion effect-based in-ear voice input interface for earphones. We utilize the Electro-Acoustic (EA) model to conduct an occlusion effectbased correlation analysis between two channels. Based on such cross-channel correlation, we design an encoder-decoder learning network to reconstruct wide-bandwidth speech from narrow-bandwidth in-ear speech. To maintain the individual timbre information, we design a one-shot timbre auxiliary subnetwork to extract timbre embeddings. Through extensive real-world experiments with 28 participants, $O E-V I^{2}$ can achieve an average MCD of 8.735, an average MSD of 0.893, and an average LSD of 11.956, outperforming existing solutions. $O E-V I^{2}$ is available on Project Website.

articleTitle: Causality-Aware Next Location Prediction Framework based on Human Mobility Stratification
abstract: Human mobility data are fused with multiple travel patterns and hidden spatiotemporal patterns are extracted by integrating user, location, and time information to improve next location prediction accuracy. In existing next location prediction methods, different causal relationships that result from patterns in human mobility data are ignored, which leads to confounding information that can have a negative effect on predictions. Therefore, this study introduces a causality-aware framework for next location prediction, focusing on human mobility stratification for travel patterns. In our research, a novel causal graph is developed that describes the relationships between various input variables. We use counterfactuals to enhance the indirect effects in our causal graph for specific travel patterns: non-anchor targeted travels. The proposed framework is designed as a plug-andplay module that integrates multiple next location prediction paradigms. We tested our proposed framework using several state-of-the-art models and human mobility datasets, and the results reveal that the proposed module improves the prediction performance. In addition, we provide results from the ablation study and quantitative study to demonstrate the soundness of our causal graph and its ability to further enhance the interpretability of the current next location prediction models.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Personality Detection Method With Behavioral Action Feature and Association Features *
abstract: Multimodal personality detecting aims to identify human personality traits from videos in computer vision. Existing methods mine different modal features separately and fuse them for the Big Five personality detection task, neglecting the mining of multimodal correlation features and behavioral action characteristics. Therefore, we propose a novel multimodal feature learning method for analyzing the personality traits of individuals in short videos. Firstly, we design an Image-Audio Association Feature extraction method (IAAF) to capture the correlation features between images and audio. This method utilizes existing pre-trained models to separately mine image and audio features and calculates the dot product between the two modal features as the association feature. Considering the role of behavioral action features in personality prediction tasks, we utilize pre-trained 3D-ResNet34 as a feature extractor to mine this feature. Meanwhile, We use CLIP to extract the image-personality descriptions feature between images and personality descriptors. This paper uses a pre-trained Roberta to extract text features to enhance the method’s robustness. Finally, the proposed method is tested on two benchmark datasets, and it outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Double-RIS aided Full-Duplex communication system: uplink, downlink and rate maximization
abstract: To explore the full potential and application of intelligent reflective surfaces (RISs) in complex and highly specialized communication environments, this paper investigates a system architecture composed of cascaded double-RISs. The system is further enhanced by the integration of advanced full-duplex (FD) communication and multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) technologies, forming a highly robust and adaptive framework. The key objective of this study is to maximize the sum achievable rate of the system (SARS) by jointly optimizing the proposed system constraints and the phase-shift control of the cascaded double-RISs. Considering the inherent complexity and high-dimensional nature of the optimization problem, we propose an iterative optimization algorithm. This algorithm is grounded in advanced mathematical techniques, specifically leveraging fractional programming (FP) to iteratively refine the objective, and Maximize-Minimize (MM) methods to ensure a balanced and globally optimized solution. Through rigorous simulation results, we demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly enhances the system’s overall performance. When compared to conventional techniques, the new approach exhibits marked improvements in system efficiency, data throughput, and overall robustness, thus indicating its superior efficacy in real-world applications over existing methodologies. These results highlight the practical advantages of applying double-RIS and FD-MIMO technology in modern wireless networks, making this a promising solution for next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: An Approach to New Bearing Fault Diagnosis Utilizing Deep Transfer Learning
abstract: Bearings, serving as crucial components in mechanical equipment, exert a direct influence on the overall performance of the system. Deep transfer learning has garnered significant attention in the realm of intelligent fault diagnosis for machines. Nevertheless, extant deep transfer learning algorithms encounter challenges when detecting newly emerging faults within the target domain. To address this limitation, this study introduces a novel bearing fault diagnosis approach for newly emerging faults, leveraging deep transfer learning principles. Initially, a multi-grained hierarchical feature extraction network is constructed to effectively capture intricate data characteristics. Subsequently, these extracted features are employed to train a fault classifier, thereby establishing a fault diagnosis network grounded in deep transfer learning. This network is capable of discriminating unlabeled new faults from labeled known faults with remarkable precision. Furthermore, an adaptive hierarchical clustering algorithm, informed by the elbow method, is incorporated to categorize the newly emerging faults. The clustered samples are then utilized to train the online sequential extreme learning machine (OS-ELM), facilitating the construction of a new fault diagnosis network tailored for diagnosing these faults in the target domain. The efficacy of the proposed methodology was rigorously verified through experiments executed on both the CWRU and XJTU-SY datasets. The outcomes conclusively demonstrated an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8. 7 5 \%}$ on the CWRU dataset and $\mathbf{9 7. 9 2 \%}$ on the XJTU-SY dataset. This model portends immense potential in tackling fault diagnosis transfer scenarios characterized by the emergence of multiple novel faults within the target domain, thereby markedly broadening the applicability of deep transfer learning.

articleTitle: CoDSDF: Constrained Decoding of SDF Quantized Vectors for Single-View 3D Reconstruction Using Conditional Generation
abstract: The Virtual Reality faces a shortage of personalized 3D resources, posing a challenge in easily extracting real-world objects and converting them into editable 3D shape meshes. Single-view reconstruction, which transforms easily accessible information such as a single image into specified 3D shapes, can be regarded as a unique conditional generation task. This paper proposes the CoDSDF network, which can generate high-quality detail-rich 3D mesh for multiple categories. We quantize 3D SDF shapes into a combination of low-dimensional discrete feature vectors and then model the distribution of these combinations, which are stored in the codebook, to associate them with image information as target conditional inputs for the generator.The CoDSDF incorporates SDF quantized vector decoding to retain more details in the generated. Additionally, a conditional encoding network built with Split-Attention combines more global and local features to predict the necessary conditional distribution inputs based on the image, guiding the generator to achieve precise reconstruction. CoDSDF captures more 3D structural details, such as holes, from a single image, demonstrating excellent single-view reconstruction results across 13 categories, including chairs, airplanes, and sofas. The generated data can be converted into point cloud meshes and integrated into digital media workflows.

articleTitle: EDNet: Edge-Optimized Small Target Detection in UAV Imagery - Faster Context Attention, Better Feature Fusion, and Hardware Acceleration

authors.preferredName: Abd Al Rahman M. Abu Ebayyeh

abstract: Detecting small targets in drone imagery is challenging due to low resolution, complex backgrounds, and dynamic scenes. We propose EDNet, a novel edge-target detection framework built on an enhanced YOLOv10 architecture, optimized for real-time applications without post-processing. EDNet incorporates an XSmall detection head and a Cross Concat strategy to improve feature integration and multi-scale context awareness, critical for detecting tiny targets in diverse environments. Our unique C2f-FCA block employs Faster Context Attention to enhance feature extraction while minimizing computational complexity. The WIoU loss function is employed for improved bounding box regression. With seven model sizes ranging from Tiny to XL, EDNet accommodates various deployment environments, enabling local real-time inference and ensuring data privacy. Notably, EDNet achieves up to a 5.6% gain in mAP@50 with significantly fewer parameters, as depicted in Fig. 1. On an iPhone 12, EDNet variants operate at speeds ranging from 16 to 55 FPS, providing a scalable and efficient solution for edge-based object detection in challenging drone imagery.

articleTitle: Revisiting Adversarial Attacks on Deep Neural Networks via Correlating Adaptive Gradient-based Features
abstract: Existing works proved that Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to artificial adversarial features, which pose challenges in the application of DNNs in security-sensitive scenarios. Exploring adversarial strategies benefits developing identical adversarial defenses that robust DNNs in security-sensitive challenges. From an adversary perspective, finding the adversarial properties with considerable adversarial capability is an optimization problem in feature generation. However, existing attacks focused on improving the adversarial performance of crafted features while ignoring the optimization of perturbation strength, which induces noticeable modifications in adversarial features. To generate adversarial features with profound capability in invading deep neural task models while preserving balanced perturbation magnitude, we introduce a simple yet flexible manner: Adaptive Gradient-based Feature Correlated Method (AFCM) that calls a few adaptive operators on original distributions and correlates such crafted gradient-based features in adaptive similarity-based constraints, which benefits from escaping from the local optimum while searching decision boundaries in adversarial processing. Extensive experiments reveal that adversarial features generated by AFCM acquire surpassing effectiveness in fooling deep neural networks while preserving fewer pixel changes on $\ell_{\infty}$ and $\ell_{2}$ norm constraints with perfect generalization and transferability.

articleTitle: ECG-DPM: Electrocardiogram Generation via a Spectrogram-based Diffusion Probabilistic Model
abstract: An electrocardiogram (ECG) records the electrical signals from the heart to assess various cardiovascular conditions. Deep learning methods have been proposed to model ECGs, but the insufficient availability of ECG data and annotations often hinders their performance. To address this challenge, this paper explores the latest data synthesis technique, i.e., diffusion probabilistic models (DPMs), to enable the generation of an unlimited number of ECGs representing various cardiovascular conditions. In contrast to previous approaches that treat ECGs as time series data or convert them into power spectrograms, we introduce a novel multi-channel spectrogram-based diffusion framework. In our method, the diffusion model enhances generation diversity, while the multi-channel spectrogram preserves both magnitude and phase information, ensuring high fidelity in the reconstructed ECGs. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world ECG data demonstrate the superiority of our approach. Notably, our ECG-DPM outperforms the best baseline by a margin ranging from ${1 2. 5 \%}$ to ${6 2. 5 \%}$ when generating ECGs for 30 seconds.

articleTitle: Intelligent Architecture for Multi-Domain Aerial-Surface-Underwater Networks with Hybrid Radio-Acoustic-Optical Communications
abstract: Multi-domain aerial-surface-underwater networks are increasingly critical in applications such as maritime surveillance and rescue. However, due to environmental and technical constraints, traditional communication methods alone are often insufficient, particularly in cross-domain and underwater-domain communication scenarios. Currently, there is very limited research on aerial-surface-underwater communication networks.
