To address the challenge of seamlessly integrating these diverse domains, this paper proposes an intelligent architecture that optimizes communication network across aerial, surface, and underwater domains with hybrid radio-acoustic-optical communications by leveraging the complementary strengths of different communication technologies. The proposed architecture comprises three layers, in intelligence layer, integrated resource management model, dynamic routing decision model and adaptive service-rate sensing model. To evaluate the performance, this paper conducts case studies in different hybrid multi-domain network scenarios through simulation and experiment. It can be concluded that the proposed intelligent architecture could effectively integrate hybrid radio-acoustic-optical communication technologies with complementary strengths and enhance efficiency and robustness of multi-domain aerial-surface-underwater communication network. This research provides an innovative framework for advancing the development of multi-domain networks with hybrid communication technologies.

articleTitle: A Maturity Model for Digital Twin Integration of Mobile Robotics
abstract: Mobile robots are increasingly present in the world around us. Simultaneously, our living, work, and play spaces are becoming more intelligent through the integration of sensor networks giving rise to digital twins. Digital twins primarily interact with the physical world through actuators and sensors, yet most of our spaces were not designed for this. By integrating mobile robots with their corresponding digital twin, we can bridge this integration gap, but unfortunately, not all mobile robots are created equal. Thus, a tool is needed to assess the suitability of these platforms for their strategic integration into digital twin solutions. However, existing maturity models for digital twins and mobile robotic platforms do not provide sufficient insight. This work takes an initial step towards developing such a tool in the form of a maturity model and applies it to two mobile robots, the Spot and Bittle platforms.

articleTitle: UWBOri: Enabling Accurate Orientation Estimation with Ultra-wideband Signals
abstract: The development of smart devices has highlighted the need for human-device interaction. A key aspect of this interaction lies in the estimation of the physical orientation of the device, which is crucial for various applications. Conventional methods employing Inertial Measurement Units (IMU) encounter limitations such as cumulative errors and magnetic interference. In this paper, we propose UWBOri, a novel method for orientation estimation using Ultra-wideband (UWB) technology. UWB technology, which is increasingly integrated into smart devices, offers superior ranging accuracy owing to its large bandwidth. By leveraging the localization information obtained between a fixed UWB-equipped anchor device and the user device, UWBOri can accurately estimate the orientation of the user device. The efficacy of UWBOri has been validated through extensive laboratory experiments designed to evaluate the accuracy of orientation estimation. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical applicability of UWBOri in two distinct scenarios: IoT device selection and augmented reality (AR). These applications illustrate the potential of our solution in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Real-time Fine-grained Gesture Recognition Based on Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: Fine-grained gesture activity recognition holds broad application prospects in smart education, assisted driving, and other fields, especially in non-contact, high-precision gesture-human interaction. Existing methods for real-time gesture recognition often require cumbersome gesture collection and operate in offline mode, not fully addressing practical issues such as gesture segmentation and recognition latency. To address these challenges, an Awa-GNN is proposed to handle sparse point cloud data and extract universal features, eliminating the need for additional collection and training, thus mitigating personalized differences among users. Moreover, by integrating bi-directional gated recurrent units (Bi-GRU) based on convolutional attention, temporal features are extracted to achieve efficient gesture recognition. Experiments demonstrate that Awa-GNN outperforms other baselines in terms of generalization and recognition accuracy on the MMGesture dataset and self-collected datasets. To validate the effectiveness of Awa-GNN, a real-time gesture recognition system named P-Gesture is constructed. The system uses a sliding window mechanism based on the state machine (SM) for automatic gesture segmentation and is deployed on the IWR1642 radar. Additionally, an end-to-end real-time application based on P-Gesture has been developed.

articleTitle: Multi-view session-based social recommendation with self-supervised learning
abstract: Session-based social recommendation (SSR) is an important branch of session-based recommendation that aims to generate more accurate recommendations by combining users’ historical sessions with their social information. Existing SSR models are usually based on graph neural networks. Although they have shown better performance compared to traditional SSR models, they ignored users’ temporal behavior patterns and data sparsity issues. Therefore, we propose a multi-view SSR model MVSSR that effectively constructs multiple views to model the temporal and global user preferences in sparse SSR scenarios. On one hand, we construct user data into multiple views to thoroughly capture users’ temporal preferences and global preferences. On the other hand, we constructed a view-aware self-supervised learning method. Through self-supervised learning within and between views, we enhance the user’s session representation to alleviate the data sparsity is-sues in SSR. We performed ex-tensive experiments on three real-world datasets to confirm the effectiveness of MVSSR. The results indicate that our model surpasses the current state-of-the-art models in terms of hit rate and mean reciprocal rank.

articleTitle: Meta-path and Meta-schema Hierarchical Aggregation for Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
abstract: With deep learning’s advancement in recent years, heterogeneous graph neural networks (HGNNs) have drawn a lot of interest. They are a group of deep learning models specifically designed for handling heterogeneous graph data, in which nodes and edges are of various types and all nodes are assumed to have either direct or indirect associations. A metaschema, which serves as a thorough and unified blueprint for the heterogeneous graph, elegantly connects varied node types to other heterogeneous nodes via multiple heterogeneous edges with rich sematincs. However, many existing methods that utilize meta-schema to mine heterogeneous information often focus on the different meta-relationships inside the schema, limiting the meta-schema to describing only the local relational semantics. To better utilize meta-schema for efficiently integrating different heterogeneous information, we organize them into a hierarchical structure(i.e., hierarchical meta-schema), with all types of nodes distributed across different layers. The layers are interconnected through heterogeneous relationships. The target type is placed at the final layer and others are arranged hierarchically in the front according to the heterogeneous relationships defined in the meta-schema. During information aggregation, according to the hierarchical meta-schema, the information of each layer is gradually aggregated to the target type on the final layer from far to near via the attention mechanism. Moreover, metapaths regularly begin and end with the same type and help to define complex structures and semantic. Therefore, we also consider the semantic information of neighbors based on metapaths within the proposed hierarchical meta-schema to enhance the complex semantics among nodes of the same-type that may be lacking in the meta-schema. Finally, we proposed a meta-path and meta-schema hierarchical aggregation for heterogeneous graph neural network model, named HGNN-MMHA. And we may allow the meta-schema to not be limitted to the metarelationship information in it, and maximize consideration of the correlations among different types of nodes in the heterogeneous graph. Extensive experiments on four real heterogeneous graph datasets show the effectiveness of the proposed HGNN-MMHA in comparison to state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: An Intrusion Detection Method for Automotive Ethernet Networks Based on Time Series Prediction and Rule Setting
abstract: Nowadays, intelligent and connected vehicles (ICVs) have rapid development, and their cyber security problems have become increasingly significant. The cyber-attacks on ICVs directly threaten the property, privacy and even personal safety of drivers and passengers. Most existing intrusion detection methods are primarily designed for CAN bus, with relatively little research focused on automotive Ethernet. This paper takes SOME/IP as an example and focuses on attack detection in automotive Ethernet. An intrusion detection method combining time series prediction and rule-based approaches is proposed. An in-vehicle network traffic prediction model that combines CNN-BiLSTM with attention mechanisms is utilized to learn the temporal characteristics of data packets in automotive Ethernet. The cosine similarity between real messages and predicted results is utilized as a rule to identify attacks. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Clustering Algorithms with Balanced Weights for Geographic Data Processing
abstract: With the rapid growth of geographic data, generated by various sensors and end equipment, new opportunities for research and practical applications can be found in various applications. However, effective utilization of this data often requires the division of geospatial space into smaller, manageable regions. An important challenge is to ensure that these regions with closed data points are balanced in terms of data size distribution (e.g., population density, resource allocation, etc.), creating a double optimization problem. The contributions of this paper are twofold. First, we propose a balance-driven partitioning algorithm, which is a coordinate-descent based algorithm using a dynamic programming technique. Second, we present a clustering-centric algorithm that improves the classic k-means algorithm with an imbalance-penalized function to allow the geographic data to be clustered together not only in terms of geographic location, but also in terms of the per-cluster total sizes in balance. Finally, to evaluate the efficiency of the proposed algorithms, we conducted experiments based on a trace geographic dataset and compared the results with those of the existing clustering algorithms. Our results demonstrate that the proposed algorithms can not only achieve the competitive clustering effects but also exhibit better performance in terms of data-size balance.

articleTitle: Task Offloading Scheme based on PTSS-DQN Algorithm for Latency Optimization in Multi-User and Multitasking Environments
abstract: Edge computing is gaining widespread attention, particularly in the domain of task offloading. Efficiently and accurately offloading tasks to edge servers presents a significant challenge due to its complexity. In this paper, we depart from the traditional user-to-edge offloading scenario and instead focus on a model where users offload tasks to base stations. These base stations, equipped with servers and possessing an extended communication range, centrally manage all tasks. A base station can either offload tasks to a specific edge server within its communication range or handle them locally. To address the scheduling challenge among multiple tasks, we propose a priority-based Time Slice Scheduling (PTSS) algorithm to calculate task processing latency. Additionally, we introduce the PTSS-DQN algorithm by integrating the Deep Q-Network (DQN) to jointly optimize the offloading strategy, resource allocation, time-slice distribution, and task execution order. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach.

articleTitle: EFLSS: An Efficient Federated Learning Security Scheme in Byzantine Attack Scenarios
abstract: Federated Learning (FL), a distributed machine learning approach, aims to protect user privacy by performing model training without centralized data collection. However, FL systems are susceptible to malicious participants uploading incorrect or harmful updates in the face of Byzantine Attacks, leading to model performance degradation or even failure. To address this problem, this paper proposes a new approach that combines an confusion factor and a parameter screening mechanism to securely and efficiently counter Byzantine Attacks. Local gradients are added with confusion factors before uploading to protect the security of local data. In addtion, we propose an improved anomaly detection algorithm that can identify and filter Byzantine nodes during the gradient aggregation phase to ensure the accuracy of the global model. Experimental results show that compared with the traditional FL mechanism, the global model obtained in this scheme has higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Children and Dogs Classification in CPD Application
abstract: In recent years, incidents of children or dogs being left in vehicles and subsequently dying have garnered significant attention from both the public and regulatory bodies. Due to the varying nature of rescue methods, environmental conditions, and other factors, accurately identifying children and dogs is a crucial component of Child Presence Detection (CPD) in vehicle cabins. This paper employs frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar to extract features through respiration detection and motion detection, and utilizes machine learning models to distinguish between children and dogs, thereby enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the detection system. The proposed methodology combines respiratory and motion features to achieve precise differentiation between children and dogs, which is crucial for appropriate safety responses, health interventions, and legal actions.

articleTitle: Human-Machine Task Allocation Based on Predicate Confidence and Dynamic Cost
abstract: Machine learning (ML) models are increasingly being used in application domains that often involve working together with human experts. Effective task allocation between humans and machines is crucial for optimizing performance and maximizing overall efficiency. We propose a novel human-machine task allocation method based on predictive confidence and dynamic cost, aiming to reduce human and machine costs without compromising task accuracy. We first define the task allocation problem, which considers the confidence of humans and machines, the cost of human and machine, as well as task rewards. Our method breaks through the limitations of traditional approaches that assign tasks to single executors only. Instead, it dynamically allocates tasks to human, machine, or both in collaboration to maximize the total expected reward. We have developed an integrated framework that includes key modules such as cost calculation, task allocation, and result fusion. This framework allows us to flexibly determine the task executors based on the specific conditions of each task. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the total expected reward compared to multiple baseline schemes, while ensuring task accuracy. Specifically, the proposed method achieves an 8 -fold increase in total expected reward on the CIFAR-10H dataset and approximately a 3-fold increase on the ImageNet-16H dataset.

articleTitle: A Speech Dataset for the Recognition and Analysis of COVID-19 Coughs
abstract: The coronavirus and its variants have spread globally, and since the virus primarily transmits through the air, efficient and convenient self-testing methods have become crucial for controlling the pandemic. Current COVID-19 detection technologies generally rely on data-intensive deep learning frameworks; however, the scarcity of COVID-19 cough voice samples has been a major barrier to advancement in this field. To address this challenge, this study innovatively constructed a specialized dataset comprising 3,395 audio recordings, covering three core categories: COVID-19 coughs, non-COVID-19 coughs, and healthy breathing sounds, ensuring data comprehensiveness and specificity. To further explore the deep features of sound signals, we employed four cutting-edge signal processing techniques—Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), and Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT)—to extract the spectral and time-frequency characteristics of the sounds, generating four sets of feature-rich images. Based on this, we selected 12 state-of-the-art classification models and conducted a comprehensive experimental process to establish a performance benchmark. The experimental results demonstrated that most models exhibited excellent recognition accuracy on our dataset, confirming both the high quality of the dataset and the effectiveness of the models.

articleTitle: Topology-aware Visualization for Interactive Graph Structure Exploration
abstract: Structural analysis of graphs can reveal significant connectivity patterns in areas of sociology, biology, etc. However, discovering specific pattern types is complex and time consuming. Besides, users can hardly recognize them via visual clues. In this paper, we propose a supervised dual-task model to predict the topological category of the graph, i.e., whether it approximates egocentric, grid, and clique patterns. Meanwhile, the model generates drawings that reflect the characteristics of these patterns to enhance user cognition. It is robust to local changes due to the training on a human-manipulated dataset of graph variants. Additionally, to simplify the visualization of graphs, we conduct iterative division to obtain hierarchical clusters and visually map them to uncertainty-encoded nodes. At each level of granularity, topology-adaptive visualization is implemented to the coarsened graph and users can interactively explore graph connectivity in a top-down manner by expanding/folding the node of interest. To prove the effectiveness of our method, case studies were conducted on both synthetic and real-world datasets. The results show that our method not only helps users to understand the graph connectivity and query for similar patterns efficiently but also achieves high scalability for large graph visualization.

articleTitle: AMMFNet: An Attention-Based Multimodal Multiscale Fusion Framework for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning-based methods provide a non-invasive, efficient, and convenient approach for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, most deep learning approaches concentrate on single-modal data, leading to instability in capturing disease traits and neglecting the multimodal aspects essential for accurate medical diagnosis in Alzheimer’s disease. Secondly, current multimodal methods exhibit relatively independent feature extraction processes for each modality and lack low-level feature interactions, thus limiting the expressive power of the features, thereby affecting the model’s performance. Furthermore, contemporary research on multimodality often employs a single scale to model brain features, hindering the adequate perception of local disease information within the brain. To overcome these challenges, we introduce a Multimodal Fusion Model with Attention (MFMA) for diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease. This framework utilizes a self-attention mechanism to merge the global features of both imaging modalities within their respective feature extraction pathways. By doing so, it facilitates a thorough multiscale integration of features from both imaging modalities, while also incorporating clinical indicator data from the patient to arrive at a final diagnosis. Experiments on the ADNI dataset demonstrate that the proposed method is highly competitive compared to current approaches.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning With Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem
abstract: Job Shop Scheduling Problem (JSP) is common in modern factories, but traditional dispatching rules (DR) and heuristic algorithms (HA) struggle with the increasing complexity of manufacturing processes. In this paper, we review research on the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) and propose a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) approach to address it. Unlike conventional methods, we represent the FJSP using a heterogeneous graph (HG) instead of a disjunctive graph (DG), allowing a Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (HGNN) to effectively extract comprehensive node information. We model the problem as a Markov Decision Process [30] (MDP) and employ an enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm for model training. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms some DRs and DRL method in terms of solution quality across generated small, medium, and large-scale datasets, as well as classic public benchmarks, all within an acceptable time frame. Additionally, it demonstrates significantly greater solution efficiency than advanced HA while maintaining similar solution quality, exhibiting strong stability and generalization capabilities.

articleTitle: SSL-DDS: Integrating SSL Encryption into DDS Communication Framework for UAV Security
abstract: The rapid advancement of unmanned systems technology has led to significant improvements in drone applications, emphasizing the urgent need for advanced communication security solutions. This paper introduces SSL-DDS, a novel UAV security method that integrates SSL encryption negotiation into the DDS framework. This innovative approach effectively addresses key challenges in authentication, key exchange, and encryption. By enabling flexible selection of encryption suites, SSL-DDS enhances compatibility across various UAV models and system architectures. It supports efficient multi-brand UAV authentication and ensures secure communication by selecting the most suitable encryption algorithms based on specific system configurations. This method provides effective and lightweight security solutions, optimizing performance for diverse hardware setups. Designed to maintain high security and reliable performance, SSL-DDS offers a comprehensive solution for modern UAV communication security, even in resource-constrained environments.

articleTitle: RGB-D Mirror Segmentation via Semi-supervised Learning
abstract: Mirror segmentation is challenging due to special reflection, which creates virtual scene intertwined with the real ones. Recently, deep learning models combining RGB and depth images have demonstrated impressive segmentation performance. However, fully supervised paradigm heavily depends on laborintensive annotation. In the paper, we propose a semi-supervised RGB-D mirror segmentation method for the first time, alleviating $\mathbf{9 3. 7 5 \%}$ of the annotation burden. In the model structure aspect, an innovative feature exchange is designed in the modal-specific decoding, which indirectly achieving the modality alignment for RGB-D multi-modal application. In the semi-supervised strategy aspect, a FlipCutMix augmentation is proposed to increase the data diversity by simulating the properties of mirror symmetry and depth discontinuity. Experiments show our semi-supervised performance with $\mathbf{1 / 1 6}$ annotation has surpassed the state-of-the-art fully-supervised ones, verifying the effectiveness of our model design and supervision paradigm for mirror segmentation. https://github.com/liuzywen/SemiMirror

articleTitle: FedAH: Aggregated Head for Personalized Federated Learning
abstract: Recently, Federated Learning (FL) has gained popularity for its privacy-preserving and collaborative learning capabilities. Personalized Federated Learning (PFL), building upon FL, aims to address the issue of statistical heterogeneity and achieve personalization. Personalized-head-based PFL is a common and effective PFL method that splits the model into a feature extractor and a head, where the feature extractor is collaboratively trained and shared, while the head is locally trained and not shared. However, retaining the head locally, although achieving personalization, prevents the model from learning global knowledge in the head, thus affecting the performance of the personalized model. To solve this problem, we propose a novel PFL method called Federated Learning with Aggregated Head (FedAH), which initializes the head with an Aggregated Head at each iteration. The key feature of FedAH is to perform element-level aggregation between the local model head and the global model head to introduce global information from the global model head. To evaluate the effectiveness of FedAH, we conduct extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets in the fields of computer vision and natural language processing. FedAH outperforms ten state-of-the-art FL methods in terms of test accuracy by 2.87%. Additionally, FedAH maintains its advantage even in scenarios where some clients drop out unexpectedly. Our code is open-accessed at https://github.com/heyuepeng/FedAH.

articleTitle: Digital Twin: Graph Formulations for Managing Complexity and Uncertainty
abstract: This paper articulates the importance of graphical models and graph-based methods as fundamental enablers of Digital Twins. Graph-based representations are well known to be suited for describing complex systems where the connections between entities are as important as the entities themselves. The interconnections within and across data, models, and decisions are central to a Digital Twin’s value. Not only does a graph emphasize the scalable representation of such interrelationships, it also provides a natural mathematical setting for addressing uncertainty and complexity—arguably the two biggest barriers to scalable deployment and adoption of Digital Twins. We discuss how recent advances in theory and algorithms for large-scale knowledge graphs and graphical models can be combined in a multi-layered formulation to provide a powerful foundation for achieving scalable Digital Twins for complex systems.

articleTitle: A Blockchain-Based Hierarchical Dynamic Collaborative Storage Model
abstract: The pervasive application of blockchain technology has led to a significant increase in data volume, presenting significant challenges to existing storage architectures in environments characterized by large volumes of data and highfrequency transactions. To enhance the scalability of blockchain, this study introduces an innovative framework, Hierarchical Dynamic Storage Management Chain Model, named HDSMC. The model consists of two stages. In the first phase of the model, when multimodal data files are uploaded, LBA techniques are employed to securely eliminate unnecessary redundancy, effectively preventing the storage of duplicate data. In the second phase, further processing is conducted on the generated blocks. This involves analyzing the frequency of block access to compute the variation in block “heat”. Based on the Block Heat (BH), the number of replicas for each block across participating nodes is then determined. Furthermore, the framework implements an adaptive tiering strategy based on data access frequency and its importance, which facilitates the timely migration of data to an appropriate storage level. A simulated Hyperledger Fabric environment was employed to deploy the HDSMC framework and to assess its performance against current storage methodologies. The empirical outcomes indicated that this approach could achieve lower storage expenditures while ensuring high reliability. This research not only presents a novel strategy for blockchain storage management but also suggests potential applications for storage optimization in other big data scenarios.

articleTitle: Assessing Perceived Factors and Effects of Mobile Phone Health Software on Users’ Health Behavior
abstract: Smartphone health applications assist users in building health awareness by collecting, storing, analyzing, and sharing daily physical activity data. The key lies in translating health data and knowledge into actual behavior. This study targets users of mobile health applications, employing a questionnaire survey method and using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to validate a user health information perception model. It evaluates the impact of information visualization and human-computer interaction, information quality and credibility, social interaction and decision support on health behavior intentions and actions. The study reveals that perceived factors of mobile health apps significantly enhance health awareness and self-motivation. The design focus should be on self-management of data and behavior control, with crucial perceived factors including ease of information retrieval, perceived usefulness, and intelligent personalized suggestions. Optimizing the data management experience and functional design can promote health awareness and positive behavior change.

articleTitle: STLL: Spatio-Temporal Graph and Lane Sequence Based Lightweight Vehicle Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Accurate and swift prediction of surrounding vehicle trajectories is essential for autonomous driving. Currently, numerous methods have achieved excellent accuracy in trajectory prediction but they often overlook the prediction speed. Autonomous vehicles must quickly respond to various situations for safe driving. Therefore, we propose a lightweight model named STLL. We model the interactions among vehicles using a graph that fully considers the spatio-temporal information. Additionally, we represent all lanes by a sequence and employ an efficient method to encode lanes. These approaches effectively enable the model to extract and fuse features of vehicles and lanes, leading to accurate and swift trajectory predictions. We conduct our experiments on the widely recognized real-world trajectory prediction datasets: nuScenes and Argoverse. The results demonstrate that our method not only significantly reduces prediction time and the number of model parameters but also maintains high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: AG-HCRL: Air-Ground Collaborative Crowdsensing Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning in City Sensing
abstract: The rapid development of unmanned technology has brought new opportunities for mobile sensing in different fields. Naturally, traditional mobile crowdsensing (MCS) based on mobile device users and unmanned vehicle sensing (UVS) based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) are especially complementary when performing sensing tasks. To further improve the intelligence in city sensing tasks, we propose an air-ground collaborative crowdsourcing framework based on deep reinforcement learning, called AG-HCRL, which is a heterogeneous crowdsensing design leveraging both manpower and unmanned vehicles (including aerial and ground). The proposed AG-HCRL framework models the different characteristics of MCS as well as UVS, achieving high-quality city sensing in a cost-effective way. A series of extensive evaluations based on simulations confirm the validity and superiority of AG-HCRL in simulated city sensing.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Real-Time Gait Event Detection Method Using Wearable Inertial Sensors
abstract: Gait analysis based on sensors integrated into wearable devices has become an emerging research field with the development of miniaturized sensors and the wide application of wearable devices. Accurate gait event detection is essential for clinical gait analysis. It is also the basis of gait phase division, which is of great importance for gait abnormality diagnosis, rehabilitation evaluation, professional running guidance, etc. This study aimed to propose a lightweight inertial sensor-based real-time gait event detection method. First, an improved method to enhance the plantar pressure-based gait event detection’s robustness was proposed, providing a reference standard for gait event detection. Then, significant signal features corresponding to each gait event were found on the angular velocity signals and were studied by mapping the specific gait events on the angular velocity signals. Four gait events could be accurately detected by the proposed significant feature detection method. The method was evaluated on a dataset collected from 15 participants (including 9 healthy individuals and 6 recovering patients). The results demonstrated high accuracy, with mean absolute error (MAE) of 12.1, 19.6, 18.7, and 11.7 ms for the heel-strike, foot-flat, heel-off, and toe-off events, respectively. These findings suggested that the proposed method was effective for detecting gait events.

articleTitle: ID-YOLOv7: A Method for Steel Surface Defect Detection Combining Residual Attention and Dynamic Upsampling
abstract: Industrial defect detection is a crucial challenge in computer vision. The accuracy of detecting defects on steel surfaces is hindered by spatially varying noise. To address this challenge, we propose an efficient method for steel surface defect detection. Firstly, considering the impact of the shape and proportions of bounding boxes on localization accuracy, we developed an Adaptive Shape-Inner Intersection over Union (ASIIoU) loss function. This function dynamically adjusts auxiliary bounding boxes and takes into account their shape and scale to optimize the loss, thereby improving the accuracy of bounding box regression loss. Secondly, to enhance the ability of the model to learn local features, we designed a Content-Guided Residual Attention Block (CGRAB). It captures rich local features across different convolutional layers via skip connections while discarding irrelevant information. Lastly, to avoid the potential issue of detail blurring caused by traditional upsampling methods, we optimized the upsampling process to preserve key details and structural information in the image, reducing unnecessary noise amplification. Experimental validation demonstrates the effectiveness of our method, which achieved a $76.7 \% \mathrm{mAP}$ on the NEU-DET dataset.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Fusion and 1D-CNN Based Elderly Fall Risk Prediction during Treadmill Walking
abstract: In today’s society, there has been an increase in the number of accidents among the elderly (60 and over) in places such as health clubs, where the main cause of accidents is due to the loss of balance on treadmills. However, traditional solutions are inefficient while consuming human resources and lagging in their inability to predict effectively and prevent upcoming accidents. A user-friendly system that can detect the movement status of the elderly in real-time and predict and alarm the fall risk is needed. Therefore, to protect the safety of the elderly when using the treadmill, in this paper we design a set of elderly exercise experiments at an elderly welfare center in Japan and propose a multi-modal fusion and 1D-CNN based elderly fall risk prediction system to integrate the short-term (e.g., skeletal features and plantar pressures in five minutes) and long-term (e.g., heart rate and sleep quality for three months) data. Finally, we have shown and discussed an application scenario with the simulation of our proposed system. The system will optimize the elderly users’ exercise experience when exercising on a treadmill, reduce the risk of falls, and provide guidance for the design of future fitness equipment for the elderly.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Exploration and Machine Learning with Exploration Results for Autonomous Control of Standalone-Intelligent Reflecting Surface
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has gained considerable attention for eliminating dead zones, a significant issue in millimeter-wave communications. However, the existing research on IRS control assumes information sharing and control instructions from the base station (BS), necessitating a backhaul link to the core network and BS. Consequently, a new network system must be constructed, which undermines the IRS’s advantages of low cost and installation flexibility. Therefore, a standalone-IRS, which operates completely independently of the core network and BS, can maximize the performance of the IRS. However, a standalone-IRS cannot obtain sufficient information required for control decisions, such as the channel state information, which is frequently used in existing studies. Consequently, it depends on inefficient control methods such as exploration. In this study, we propose an IRS control method that significantly reduces the overhead through hierarchical exploration and enhances the communication quality by using exploration results as training data, thereby achieving further overhead reduction. We performed simulations to evaluate the overhead and communication quality of the proposed standalone-IRS control method, which combines these techniques.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dual Attention Matching Network Through Multi-Scale Neighborhood Aggregation of Long-Tail Entities
abstract: Knowledge graphs (KGs) are crucial for tasks like recommendation systems and data analysis. Entity alignment, the process of matching equivalent entities across different KGs, is essential for integrating knowledge. However, challenges such as long-tail entities and cross-lingual entity names hinder alignment accuracy. This paper introduces Dual-LTE, a model that uses a multi-scale neighborhood aggregation mechanism to enhance long-tail entity representation and leverages entity names for improved alignment. Experimental results show a 1-1.5% improvement over existing methods on benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Multilevel Drowsiness Detection Using Multimodal Physiological Signals
abstract: Drowsiness detection is critical for preventing incidents such as drowsy driving, which can lead to severe accidents. This study investigates multilevel drowsiness detection through the analysis of multimodal physiological signals, including ECG, EMG, EOG, and EEG. Deep learning models were employed to classify drowsiness levels across both single-modality and multimodality approaches. Detecting slight drowsiness is essential for practical applications, especially in scenarios like preventing drowsy driving. Unlike existing studies that typically focus on binary classifications, i.e., detecting someone is alert or sleepy, this research examines the efficiency of multimodality in finer-grained drowsiness classification. Our findings indicate that while single-modality signals like ECG and EOG offer robust performance, combining modalities, specifically ECG with EMG and EOG with EEG, yields superior accuracy in detecting more detailed levels of drowsiness. The results emphasize the potential of multimodality approaches in enhancing the precision of drowsiness detection, with implications for applications in automotive safety and other critical fields.

articleTitle: Motion Magnification Method Based On Hybrid Channel And Window Attention Mechanism
abstract: Video motion magnification (VMM) aims to enhance the visibility of subtle motions in video sequences, providing a spatially dense and holistic understanding of minute movements within scenes of interest. However, current methods face challenges in distinguishing between subtle motion and background noise. Especially when dealing with sub-pixel level motion, it is inevitable that the output will be affected by noise and blur. To address this issue, we propose a method called HAT-VMM, a novel motion amplification approach based on a hybrid channel and window attention mechanism. This method ingeniously combines channel attention with window-based self-attention to effectively extract motions from noisy data. The synergy of these attention mechanisms allows for a fine balance between global context awareness and robust local representation. Additionally, an innovative overlapping cross-attention module is implemented, enhancing feature integration between windows, significantly improving the model’s ability to interpret complex motion patterns. The proposed method shows a significant improvement in output image quality compared to existing frameworks, producing clearer and more accurate magnified motion outputs while minimizing artifacts and noise, setting a new benchmark for video motion magnification technology. The enhanced magnification accuracy has the potential to broaden the application scope and effectiveness of video motion magnification in scientific and engineering domains.

articleTitle: A Synthetic Data-enhanced Differential Privacy Reinforcement Learning Policy Optimization Method
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (offline RL) has achieved success in various domains in recently year, which helping researcher deploy the policy into the real-word engineering tasks. But there still a challenge in protecting the privacy of the sensitive offline datasets, introducing privacy protect technology into those sensitive datasets is a feasible method to handle this challenge. The recent research prove that different privacy (DP) is an efficient way to introduce DP mechanism into offline RL algorithm, but the DP mechanism could also decrease the policy performance seriously. To address this issue, in this work we purpose Differential Privacy Impact Policy Performance Compensate Buffer (DPCB), a diffusion-based approach to provide high quality dataset for training a well-performing policy with privacy protection. We show that DPCB has a generalization capacity combinate with different offline RL algorithm. Furthermore, we compare DPCB with other offline RL different privacy protect algorithm in privacy protect effectiveness and policy performance, the experiment indicates that DPCB is an effective method to compensate the impact of policy performance and policy oscillation brought by DP mechanism.

articleTitle: Improving Human Activity Recognition by Converting Time-series Point Cloud Data from mmWave Radar into Images
abstract: This study explores the use of millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar technologies for Human Activity Recognition (HAR), emphasizing its advantages over other technologies, such as privacy protection, superior penetration capabilities, and the ability to function independently of ambient light. Existing methods for handling time-series point cloud data for action recognition often involve LSTM or Transformer models. However, those methods have challenges in real-time recognition because of their high computational cost. In this paper, we present a robust method by converting time-series point cloud data into fourchannel images and employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). By transforming the data into images, we leverage CNN to perform efficient and high-accuracy recognition. Our system recognizes the seven activities with $\mathbf{9 8. 3 8 \%}$ accuracy in just 121.40 seconds of training time. Additionally, a more lightweight model achieves $\mathbf{9 8. 2 8 \%}$ accuracy in 59.67 seconds. Our model uses data representing the transitions of the four channels of separated data feature attributes over multiple frames and data capturing interrelationships between each channel. Independent models are trained on each data type, with final classification based on the final layers’ output. In conclusion, our approach offers a lightweight and better-performing solution for potential real-time applications.

articleTitle: InfraTag: Customizable Infrastructure Interaction Activity Recognition on Resource-Constrained Hardware
abstract: Recognition of infrastructure interaction activity can provide environmental context, which is essential for achieving human interaction with ubiquitous computing environments. However, there are different types of infrastructure and user habits, and existing methods generally rely on special-purpose sensing hardware or training models in situ, which are task-specific with a high user burden for open-set recognition tasks. To address this challenge, we created InfraTag, through our proposed customizable method to conduct one-shot customization that combines generalizability and flexibility. This method utilizes prototype encoding by introducing domain knowledge to learn a generic motion posture feature embedding and with a similarity-matching design to achieve one-shot customization on resource-constrained hardware. InfraTag can be attached to infrastructures, and after one-shot learning of the new infrastructure interaction activity sample during the initial deployment, ongoing recognition can be well performed. For example, we apply InfraTag to in-home infrastructures, such as doors, windows, waterpipes, etc., that can augment everyday experiences with context-aware functionality. Overall, our work demonstrates a more general approach to recognizing infrastructure interaction activities in ubiquitous scenarios, and its resource-efficient and easy-to-deploy make it a more feasible option for future consumer devices.

articleTitle: A Human-Machine Reinforcement Learning Framework with Multi-dimensional Human Feedback Fusion
abstract: When addressing complex reinforcement learning problems in practical settings, crafting precise and interpretable reward functions proves challenging and laborious. A more viable strategy involves directly learning reward functions from human feedback, facilitating the integration of human expertise into agent policy optimization. Nonetheless, existing methods often depend on a single teaching mode, such as solely employing demonstrations or preference feedback, thus constraining the diversity of training data. To address this obstacle, we propose a Multi-Dimensional human Feedback-based Human-Machine Reinforcement Learning framework (MDF-HMRL), which integrates expert demonstrations and trajectory preference feedback using a dynamic adaptive weighting method to enhance the robustness and coherence of the reward model. The MDFHMRL framework employs a staged optimization process: firstly mimicking expert behavior via generative adversarial imitation learning, and then integrating preference rewards to refine the policy towards user-specified objectives. Moreover, the framework resolves conflicts between demonstrations and preferences through dynamic reward weight adjustment, outperforming single feedback methods in MuJoCo and Atari game benchmarks. Even under suboptimal demonstration conditions, MDF-HMRL achieves optimal performance by gradually increasing preference feedback utilization. Finally, it reduces reliance on human preferences by about $30 \%$, thereby diminishing the necessity for human-labeled data.

articleTitle: KCIN: A Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolutional Network-Based Model for Transportation Mode Recognition With Incomplete Sensor Series
abstract: Advances in ubiquitous computing and artificial intelligence have catalyzed the rapid evolution of Human Activity Recognition (HAR). As a branch of HAR, Transportation Mode Detection (TMD) have been widely studied in recent years. However, traditional machine learning-based methods are constrained by the limited expressiveness of handcrafted features. Deep learning-based TMD algorithms have shown significantly outperform by automatically extracting high-level features through extensive supervised learning to enhance the model’s representation ability of complex behaviors. Yet, most existing Deep Neural Network models, inspired by Multilayer Perceptions (MLPs), are limited by the nonlinear expressiveness of MLPs and data integrity, failing to learn correct feature representations when sensor data is incomplete. To address this challenge, we introduce a method named KAN-Conv based Context Interpolation Attention Network (KCIN). KCIN adopts the Kolmogorov-Arnold Convolution Network (KAN-Conv) as its foundational structure and leverages Context Interpolation Attention (CA) to recover representations of missing sensor data. This approach effectively enhances the model’s capability to extract robust motion features from sensor series, particularly in scenarios with data loss. Experiments conducted on three realworld datasets substantiate the efficacy of KCIN across various practical settings. Experiments conducted on three real-world datasets have demonstrated KCIN’s effectiveness, achieving accuracies of ${7 8 . 4 6 \%}, 76.31 \%$, and $81.49 \%$ even with ${9 0 \%}$ missing data.

articleTitle: FID: Detecting Adversarial Attacks with Feature Invariants and Applying to License Plate Recognition
abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become an integral part of everyday life. However, researchers have found that DNNs are vulnerable to adversarial examples attacks, which can cause abnormal behaviors such as misclassification. The existence of adversarial examples poses a significant threat to the application of DNNs, particularly in scenarios with high security requirements, such as license plate recognition systems. Current adversarial example defense and detection techniques are effective against specific types of attacks but generally lack universality across all attack types. To address adversarial attacks in real-world license plate recognition systems, we analyze the intrinsic variation of neural networks trained on clean samples and the dimensional complexity between clean samples and propose an unsupervised adversarial example detection system based on feature invariants derived from neural network invariants and local intrinsic dimensionality invariants, named Feature Invariant Detection (FID). We deploy the FID into the widelyused open-source license plate recognition systems HyperLPR and EasyPR, and conducts extensive experiments on FID with the real dataset, the Chinese license plate dataset (CCPD). Experiments are conducted on 11 different types of attacks, and the results show that FID can effectively detect all of these attacks at a lower false positive rate compared to the other four state-of-the-art detection methods, and the accuracy is always as high as $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$. Therefore, FID has good generalization to various types of adversarial attacks.

articleTitle: Research on Machine Unlearning Verification Based on Predictive Cross-Entropy
abstract: The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), implemented by the European Union in 2018, set a global standard for personal data privacy protection. Among its requirements is the “right to be forgotten” which mandates that service providers must delete a user's personal data upon the user's request to withdraw data authorization. However, deep learning networks tend to retain learned information, making them susceptible to privacy attacks. While several methods exist for achieving machine unlearning to enforce the right to be forgotten, verifying the effectiveness of machine unlearning remains challenging. In this paper, we propose the metric “Percentage of Unlearning” (PoU), which measures the extent of machine unlearning through the change in predictive cross-entropy of the data intended to be forgotten during the unlearning process. We introduce a machine unlearning verification framework based on predictive cross-entropy, enabling users to self-verify whether their data has been deleted without solely relying on the service providers' assurances. This framework also assists service providers in ensuring complete machine unlearning while minimizing time and computational costs. We compared the PoU metric with existing verification metrics such as ACC and MIA recall. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to existing verification methods, the PoU metric not only confirms the effectiveness of machine unlearning but also addresses the shortcomings of existing metrics by quantifying the degree of unlearning.

articleTitle: News-ExplaiNER: An Automated Fake News Detector and Explainer with Deep Learning and NLP
abstract: The widespread of the fake news on online platforms has emerged as a major concern in today’s information era. To counteract the spread of misinformation, researchers have put in a lot of efforts in researching effective and accurate fake news detection models. However, the lack of transparency and explainability hinders those models’ usage. This paper presents a novel methodology on detecting the veracity of the news contents and simultaneously providing an explanation on the prediction result, thereby enhancing transparency and trustworthiness of the model. This work proposes the News-ExplaiNER framework, an automated fake news detection and explanation system. The framework comprises of a news content classification model and a result explanation model. The classification achieved an accuracy score of $\mathbf{8 9. 4 4 \%}$, surpassing previous endeavours in this domain by 4%. Additionally, our explanation model implements a mechanism to quantify the performance of explainability in this particular task.

articleTitle: CLPCare: Bootstrapping Multimodal Large Language Models for Ultrasound Cleft Lip and Palate Recognition and Analysis
abstract: Cleft lip and palate is a common congenital malformations in fetuses, and early diagnosis is crucial for reducing the physical and psychological impact on pregnant women and their families. Traditional image processing methods for recognizing and analyzing cleft lip and palate rely on manual annotation and have limited interpretability. To address this issue, we propose a method for ultrasound image recognition and analysis of cleft lip and palate based on multimodal large language models. Firstly, we design a specific ultrasound image findings instruction finetuning template and fine-tune the multimodal large language model to enhance the model’s recognition capability. Secondly, we conceive a specific retrieval-enhanced prompt template aimed at improving the model’s understanding of cleft lip and palate analysis. Lastly, we evaluate our framework using a real dataset from Xiamen Maternal and Child Health Hospital in China. Additionally, we develop a medical system for the recognition and analysis of cleft lip and palate.

articleTitle: DNS Tunneling Detection with New Patterns Emerging For Intelligent Agriculture: A Forest-Based Classifier with An Unknown Option
abstract: In Intelligent agriculture, securing data transmission is critical due to the vast amount of data generated by sensors. DNS tunneling poses a threat by exfiltrating data through DNS queries, a challenge for traditional classifiers, especially with “unknown queries” not seen during training. This paper frames DNS tunneling detection as a machine learning problem involving Classification with New Patterns Emerging (CNPE). We introduce a forest-based classifier that identifies unknown patterns as a new class and accurately classifies known samples. Our model is efficient in both computation and memory. Experiments on live network data and public datasets validate its effectiveness, demonstrating its potential to enhance data security and system reliability in Intelligent agriculture.

articleTitle: Design of a Parkinson’s Rehabilitation Management System Based on Multimodal Learning and Digital Twin Technology
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD), a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, significantly impairs motor functions, necessitating effective rehabilitation management. This paper presents the design of a Parkinson’s rehabilitation management system leveraging multimodal learning and digital twin technology. By integrating data from diverse sources—such as speech signals, hand motion data, and gait videos—this system comprehensively captures PD symptoms, facilitating early detection and accurate diagnosis. Employing deep learning techniques, the system analyzes and fuses multimodal data, enhancing diagnostic precision and providing personalized rehabilitation plans. The digital twin component creates a virtual model of the patient, continuously monitoring motor functions, medication responses, and symptom changes, thus optimizing treatment plans and improving quality of life. Case studies demonstrate the system’s efficacy in speech recognition, tremor identification, and tremor severity assessment, highlighting its role in enhancing patient self-management and rehabilitation outcomes. The proposed system not only advances PD rehabilitation management, but also sets a precedent for intelligent healthcare solutions by integrating multimodal data analysis with digital twin technology.

articleTitle: Overcoming the Data Availability Paradox with Managed Digital Twin Instances
abstract: Digital transformation, IoT, and cloud storage have led to vast data collections that tend to exist in isolated silos, thus limiting their utilization. This leads to the data availability paradox, in which individuals, groups, and organizations possess vast amounts of data but struggle to utilize or share it effectively. The struggle is due to privacy, security, and intellectual property concerns. When this happens, individuals and institutions are unable to take full advantage of the capability of Industry 4.0 and digitalization. This paper proposes using managed Digital Twin Instances (DTI) to overcome this paradox. The fully managed digital twin instances provide well-defined and fully controlled access to models derived from the underlying data sets. Digital twin instances, therefore serve as virtual replicas of real-world systems, entities, or processes, enabling controlled access. A key issue in this approach is the effective hosting and managing large numbers of digital twin instances. The paper introduces a management and hosting framework and its evaluation in the MS Azure cloud environment.

articleTitle: Explainable Traffic Accident Severity Prediction with Attention-Enhanced Bidirectional GRU-LSTM
abstract: This study aims to improve the accuracy and interpretability of traffic accident severity nowcasting by introducing a stacked Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) deep learning model. Accurately predicting traffic accident severity is crucial for enhancing traffic management and reducing the impact of accidents. We employed a stacked Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) - Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) model with an attention mechanism, integrating multivariate accident data to capture complex temporal dynamics. The use of SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values enhances the interpretability of the model. The model demonstrates high reliability and effectiveness, achieving an accuracy of 88.06% and an F1-score of 0.867 in real-time applications. It provides valuable insights into the factors influencing predictions, making the decision-making process transparent. This framework not only advances predictive performance but also aligns with ethical AI deployment, making it a valuable tool for traffic management and policy formulation.

articleTitle: A multimodal feature learning framework with graph structure learning and CLIP for apparent personality analysis*
abstract: Automatic personality prediction has become a challenging topic in computer vision. This paper proposes a novel multimodal feature learning framework with graph structure learning and CLIP for analyzing personality from short videos (GSL-CLIP). We construct a facial graph for the visual modality and propose a Geo method based on GCN and CNN to extract static facial appearance and geometric features. Furthermore, the pre-trained CLIP and VGGish CNN are used as feature extractors to extract their spatial features. Then, we design a graph relation attention network to mine their temporal feature in visual and audio modalities. Finally, we aggregate these two features through MLP to form a scene-audio association feature. Additionally, to enhance our framework’s robustness, we employ the pre-trained VGGish CNN for audio spatial features, and the BiRNN with an attention mechanism is used to extract significant audio temporal features. Finally, we introduce a multimodal channel residual attention network for fusing multimodal features and leverage an MLP regression model to predict scores for personality traits. The experimental results indicate that the effectiveness of our proposed GSL-CLIP is superior to state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Situational Design for Equitable Home Safety: Bio-Psycho-Social Approach Based on Data-Driven Situational Risk Assessment
abstract: The technology for enabling more inclusive and equitable home safety by considering diverse living situations is strongly needed. This study proposes a novel assistive technology designed to enhance injury prevention at home, grounded in situational risk and a bio-psycho-social model. Unlike the conventional information dissemination system such as hazard prediction training systems, the proposed system allows us to quantitatively assess risks based on a large amount of accidental situation data in a data-driven way. It also deals with a function for lowering psychological barriers to taking preventive measures at actual home environments. To this end, the proposed method comprises the following three primary functions on a virtual reality system: 1) presenting accident data within similar living conditions based on situational risk at the biological level; 2) identifying psychological barriers to adopting preventive measures at the psychological level; and 3) providing information for accessing social support at the social level. The system was implemented using accident data from the Tokyo Fire Department (429,848 cases) and survey data from 600 caregivers regarding their reasons for not implementing prevention measures. In addition, a questionnaire survey of 11 practitioners, including doctors, nurses, and nursery staff, was conducted to evaluate the system’s core functionalities.

articleTitle: A Vulnerability-Driven Gym for Training Autonomous Cyber Agents with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Autonomous agents allow frequent and regular penetration testing to be performed, which is increasingly necessary as there is a growing need for skilled and expensive specialists to examine and improve the cybersecurity of organizations. Besides, given the success of reinforcement learning in various domains, it is promising to explore the application of its methods to the development of intelligent and autonomous cyber agents. Currently, the cyber agents are trained only on limited scenarios and have weak transfer capabilities to new environments. This study is intended to train red agents that can conduct automated attacks in unexplored new cyber scenarios. To achieve this, we propose a vulnerability-driven approach called VDGym, which is a four-step cyber gym generator. By combining two augmentation methods, VDGym is able to generate diverse cyber scenarios. To verify the validity of our method, we train our agents on plenty of RL training scenarios randomly generated by VDGym and test the trained model on existing well-designed scenarios without reinforcement. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively help train agents and generalize better to new scenarios.

articleTitle: Design and experiment of a VSLAM system by calculating feature points with a wide-angle camera
abstract: Precise localization is important for the intelligent navigation of mobile robot systems. To address the issue of distortion in images from a wide-angle camera and enhance localization accuracy, an enhanced visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) framework utilizing a correction model for wide-angle cameras is proposed. Firstly, images are divided into blocks, and the details of certain selected blocks are enhanced. Secondly, feature points from enhanced blocks are extracted, which improves the extraction of feature points across the entire set of images. Finally, points corresponding to incident light on a normalized plane are designed as template points. The template points and the images are matched using the wide-angle camera model, leading to the calculation of the pixel coordinates of the template points within the images, along with their descriptors. Furthermore, lots of experiments are conducted with public datasets. The results indicate a reduction in trajectory and translation errors when employing the proposed VSLAM framework, leading to the improvement of the average matching accuracy by about 3.5% compared to exist systems.

articleTitle: Themis: Adaptive CPU Resource Allocation for VMs on Heterogeneous Multicore Architectures
abstract: Tenants usually rent virtual machines (VMs) to deploy their applications, while those VMs are generally colocated on the same physical machine by the cloud provider to improve resource utilization. Meanwhile, modern CPUs are evolving towards heterogeneous multicore architecture, which integrates powerful brawny cores and power-efficient wimpy cores into a CPU of a machine. This paper focuses on how to allocate CPU resources when co-locating VMs on the heterogeneous architecture. When a VM is created by the Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) virtualization technology, it consists of vCPU threads and Emulator threads. Our investigation shows that properly setting the range of CPU cores where Emulator threads are allowed to run can further improve the VM performance, when using Linux Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) to schedule VMs. However, it is challenging to find the proper range setting because running different applications in the VM leads to nonidentical optimal range settings, and the VM is usually a black-box from the perspective of the cloud provider. We therefore propose Themis, a runtime system comprising a core scheduler and a load monitor. The core scheduler finds the proper range setting based on low-level information, while the load monitor identifies whether the load of the VM is significantly changed and the range is required to be adjusted. The experimental results show that Themis improves the performance of popular cloud applications by up to 48.4% compared with prior work.

articleTitle: Intelligent Urban Emergency Response: Integrating Large Language Models, Multi-Objective Optimization, and Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Urban emergency response plays a critical role in protecting lives and property during crises. However, traditional emergency response systems often struggle with inefficient resource allocation, uncoordinated relief efforts, and delayed decision-making. To address these challenges, we propose a novel intelligent decision-making framework that integrates large language models for victim interaction, multi-objective optimization for resource allocation, and reinforcement learning for personalized dispatch. Our approach consists of three main components: an intelligent voice assistant that engages in human-like conversations with victims, a multi-objective optimization model (ERMOO) for efficient resource allocation, and a Deep Q-Networks (DQN) based reinforcement learning approach for personalized dispatch policies. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our approach compared to existing baselines. The results highlight the immense potential of integrating cutting-edge AI techniques to revolutionize urban emergency response practices. By bridging the gap between artificial intelligence and human intelligence, our framework provides a solid foundation for creating more resilient, equitable, and human-centered emergency management systems. This work aims to inspire further research and innovation in this critical domain, ultimately benefiting urban societies worldwide.

articleTitle: AH-UNet: An Efficient and Enhanced Network for Accurate Melanoma Segmentation
abstract: Melanoma (MM) is a highly metastatic and deadly skin disease. However, current diagnostic methods for melanoma face challenges such as invasiveness, poor repeatability, and subjectivity. Therefore, researchers are attempting to use computer technology and algorithms to assist doctors in the diagnosis and treatment of melanoma. In this study, two modules, the adaptive context aware feature attention (ACAFA) and the hybrid attention block with dilated and external mechanisms (HADEM), are first constructed to balance the extraction of global features and local detail features, effectively capturing the multiscale features and long-range dependency relationships of melanoma images. Subsequently, these two modules are combined with the UNet model to propose an optimization network called AH-UNet aimed at improving the accuracy of melanoma segmentation. The feasibility and performance of the AH-UNet model are demonstrated and quantified using the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2017 and 2018 datasets. Quantitative and qualitative analysis results demonstrate the advantages of the $\mathbf{A H}$-UNet algorithm in handling image noise and skin lesion edge details. Additionally, the model was compared to 8 different deep learning models, achieving optimal segmentation accuracy values of 95.94% and 94.56% in the ISIC-2017 and ISIC-2018 databases respectively, proving the effectiveness of the AH-UNet model in melanoma lesion segmentation.

articleTitle: Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection via Proxy Task Learning on Normal Samples
abstract: Traditional industrial anomaly detection methods rely on extensive samples through unsupervised learning using the one-product-one-model paradigm. This data-hungry and rigid training-inference paradigm is not prone to adapting to flexible and changeable real industrial scenarios. Few-shot learning and contrastive learning offer promising solutions by enabling models to recognize anomalies with a few normal samples. This paper presents a novel approach that enhances model robustness and accuracy by leveraging three different proxy tasks learned from normal samples. We generate positive samples through image geometric transformations and negative samples by injecting anomaly noise into normal samples. A multi-level, multi-scale feature fusion structure is proposed to produce refined, fine-grained image feature maps. Specifically, we employ a rotation prediction task, a pixel-level contrastive learning task, and an image-level contrastive learning task to jointly optimize our model. Comparative and comprehensive experiments were conducted on two sought-after industrial anomaly detection datasets. The results demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to other advanced methods.

articleTitle: KGViT: Knowledge Graph Integrated Vision Transformer for EEG-Based Emotion Recognition
abstract: Emotion recognition using electroencephalography (EEG) has attracted considerable attention and achieved significant advancements in the brain-computer interface field. Although many deep learning methods have shown superior performance over traditional approaches in emotion recognition tasks, existing studies neglect auxiliary information, such as participants’ details and descriptions of stimuli, focusing solely on EEG data. This oversight may lead to poor generalization across different participants. To address this issue, we propose a knowledge graph integrated with a vision transformer (KGViT). The KGViT model utilizes the vision transformer to capture effective features from the 3D temporal-spectral-spatial representations of EEG data. Innovatively, we design a knowledge graph feature extraction module using a graph convolutional network. This module processes node and relation matrices constructed from the EEG dataset, enabling the model to leverage prior knowledge for improved performance. The hybrid feature fusion module is introduced to calculate dynamic weights for knowledge graph features based on EEG features and integrate them into a unified representation. Extensive experiments were conducted on the DEAP and DREAMER datasets to assess the effectiveness of KGViT, with outcomes surpassing the state-of-the-art baseline. Accuracy rates of $\mathbf{9 7. 7 8 \%}, \mathbf{9 8. 0 6 \%}, \mathbf{9 8. 8 9 \%}$, and $\mathbf{9 7. 4 7 \%}$ were achieved on DEAP-Valence, DEAP-Arousal, DREAMER-Valence, and DREAMER-Arousal, respectively.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning based on Diffusion Graph for Implicit Collaborative Filtering
abstract: Recently, collaborative filtering based on contrastive learning has been intensively researched in the recommendation community, where positives are user-item interactions and negatives are selected from uninteractions. Although most studies have focused on negative sampling strategy and loss function design, few have investigated how positives would impact recommendation performance. Indeed, it could happen that some user-item interactions are kinds of misclicks, acting as noises during contrastive learning. This paper studies how to mitigate the effects of misclicks via the feature mixup technique and improves all components of contrastive learning. Taking the user-item interaction matrix as a bipartite graph, our proposed CLDG4CF model first obtains the associate matrix of its diffusion graph via the personalized random walk with restart. The associate matrix to some extent describes the potential interaction likelihoods between users and items in the convergence state, which is used for positive generation, negative sampling, and weighted loss in contrastive learning. In particular, we randomly select interacted items and weighted mixup their encodings as a generated positive. We select uninteracted items as negatives based on the item-item part in the associate matrix according to their association coefficients to those already selected interactions. Finally, we use their association coefficients to compost a weighted contrastive loss in contrastive learning. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our design in terms of the improved recommendation performance over the peer contrastive learning approaches.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder Based on Anomaly Detection with sMRI Gray Matter Slices
abstract: The current research focus on Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a reflection of its significant adverse impact on individuals and society. Structural magnetic resonance imaging (SMRI) is a valuable tool for clinicians in diagnosing and identifying MDD. sMRI employs a uniform imaging protocol, and images of gray matter slices in the same plane across different sMRIs demonstrate high similarity, revealing repetitive anatomical structures between patients. Given the consistency of anatomical structures, the same regional evidence in normal images presents similar physiological structural information. Lesions, meanwhile, cause structural changes that manifest as abnormal patterns. In this paper, we apply the SQUID model, which is capable of detecting abnormal structural information, to the MDD classification problem. The study employed gray matter slice data generated by SMRI from 1025 individuals with MDD and 1205 Healthy Controls(HC). The objective was to undertake an abnormality detection classification task in MDD and HC, and to further verify the pivotal role of the hippocampus in the diagnosis of MDD through masked experiment. The findings contribute novel methods and evidence for the clinical diagnosis of MDD.

articleTitle: Survey on Blockchain-Based Internet of Things Security Technologies
abstract: Internet of Things(IoT) terminals are characterized by large number, wide distribution, complex hierarchical structure, etc., and are often in complex environments, which are more susceptible to attacks than traditional Internet terminal devices, and their security management faces greater challenges. Because blockchain technology has the advantages of being distributed, decentralized, and not easily tampered with, it is very suitable for solving the current security problems faced by the Internet of Things. In this paper, the research on the security aspects of IoT based on blockchain technology in recent years is sorted out, discussing the application of blockchain technology in the field of IoT security from three aspects of privacy protection, identity authentication, and access control, analyzing the technical characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of different technical solutions, and looking forward to the future development of these fields.

articleTitle: Lyapunov-Based Network Slicing and Resource Optimization in Air-Ground Integrated Networks
abstract: The air-ground integrated network (AGIN) architecture is the key support for future 6 G to realize ubiquitous network connectivity. For the diversity and heterogeneity of the AGIN, we need to divide the slicing resources for different services. To cope with the suddenness and uncertainty of business arrivals, a flexible resource slice management solution is required. This paper models the joint optimization problem of service request scheduling, network slicing, and resource allocation as a multi-stage stochastic mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem. The goal is to maximize the system utility under long-term user data queue stability constraints and minimize the number of re-slicing times by rational resource allocation when service requests change dynamically. In order to solve the coupling problem of service request scheduling, network slicing, and resource allocation in different time frame decisions, we propose an online control algorithm named ORSRM. It first applies Lyapunov optimization to decouple the MINLP problem into a series of per time slot deterministic subproblems. Then a clustering algorithm is used to determine the UAV location and the service request scheduling decisions are generated based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Finally, the per time slot system utility is maximized by optimizing the upper bound of the Lyapunov drift plus penalty function. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can ensure system stability while meeting user needs and try to avoid network re-slicing caused by changes in service requirements as much as possible.

articleTitle: Industrial Data Space Framework Design and Feasibility Analysis - A Case Study of China’s New Energy Industry
abstract: In the rapidly evolving field of new energy, technological advancements and the expansion of application scopes have underscored the importance of effective data management and analysis. However, the new energy industry faces challenges such as the imbalance in spatial and temporal distribution and the significant impact of weather on the efficiency of wind and photovoltaic power. This study, based on the actual conditions of China’s new energy industry chain, proposes an innovative data space framework aimed at accelerating the development of the new energy sector. The framework features a modular design, offering a flexible, scalable, and user-friendly solution through key processes such as data analysis, data transmission, and data governance.At the onset of the research, core requirements for data management in the new energy field were identified through an in-depth analysis of the industry background.
