Based on these requirements, a four-layer architecture model was constructed, comprising the data layer, analysis layer, interaction layer, and server layer. To verify the practical feasibility of the designed framework, a comprehensive study of China’s new energy industry was conducted, and a series of empirical analyses confirmed the framework’s applicability and effectiveness in Chinese new energy projects. The data space framework proposed for the new energy field in this study is technically viable. Future research will focus on further optimizing and expanding the functions of the framework, with the aim of widespread implementation and application in a broader range of new energy scenarios.

articleTitle: SGNet: A Multi-Scale Method for Steel Surface Defect Detection
abstract: The large variation in target scales within steel surface defect images often results in low detection accuracy. To address this issue, we have developed a multi-scale defect detection method named SGNet. Initially, we introduced a Self-Guided Bi-Level Routing Transformer (SG-BiFormer) as the backbone network of our model. SG-BiFormer utilizes a self-guided strategy to model global information and dynamically reallocates tokens based on the importance of image regions, increasing token quantity in significant areas to preserve fine-grained details and reducing it in less critical areas. This strategy significantly enhances the accuracy and efficiency of the model in handling multi-scale targets. Subsequently, we incorporated Grouped Separable Convolutions (GSConv) to manage local information of multi-scale features. GSConv automatically adjusts the size and shape of the convolution kernels according to different input features. This design not only improves global information processing capabilities but also ensures sensitive and precise detail capture. Lastly, we employed MPDIoU as the loss function for our model, which optimizes corner positioning to tackle the challenges of regression tasks, substantially improving the accuracy of the model in handling complex defects. Experimental evidence confirms the effectiveness of this method. Our SGNet achieved a 77.1% mAP on the NEU-DET dataset, demonstrating outstanding performance.

articleTitle: Dual Knowledge Aware Graph Convolutional Networks Over Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Recently, graph convolutional networks (GCNs) have become effective approaches to capture the semantic information of sentences in aspect-based sentiment analysis (ABSA) tasks. Nonetheless, these approaches still face challenges due to syntactic and contextual dependency information from graphs. Therefore, we propose a novel ABSA model by constructing a Dual Knowledge aware Graph Convolutional Networks (DKGCN). First, we obtain the attention score of sentences and aspect words, respectively, via a context-based attention mechanism, to enhance the accuracy of contextual words related to aspect words. Second, we propose a novel syntactic knowledge-based GCN via dependency trees to reduce the connections of words that are not related to the aspect words. Afterward, we propose dual graphs based on context knowledge, consisting of the aspect topic graph and the aspectinfer graph, to achieve contextual knowledge representation of critical aspect words more effectively. In particular, the aspect-topic graph represents relationships between specific aspects and their contextual words according to syntactical dependencies. Moreover, the aspect-infer graph is constructed by an aspect word and other related aspect words inferred by their relationships based on the aspect-topic graph. Finally, we feed dual graphs into the GCNs and the interactive network to extract the fused feature information. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed DKGCN model surpasses advanced baselines in aspect-level sentiment classification.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition with Residual Attention Using Commodity Millimeter Wave Radar
abstract: Gesture recognition technology based on millimeter wave radar can identify and classify user gestures in non-contact scenarios. To address the complexity of data processing with multi-feature input in neural networks and the poor recognition performance with single-feature input, this paper proposes a gesture recognition algorithm based on ResNet-Long Short Term Memory with attention mechanism (RLA). In the signal processing stage of RLA, a range-Doppler map is generated by extracting range and velocity features from the original mmWave radar signal. In the network architecture, RLA combines the features of a residual network with channel and spatial attention modules, ensuring that no useful information is overlooked. We introduce the residual-attention mechanism to enhance the network’s focus on gesture features and avoid the impact of irrelevant features on recognition accuracy. Furthermore, the long short-term memory network is employed to handle temporal features, ensuring high recognition accuracy even when only single-feature inputs are available. A series of experimental results show that the proposed RLA algorithm in this paper has superior recognition performance.

articleTitle: ViT-MGI: Context-aware Lightweight Malicious Gradient Identification for Federated Vision Transformer Systems against Poisoning Attacks
abstract: With the continuous development of large vision models, training requires increasingly large datasets. Federated Learning for Vision Transformer models (Federated ViT) is needed to train models without data leaving multiple clients while capturing complex global features. However, various attacks, such as tampering with gradient data, label-flipping, and backdoor attacks, pose significant challenges to federated learning. Existing defense mechanisms like the Krum algorithm, PCA, and Sniper scheme exhibit low efficiency and poor robustness in Federated ViT scenarios due to the vast number of parameters and inactive neurons. This paper proposes a two-stage, context-aware lightweight malicious gradient identification method for ViT to improve the efficiency and robustness of malicious user detection. By using feature layer extraction and Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we eliminate invalid gradient information, enhancing both detection efficiency and robustness. We reduced data dimensions to $\mathbf{0. 4 \%}$ of the original without compromising detection accuracy. The Isolation Forest algorithm distinguishes between malicious and benign users based on extracted gradient features, and a Subjective Logic Model performs temporal accumulation of user scores to improve accuracy and reduce erroneous identifications. Experiments on CIFAR-10, MNIST, and OrganAMNIST datasets show that our model reduces processing time by approximately 70% compared to advanced PCA methods, while significantly improving accuracy and F1 scores. Additionally, our method offers substantial advantages in both efficiency and robustness compared to pooling techniques aimed at reducing computational load. We have named our model ViT-MGI and released its source code to facilitate future research in this field: https://github.com/LetMeFly666/ViT-MGI.

articleTitle: Low-Light Optical Flow Estimation by Enhancing Reflection Component with Global Attention
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for optical flow estimation under low-light conditions, addressing the limitations of existing techniques. Our approach enhances reflection components with global attention within a matching framework, achieving high precision with minimal iterations. We extract global and local motion features by decomposing input images and computing global correlations between adjacent frames, enabling accurate optical flow estimation. A key contribution is the creation of a specialized dataset for lowlight optical flow, featuring synthetic data generated by adjusting brightness and adding noise to standard datasets, alongside real-world low-light videos. This dataset serves as a robust benchmark for evaluating our method. We further optimize computational efficiency using partial convolutions and sparse matching strategies. Experimental results show that our method surpasses existing techniques, particularly in lowbrightness scenarios, validating our approach’s and dataset’s effectiveness.

articleTitle: Practical Self-Supervised Contrastive Driver Maneuver Interaction Learning via Augmenting Inertial Measurement Unit Signals
abstract: Driver maneuver interaction learning (DMIL), i.e., learning and classifying the maneuver types (e.g., left or right turns, acceleration and deceleration) of a driver, is essential for developing advanced driver assistance systems and understanding driver behaviors in complex traffic environments. In this study, we propose S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-DMIL, a self-supervised contrastive DMIL framework. We focus on the inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors, i.e., accelerometer and gyroscope, and aim to (a) reduce the reliance on large-scale labeled or annotated IMU for DMIL; and (b) capture crucial and meaningful representations for accurate DMIL in complex traffic environments. To this end, we have performed data augmentation upon time series of the unlabeled IMU signal data (e.g., through cropping, permutation), and designed self-supervised contrastive learning to capture the important representations. Within the contrastive learning process, we have implemented efficient convolution blocks as the feature encoding module, and pre-train it for the subsequent maneuver classification. Based on the pre-trained feature encoding module from the self-supervised contrastive learning, we further fine-tune S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-DMIL based on labeled driver maneuvers toward classification of the complex driver behaviors. We have conducted extensive data-driven studies upon a total of 5,799 samples from the open-sourced dataset (Berkeley Deep Drive-X). Our results demonstrate that our S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-DMIL outperforms the other baseline approaches (e.g., by about 12% on average in terms of accuracy) in learning the complex driver maneuvers.

articleTitle: Dual-Branch Network with Transformer and CNN for Underwater Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Underwater semantic segmentation provides visual information for underwater exploration and surveying applications, playing a crucial role in the development and conservation of marine resources. However, semantic segmentation of underwater images is technically challenging due to the complexity and challenging nature of underwater environments. In this work, we propose an underwater semantic segmentation network based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Transformers to extract comprehensive features of underwater objects from both global and local perspectives. To address the scale variations of underwater objects, we propose a multi-scale feature enhancement module (MSFE), which utilizes multiple receptive fields to adapt to underwater objects at different scales. In addition, a local feature extraction (LFE) module is introduced to capture underwater objects of different shapes, which adaptively fuses conventional and deformable convolutional features using the spatial attention mechanism. Experimentally, our model outperforms previous semantic segmentation methods on the underwater semantic segmentation benchmark datasets, i.e., the SUIM dataset, and the DeepFish dataset. In detail, the mean intersection over union (mloU) and mean pixel accuracy (mPA) of our model on the SUIM dataset achieve $\mathbf{7 4. 2 1} \%$ and $\mathbf{8 1. 6 7 \%}$, $\mathbf{2. 4 4 \%}$ and $\mathbf{2. 9 1 \%}$ higher than the baseline model, respectively. And for the DeepFish dataset, our model achieves $\mathbf{9 6. 5 7 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 7. 9 9} \%$ for mloU and $\mathbf{m P A}$, respectively.

articleTitle: QMLFQ: A Quantization-based Queue Scheduling Framework for Efficient LLM Serving
abstract: Fueled by advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs), applications like ChatGPT have ushered in a transformative era for AI-powered interactions. However, the computational demands of LLMs, characterized by their massive parameter size and intricate computations, pose a significant challenge to its model serving. Under high concurrency or resource-constrained scenarios, LLM service systems can experience substantial latency and potential crashes, jeopardizing user experience and system stability. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel LLM serving framework that leverages dynamic queue scheduling and quantization switching to alleviate computational bottlenecks and reduce response latency. Specifically, we propose an enhanced scheduling algorithm based on the Multi-level Feedback Queue (MLFQ) that dynamically switches between various quantized-level models and prioritizes requests, thereby improving LLM inference parallelism and reducing job completion time (JCT) as well. Through extensive experiments conducted on open-source datasets, we demonstrate that our proposed approach effectively reduces JCTs compared to other leading baselines. This improvement in JCT ultimately leads to enhanced quality of service (QoS) for LLM-based applications.

articleTitle: An Offloading Scheme for Diverse Inter-Dependent Tasks in Vehicle Edge Computing
abstract: Vehicle Edge Computing (VEC) is a promising paradigm for efficiently processing massive amounts of data from sensors and stable responses to diverse applications from vehicles. In the usual scenario, the data needs to be transmitted between different nodes and the applications can be represented as inter-dependent tasks. Moreover, the subtasks in each task have diverse interdependencies and each task has a different deadline. Therefore, in order to make the task offloading decision, two questions must be answered: when and where each subtask should be offloaded according to its dependencies. This paper formulates the execution sequence of subtasks by modeling the relationships between subtasks with Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG). Meanwhile, to satisfy the deadline of applications, the computing resources of idle vehicles are sufficiently utilized, and the computing resources on the VEC server are efficiently allocated to tasks. To optimize the overall performance of the system, this paper constructs an optimization problem of minimizing average task completion delay, and proposes the Optimal Offloading Strategy and Resource Allocation for Multi-Dependent Tasks (OSRA-MDT) scheme to solve this optimization problem. Simulation results show that our proposed OSRA-MDT scheme has achieved up to $24 \%$ improvement in reducing the average task completion latency of the system compared to the baseline scheme.

articleTitle: RSBO based LSTM network for pulsed eddy current steel wall-thinning inspection
abstract: Corrosion-induced wall thinning in steel pressure vessels presents a critical threat to the safety and reliability of industrial operations, requiring effective inspection methods. In this paper, the random searching Bayesian optimization (RSBO) based long-and short-term memory (LSTM) network is proposed to estimate the wall thinning. To improve computational efficiency and reduce data redundancy, data augmentation is firstly conducted by selecting the sample interval with more features. Then the RSBO based LSTM model is designed to estimate the thickness. With the designed estimator, it can automatically tune the hyperparameters for the LSTM network which is friendly for the users. Experiments have been carried out and, from the experimental results, the proposed model has a better performance and can achieve the thickness estimation with the average MAPE of 5.54% and MAE of 1.98 mm.

articleTitle: HCMANet: Hierarchical Cross-Modality Attention Network for Underwater Salient Object Detection
abstract: Combining RGB images with depth maps for salient object detection (SOD) has gradually become a familiar approach. However, underwater imagery suffers severe quality degradation because of challenges like scattering, light absorption, and marine snow. These challenges invalidate the applicability of conventional salient detection methods designed for natural images. To address this challenge, we propose the Hierarchical Cross-Modality Attention Network (HCMANet) for underwater salient object detection (USOD), which effectively fuses features from RGB and depth modalities to suppress underwater noise interference and generate saliency prediction maps. Specifically, the HCMANet network employs a dual-stream parallel encoder to extract features from RGB and depth maps separately. Drawing on attention mechanisms, we further propose the Multimodal Knowledge Interaction Module (MKIM) to establish long-range dependencies between RGB and depth features and generate more discriminative information, thereby effectively tackling underwater noise and fostering feature alignment. Then, we design the Fusion Decoder (FD) that decodes the aligned features step by step to obtain accurate prediction maps. Extensive comparisons with recently proposed methods on two public USOD datasets demonstrate the superiority of our methods.

articleTitle: How to Make Your Multi-Image Posts Popular? An Approach to Enhanced Grid for Nine Images on Social Media
abstract: The nine-grid layout is commonly used for multiimage posts, arranging nine images in a tic-tac-toe board. This layout effectively presents content within limited space.Moreover, due to the numerous possible arrangements within the nineimage grid, the optimal arrangement that yields the highest level of attractiveness remains unknown. Our study investigates how the arrangement of images within a nine-grid layout affects the overall popularity of the image set, aiming to explore alignment schemes more aligned with user preferences. Based on survey results regarding user preferences in image arrangement, we have identified two ordering sequences that are widely recognized: sequential order and center prioritization, considering both image visual content and aesthetic quality as alignment metrics, resulting in four layout schemes. Finally, we recruited participants to annotate various layout schemes of the same set of images. Our experiential-centered evaluation indicates that layout schemes based on aesthetic quality outperformed others. This research yields empirical evidence supporting the optimization of the nine-grid layout for multi-image posts, thereby furnishing content creators with valuable insights to enhance both attractiveness and user experience.

articleTitle: DASM: Dual Attention Subgraph Matching Model Incorporating Local Behavior-Aware Features for Threat Hunting
abstract: Threat hunting represents a crucial instrument for safeguarding network security, entailing the proactive identification of potential security threats within a system. However, the types of operations represented in the provenance graphs are diverse and complex. Most learning-based threat matching methods concentrate on the learning of the overall graph structure, yet they neglect to delve deeply into the local structural features that emerge under different operation types. To address these issues, this paper proposes DASM, a dual attention subgraph matching model incorporating local behavior-aware features for threat hunting. Specifically, at the local level, we propose a local operational feature learning method for the provenance graph, constructing an independent local graph for each operation type and applying a node attention mechanism to refine feature learning. At the global level, we design an attack operational semantic attention network that adaptively adjusts the importance weights of different operations, ensuring that core behavioral features are accurately identified. DASM effectively captures local details while emphasizing global behavioral patterns, thereby enhancing the accuracy and reliability of complex attack pattern matching. Subsequently, we implement an efficient graph matching procedure for provenance and attack query vectors in an ordered embedding space. Experimental results show that DASM excels in attack graph matching on the DARPA dataset, achieving 95% accuracy and outperforming recent provenance graph-based attack subgraph matching methods.

articleTitle: Multi-hop Link Quality Prediction for DRL based Task Offloading in RSU-assisted IoV
abstract: Roadside units (RSUs) with strong sensing abilities enhance the feasibility of the RSU-to-Everything (R2X) paradigm, providing crucial infrastructure support for mobile edge computing and reducing data processing latency. Due to the limited computing capacity of RSUs, it is beneficial to offload tasks to other RSUs, vehicles, and cloud servers for processing, allowing for the efficient utilization of computational resources. To leverage the abundant idle vehicle resources on the road, tasks can be offloaded to vehicles outside the coverage area of the RSUs through multi-hop transmission. Due to the high mobility of vehicles, there is a risk of communication link disconnection during task transmission, which poses a challenge to the reliable transmission of tasks. In this paper, we ensure the communication link quality among nodes based on the established vehicle mobility model, and design a mechanism for selecting forwarding vehicles. The goal is to find the path with the highest reliability between vehicles and the source RSU. To encourage nodes to participate in multi-hop transmission, a certain relay cost and computational cost are paid to the computing nodes. We establish a joint optimization model focusing on task delay and task cost. To achieve this, we develop a 0-1 mathematical model and then transform it into a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Building on this foundation, we propose a solution based on Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly reduces task delay and task cost.

articleTitle: Digital Twins for IC Packages and Electronics-enabled Systems
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) is a key technology in Industry 4.0 and has been embraced by several industries, including manufacturing, automotive, and electronics. With the ever-increasing complexity of electronics packaging, Digital Twins are even more relevant as they offer a revolutionary approach by enabling real-time monitoring, analysis, and optimization. There are several contextualized definitions and application-specific interpretations of DT that don’t necessarily clarify the reach of the concept. This paper presents an overview of the concept evolution, its architecture, and the workflow of a Digital Twin system. Then, the five-dimensional model of DT is further expanded for the microelectronics domain, and its implementation in six related applications representing different aspects of IC packages and electronics-enabled systems is elaborated on. Finally, the present relevance, challenges, and future scope of the Digital Twin technology are discussed.

articleTitle: Reducing Wind-Induced Noise in Millimeter-Wave Radar Point Cloud Data to Enhance Accuracy in Human Motion Monitoring
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar systems operate by transmitting and receiving electromagnetic signals within the millimeter-wave spectrum, utilizing the Doppler effect to determine the distance, velocity, and angle of target objects. Due to their high resolution and strong penetration capabilities over limited ranges, millimeter-wave radars are widely used for non-contact health monitoring. However, in indoor environments, wind can introduce noise into the point cloud signals, affecting the accuracy of human motion recognition. This study aims to mitigate wind-induced noise in millimeter-wave radar point cloud data. The research begins by simulating the impact of wind on human motion across diverse scenarios. By controlling wind volume and direction, point cloud data of humans in different states will be collected, and motion point cloud data in windless conditions will be gathered for comparative analysis. The point cloud data will then undergo preprocessing, including filtering, clustering, and voxel grid filtering methods. A transformer model will be employed to identify and attenuate wind noise features, with results compared against data obtained under windless conditions. Metrics such as recognition accuracy, changes in signal-to-noise ratio, and point cloud density variations will be recorded to evaluate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Dimensionality Reduction with Adaptive Neighbors for Intellgent Agriculture
abstract: In the intelligent agriculture, the popularity of high-dimensional data highlights the importance of dimensionality reduction algorithms. However, Traditional methods struggle with graph quality. The new semi supervised adaptive neighbor dimension reduction (SAN) algorithm addresses this limitation by seamlessly integrating dimension reduction and graph learning within the label propagation framework. SAN simultaneously learns the projection matrix and refines the graph structure to promote mutual enhancement between the two. Extensive experiments conducted on five different datasets have shown that SAN surpasses current state-of-the-art methods and provides a powerful solution for processing complex high-dimensional data in smart agriculture applications.

articleTitle: Negative Bidirectional Distillation Model based on Self-Supervised Learning
abstract: Knowledge distillation techniques have shown significant potential in the challenging field of unsupervised anomaly detection (AD). The difference in anomaly representation in teacher-student (T-S) models provides crucial insights for AD research, but several core issues remain in practical applications. First, the limited samples make it difficult for traditional techniques to learn abundant, generalizable representations. Second, due to the lack of direct involvement of anomaly samples, it’s difficult for the model to learn discriminative features that effectively distinguish between normal and abnormal samples. Furthermore, using similar or identical architectures in T-S models might limit the diversity of anomaly representation, making it difficult for the model to build a stable decision boundary to accurately distinguish anomalies. To address these challenges, we propose the NBDM (Negative Bidirectional Distillation Model) method, which adopts a bidirectional distillation architecture combined with self-supervised learning and simulated anomaly strategies to distill the pre-trained teacher network’s feature extraction capability on normal samples. Meanwhile, NBDM introduces a negative learning mechanism that restricts the model’s handling of anomalies, reducing the adverse impact of anomaly features on model performance. Experimental results on the MVTec unsupervised anomaly detection benchmark dataset show that NBDM achieves significant performance improvement over existing methods, demonstrating stronger competitiveness and advantages.

articleTitle: Interpretable Dual-Branch Network with Multi-Modal Multi-Prototype Attributes for Dynamic Region-Based Zero Shot Learning
abstract: Zero shot learning (ZSL) leverages shared attributes to transfer knowledge between seen and unseen classes, enabling the recognition of novel classes. Most existing ZSL models correlate global image features with attributes, leaving the potential of correspondence between image patches and attributes underexplored. In this paper, we propose an interpretable dual-branch framework that elucidates the visual cues for mapping images to attributes. One branch is a traditional semantic embedding branch, aggregating image features and mapping them into the semantic space of attributes. The other branch is an interpretable branch, responsible for extracting features related to each attribute within dynamic regions of the image. The interpretable branch then compares the extracted features with multiple multimodal prototypes of each attribute to predict attribute scores. Additionally, the crossbranch interaction can refine and enhance the performance of the semantic embedding branch. Experiments on multiple ZSL datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework not only provides rich and human-understandable interpretability for the reasoning process, but also achieves comparable performance to other methods without fine-tuning the backbone. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to explore constructing multiple prototypes for a single attribute and directly performing zero shot classification based on the prototype network.

articleTitle: Advanced Liveness Detection for Facial Recognition: Combating Fake Faces with Reflectivity Analysis
abstract: Facial recognition technology has become integral to daily life, facilitating processes such as online payments, smart door locks, and mobile phone unlocking, while enhancing security. However, its accuracy can be compromised by variations in illumination and action scale, making it vulnerable to high-fidelity fake face attacks. This project addresses these issues by identifying the differing reflectivity of human skin, video images, and fake face headgear under light. Utilizing spatio-temporal domain characteristics of facial key points, a novel face action liveness detection algorithm was developed. This algorithm integrates motion trajectory, historical data, and skin color information to improve liveness detection. The project processes facial video to extract reflective layers at key points, using this data to train a model capable of distinguishing real faces from fake ones, thereby improving the robustness of facial recognition systems.

articleTitle: Mask Refinement with Reverse Attention for Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Automatic segmentation in medical image plays a significant role in improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic planning. Although fully supervised deep learning models perform well, they require extensive annotated data for training, which can be challenging to acquire. In contrast, fewshot semantic segmentation provides a solution by leveraging a few labeled examples to make predictions for new and unseen classes. Current leading strategies for few-shot medical image segmentation perform segmentation using multiple or optimized prototypes. However, due to the anatomical variability of medical images, prototype representations are limited, leading to blurred prediction boundaries. In this study, we present a novel few-shot medical image segmentation framework with a High-level Feature Aggregation (HFA) module to enhance feature discriminability and a series of Reverse Attention (RA) modules for mask refinement. Specifically, the HFA module densely aggregates multi-scale high-level features to enrich feature information. The RA modules iteratively refine the segmentation masks by delineating the association between the target regions and boundaries, thereby rectifying incorrect predictions. Furthermore, we introduce Connected region-based Pseudo-label Preprocessing (CPP) to augment the quality of the pseudo-label used for training. Our approach surpasses current leading methods across three public medical image datasets, delivering higher accuracy and precision in segmentation.

articleTitle: Discriminative and Semantic Reinforcement Learning for Domain Adaptation
abstract: Domain adaptation algorithms aim to align distributions of source and target domains in subspace, thereby improving model generalization on the target domain. Unfortunately, this process faces two main challenges: a) Errors in pseudo-labels mislead discriminative learning; and b) Due to the lack of guidance of label correlation, the features learned in the subspace cannot accurately reflect the original structure of the data. To tackle these challenges, we propose a domain adaptation approach called Discriminative and Semantic Reinforcement Learning (DSRL). DSRL consists of two methods, i.e., Reliable Discriminative Learning (RDL), and Semantic Reinforcement Learning (SRL). RDL calculates the strength of discriminative learning based on soft labels. SRL learns label correlation through self-representation and adjusts the geometric similarity of samples based on that correlation. Our experiments demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance on multiple domain adaptation datasets.

articleTitle: Learning Inverse Dynamics of Multi-segmented Larval Crawling Neuromechanics
abstract: Neuromechanical modeling that bridges neural activity and locomotion patterns is essential for studying locomotion control. The Drosophila larva, with its diverse softbodied locomotion, serves as an ideal subject for biomimetic research. Constructing a neuromechanical model of Drosophila larvae presents two primary challenges: efficiently simulating the larva’s soft, multi-segmented body and controlling locomotion within a large action space by actuating muscle groups. This work presents a three-dimensional neuromechanical model of the larva and introduces an inverse dynamics learning method for locomotion control. Our approach efficiently simulates the larva’s multi-segmented, deformable body by integrating computational modules for soft tissues, muscles, and friction. We employ a parameterized controller to reproduce peristaltic waves and use a hybrid artificial neural network architecture to learn inverse dynamics from partially observed states. Balancing biological interpretability with modeling complexity, this model advances the understanding of brain-body-environment interactions in Drosophila larvae, contributing to nature-inspired intelligent systems research.

articleTitle: FSPB: Filtered Semantic Paths and BERT for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Currently, the field of Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) faces the challenge of not being able to effectively handle the new entities in inductive scenarios. With the development of pre-training language models (PLMs), many researchers have attempted to use PLMs for inductive scenarios KGC and have achieved excellent results. However, these efforts often use extra information that is too redundant. In addition, the semantic information of knowledge graphs (KGs) is significantly different from ordinary natural language sentences, which makes the use of PLMs for processing KGC tasks unsatisfactory. In this paper, we propose a new model called FSPB (Filtered Semantic Path BERT), which filters out redundant information by selecting paths with high relevance to triple and design a Knowledge Semantic Masking Prediction Module tailored to the semantics of KGs combined with comparative learning. FSPB improves the model’s ability to handle new entities and relations in an inductive scenario, in addition to improving ranking performance in the link prediction task. We conducted experiments under both transductive and inductive scenarios on several datasets, and the results show that FSPB outperforms existing state-of-the-art KGC methods on MRR and hit@1.

articleTitle: I Can See Your Secrets, A Way to Recognize User Pin Codes by Surveillance Camera
abstract: Surveillance cameras are currently widely used in public and private places to enhance area security and reduce crime rates. However, the extensive use of surveillance cameras also poses significant threats, particularly concerning the leakage of users’ private information. Surveillance cameras are often installed in the corners of areas such as hotel front desks, supermarket checkout areas, or ticket offices to observe user behavior, which can lead to shoulder-surfing attacks. In these public or private settings, when users input their personal identification number (PIN) for unlocking or payment, this process may be intentionally or unintentionally exposed and recorded. If the PIN is compromised, it can result in severe privacy breaches and financial losses for users. Existing work primarily focuses on dedicated handheld recording devices such as cameras and smartphones, lacking discussion on public surveillance cameras. In this paper, we first present an attack model for such scenarios. Based on this model, we design and implement an automated attack system for PIN recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed attack model is both feasible and effective, achieving $90 \%$ accuracy with our system. Finally, we urge users, smartphone manufacturers, and surveillance camera manufacturers to be aware of this attack vector to prevent further harm.

articleTitle: An Information-Augmented Approach for Graph Similarity Computation
abstract: Graph similarity computation is a critical task in various fields, including bioinformatics, social network analysis, and pattern recognition. Traditional methods, such as Graph Edit Distance, face challenges in computational complexity and accuracy. In this paper, we propose IASim, a method for computing graph similarity with information enhancement, leveraging Graph Neural Networks to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of graph similarity computation. IASim incorporates edge information and multi-level node information into the graph embedding process, utilizing a multi-layer neural tensor network architecture and a novel attention mechanism to capture the intricate relationships between nodes and edges. Our experiments on three diverse real datasets demonstrate that IASim outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency, exhibiting outstanding robustness and stability across a range of embedding dimensions. IASim emerges as a promising tool for a variety of applications demanding graph similarity computations.

articleTitle: Ensemble based unsupervised anomaly detection with concept drift adaptation for time series data
abstract: Anomaly detection is the identification of instances that substantially deviate from the majority of the data and do not conform to a well-defined normal behavior. Investigating time series anomalies has become increasingly popular in recent years due to widely deployed IoT devices and sensors. Although most existing methods apply image anomaly detection algorithms directly on time series and commonly assume the data is IID (independent and identically distributed). However, in most realworld applications, the underlying data distribution alters over time. Changes in data over time are referred to as concept drift and can significantly degrade the efficacy of an anomaly detection model. Existing research also indicates that the majority of anomaly detection frameworks ignored concept drift, resulting in poor long-term model performance. This paper presents an ensemble-based, unsupervised anomaly detection framework that is adaptive to the concept drift in time series data. Both distribution and performance-based techniques are used to detect concept drift and update the model to ensure the framework’s longterm performance reliability. The proposed method is evaluated using a real-world univariate time series data that captures sea surface temperature data over a 2 -year period. By comparing our proposed framework to other state-of-the-art algorithms, we demonstrate our proposed method has obvious benefits in accuracy and long-term stability.

articleTitle: Traffic Prediction Approach based on Deep Learning for Heterogeneous Communication Networks
abstract: Heterogeneous communication networks have gained increasing attention for integrating complementary communication technologies, thereby enhancing network performance in complex scenarios, such as multi-domain air-sea-underwater communication networks. Accurate traffic prediction can introduce several new possibilities for enhancing Quality of Service (QoS) in future multi-domain communication networks. However, previous traffic prediction methods have primarily focused on homogeneous communication networks, with almost no research addressing traffic prediction in heterogeneous communication networks. Additionally, there is currently no simulation or experimental dataset available for heterogeneous radio-acoustic-optical communication networks. To fill this gap and advance traffic prediction research, this study simulates multi-domain communication nodes, links, and networks using the NS-3 simulation platform and constructs a novel dataset for heterogeneous radio-acoustic-optical communication networks. This paper proposes an intelligent traffic prediction approach based on LSTM, GRU, and Transformer models to forecast future traffic values from historical traffic time series. Furthermore, we optimized the link adaptive loss function to effectively address challenges caused by link rate differences and traffic imbalance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed prediction approach performs well on evaluation metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE).

articleTitle: A Lightweight Transformer-Based Model for Efficient Industrial Fault Diagnosis
abstract: The complexity of industrial systems has triggered an ever-increasing demand for accurate fault diagnosis. However, traditional methods are typically unreliable, particularly in scenarios with limited data. This paper proposes the Separable Multi-Scale Convolutional MLP Network (SMCMN), a lightweight fault diagnosis framework designed to address the challenges of deploying complex Transformer models in resource-constrained environments. The SMCMN framework reduces the complexity associated with the Transformer’s multi-head self-attention mechanisms and traditional CNN cross-channel convolution by redesigning the Multi-Scale Separable Convolution (MSSC) block. This block incorporates large kernel sizes and dropout layers to enhance accuracy. Furthermore, the framework replaces conventional attention mechanisms with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) layer, thereby reducing model complexity. Extensive testing across two diverse datasets has demonstrated that the SMCMN framework exhibits superior robustness and performance, proving to be an effective solution for fault diagnosis in practical applications, even under varying noise levels.

articleTitle: Multi-Level Feature Calibration for Adversarial Training Against Attack
abstract: While excelling in various vision tasks, deep neural networks remain vulnerable to adversarial samples, which cause erroneous predictions with minor input perturbations. In this work, we reveal the differences in feature mapping between adversarial and natural examples and propose a Multi-Level Feature Calibration (MLFC) training method based on this insight. We introduce a fine-grained calibration module that utilizes gradient information to adaptively adjust feature representations in the latent space. By calibrating features at multiple levels, the model achieves a more stable and accurate representation of the input data. Additionally, the objective function not only maximizes the confidence of each sample’s target label but also incorporates a central metric loss to promote feature distributions with high inter-class separation. This loss faithfully reflects the ground distance between samples through the angular distance measure, which further mitigates the differences in the sample feature distributions. Experimental results from various white-box and black-box attack scenarios demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in enhancing model robustness and generalization ability. Specifically, MLFC improves the robustness of existing adversarial training methods under PGD attacks by ${3. 3 \%}$ on CIFAR-10 and ${3. 8 8 \%}$ on CIFAR-100.

articleTitle: VG-Net: Sensor Time Series Anomaly Detection with Joint Variational Autoencoder and Graph Neural Network
abstract: Intelligent Cyber-Physical Systems typically utilize sensors to gather a significant amount of raw data which often possesses temporal and high-dimensional characteristics. Ensuring the data reliability is crucial for the normal operation of the system. While most existing methods are capable of identifying anomalies in high-dimensional time series data from sensors, they often lack adequate accuracy and fail to adequately consider the correlation between sensor nodes. To address these limitations, we propose an unsupervised framework which is a combination of variational autoencoder and graph neural network(VG-Net). By jointly optimizing the reconstruction module and the prediction module, VG-Net effectively models the correlation between sensor nodes while simultaneously detecting anomalies. The reconstruction module is responsible for modeling the latent representation space and reconstructing the time series data through variational autoencoder. The prediction module leverages bidirectional long short term memory networks and neural tensor network to learn the relationships between sensor nodes, and uses graph neural network to predict the future behavior of the data. Experiments on eight real and synthetic datasets demonstrate that, compared with existing methods, VG-Net can accurately model the relationship between sensor nodes and enhance the anomaly detection performance of high-dimensional time series data.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Goal Decomposition Decision Model for Satellite Tracking with Noncooperative Ground-Based Equipment
abstract: The proliferation of nongeostationary orbit (NGSO) satellites necessitates innovative tracking solutions for noncooperative satellite observation and signal detection. This study introduces an adaptive goal decomposition decision model that integrates adaptive calibration, goal decomposition, and strategic decision-making to optimize tracking precision and ensure the orbital safety of various satellite constellations. The model self-calibrates orbital parameters using ephemeris data, employs four objective functions for conflict-free optimization, and identifies optimal tracking strategies based on specific criteria defined by five metrics. Demonstrating robustness across diverse NGSO scenarios, the model significantly boosts ephemeris calculation efficiency, surpassing traditional methods. For Starlink, prioritizing angular coverage during satellite passes increases overall performance by $21.63 \%$, and tracking numbers by $\mathbf{1 8 . 1 8 \%}$, compared to the least effective objective function that solely resolves time conflicts. For OneWeb, balancing pass duration and angular coverage optimizes performance, resulting in a $27.55 \%$ enhancement in efficiency and an $\mathbf{8 0 0 . 0 0 \%}$ increase in tracked satellites than the least effective small-angle-switching objective.

articleTitle: CLNet: A Federated Learning Approach for Privacy-aware Cognitive Load Evaluation while Walking Using Smart Shoes
abstract: Cognitive load while walking plays a role in safety, human-computer interaction, medicine, and other fields, and gait has been shown to have a robust connection with cognitive load. However, most studies on this issue only focus on controlled laboratory or clinical settings. Also, data privacy is not considered in the process. We propose a method based on smart shoes with multiple modalities and a federated learning approach that could evaluate cognitive load during walking in real-world scenarios. In our study, the classical N-back tasks are utilized, and the NASA-TLX questionnaire is used as ground truth. Our pipeline demonstrates utility in cognitive load evaluation while walking in the wild, with an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9 . 1 6 \%}$. Our method provides a potential way to perform in-wild cognitive load evaluation in a user-friendly manner, which could be useful in various applications, especially in privacy-sensitive domains.

articleTitle: An Algorithm Combining Deep Reinforcement Learning and Dynamic Programming for Solving TSP-D
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles serve as versatile terminal devices applicable across various scenarios, involving the coordination among humans, drones, and the environment. This integration represents a typical application of the fusion development of ‘human-machine-environment’. The outstanding performance exhibited by UAVs enables their application in traditional truck delivery systems. However, effectively integrating truck and drone route planning poses a new challenge, known as the Traveling Salesman Problem with Drone (TSP-D). The current algorithm only focuses on TSP-D instances where the number of truck nodes is smaller than or equal to the number of drone nodes. Therefore, we decompose the TSP-D problem into two parts: path point planning and path generation, proposing a two-stage solution algorithm that combines deep reinforcement learning and dynamic programming. Firstly, by designing a novel reward function, we employ reinforcement learning algorithms to train pointer networks to generate the sequence of path points for trucks and drones. Subsequently, dynamic programming is used to collaboratively plan accurate paths for trucks and drones by coordinating their path points. This paper demonstrated the feasibility of the algorithm in experiments with 11, 21, and 51 nodes. The results indicate that as the number of visiting nodes increases, the drone’s flight distance gradually exceeds the truck’s driving distance. This further confirms that the drone can effectively become the main force in the task, significantly reducing the operational time of TSP-D.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Ship Detection in SAR Images Based on Fusion of Statistical and Structural Features
abstract: SAR Ship detection plays an important role in ocean monitoring. For deep learning-based detection methods, it often requires a large number of accurate target-level annotations, which are usually hard to obtain. In this paper, an unsupervised ship target detection method based on fusion of statistical and structural features is proposed to deal with unlabeled synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image data. An iterative optimization detection strategy is developed to improve the accuracy of the parameter estimation of the gamma distribution statistical model in the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector. First, a large number of bounding boxes with false alarms are obtained with CFAR detector. Then, the knowledge distillation model is designed to increase the inter class gap between the clutter and target in the bounding boxes. The soft label information provided by the CFAR detector is employed to constrain the training of the Faster-RCNN detector. The bounding boxes generated by FasterRCNN serve as adaptive detection units within CFAR detector. After several iterations, the CFAR detector and the deep network detector are mutually optimized. The iteration is stopped when the total detection rate of the target and clutter falls below a preset threshold. Finally, the optimized Faster-RCNN detector model is used for target detection of other SAR image data. The effectiveness of the proposed method on SAR ship detection is demonstrated by some experiments with real SAR images datasets without annotations.

articleTitle: Improving 3D Human Body Reconstruction Using Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based Kansformer
abstract: As the unique advantages of millimeter wave (mmWave) radar technology in handling complex environments become increasingly apparent, research into constructing 3D human models using mmWave radar has received extensive attention. Capable of operating effectively in adverse conditions such as smoke, snow, and poor lighting, mmWave radar holds significant potential for applications in emergency response and security monitoring. This paper investigates the possibility of reconstructing accurate 3D skeletons or mesh models by analyzing noisy and sparse radar signals. Moreover, addressing the issues of large parameter size and long training periods inherent in traditional Transformer models, this study employs an optimized Kolmogorov-Arnold Network(KAN) [1] structure to enhance the Transformer model, which called Kansformer. This structural optimization significantly reduces the model’s parameter count and improves its learning efficiency and generalizability across different scenes. The results demonstrate that the optimized model exhibits higher robustness and accuracy in mmWave human body reconstruction tasks, especially in visually obstructed environments.

articleTitle: Optimization of Intelligent Reflecting Surface Dimensions under Partial Blockages
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) can eliminate dead zones by creating alternative paths for radio propagation. However, in environments with numerous moving obstacles, the aperture of the IRS may become partially obstructed, reducing the effective area and consequently, the gain of the IRS. Although increasing the aperture size of the IRS can mitigate the impact of obstacles, the possible installation area is limited owing to location and cost constraints. Therefore, this study proposes a method to optimally design the installation area of the IRS by considering spatial characteristics, such as the size and density of obstacles. Based on numerical analysis, moving obstacles should be considered to effectively determine the IRS installation strategy. This study contributes to the construction of communication areas in environments with numerous obstacles, such as smart factories, offices, and warehouses.

articleTitle: Stable Task Assignment for Socially Aware Collective Computing Systems
abstract: Collective Computing is the latest generation of computing paradigm that has received a lot of attention recently. One of the important things in Collective Computing systems is how to assign tasks to human participants. When doing the assignment, the platform may face the challenge of inadequate availability of skilled workers. To deal with this challenge, some researchers leverage the property that workers are socially aware and consider assigning tasks to workers with the assistance of social networks. However, the objectives of task requesters and workers can conflict and may result in unstable assignments due to unhappy requesters and workers, which is ignored by most of these works. This paper leverages the influence propagation on the social network to assist task assignment and takes requesters’ preferences and workers’ preferences into consideration. Stable Matching Theory is leveraged to solve the problem of matching tasks with seed workers and an efficient task assignment algorithm is proposed. Through extensive simulations, the performance of the proposed algorithm is evaluated in different settings. Empirical studies show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the baseline algorithms in achieving stability and system efficiency.

articleTitle: Maritime target intent recognition based on Transformer
abstract: Maritime target intent recognition refers to the process of inferring the intent and objectives of maritime targets through the analysis of their behavior, movement trajectories, and communications. This recognition is crucial for maritime security and defense. Currently, many methods for inferring tactical intent employ recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and their variants. However, due to the relatively slow movement of maritime targets, similar patterns may be observed over short time sequences, necessitating a longer duration to accurately reflect the target’s intent. RNNs tend to suffer from memory degradation on long-sequence data, leading to the loss of early data and a decline in the accuracy of intent recognition for maritime targets. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Transformer-based intent recognition model, which demonstrates improved capability for capturing long-term dependencies and effectively mitigates long-term memory degradation. The efficacy of the proposed model is validated through comparative experiments on a maritime dataset obtained from simulations.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Embedding via Delicate Negative Sampling and Efficient Biased Learning
abstract: Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) plays a dominant role in the study of Knowledge Graph (KG). Although KGE has received special concern in recent years, it is still in its infancy and many reported publications have some obvious drawbacks. For instance, the scoring function is usually defined in a rough way, inevitably degrading the precision of the entity embedding. Besides, negative sampling in KGE is somewhat conservative since it has not taken the data distribution into account. To address these issues, in this paper, a novel KGE via Delicate Negative Sampling and Efficient Biased Learning (DNS-EBL) is put forward. The proposed DNS-EBL has the following three obvious advantages: 1) concerning the limited capacity of extracting the latent relation between entities, the bias is introduced to the scoring function, thereby enlarging the solution space to improve the quality of embedding; 2) Gaussian noises with the known distribution are injected into KGE to make good use of the statistical character of data and reduce the risk of overfitting; and 3) a dynamic clustering method is adopted to establish inter- and intra- clusters for entities so that negative samples with high-quality can be selected during embedding. Finally, experimental results on three datasets: FB15k, WN18 and WN18RR demonstrate the superiority of DNS-EBL in accomplishing the KG Completion task over some state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: LRBEAL: Learning Representation of Behaviors Extracted from Audit Logs
abstract: Audit logs provide data support for intrusion detection and attack investigation. However, these logs are fine-grained, large-scale, and there is a semantic gap between them and user behaviors. This poses challenges for security analysts to identify behaviors and discover abnormal activities. Existing methods abstract user behavior through the information flow between system entities, and perform representation learning and clustering analysis to bridge the semantic gap between logs and behaviors. However, challenges remain in effectively extracting and representing behavior. In this paper, we propose LRBEAL, a framework for behavior analysis based on audit logs. LRBEAL aims to extract behaviors from logs, denoise, represent the behaviors, and identify anomalous behaviors. We design a denoising method specifically for behavior instances, which filters logs by analyzing the correlation between logs and behaviors in order to construct concise and effective behavior instances. Additionally, we propose a behavior representation method based on temporal and semantic analysis, using semi-supervised and contrastive learning to learn semantics in behavior instances under the guidance of the semantics contained in the command lines. Finally, we use DBSCAN to cluster behavior instances and detection anomalous behaviors. We evaluated LRBEAL on DARPA, and the results shows that LRBEAL effectively identifies user behavior and performs well in both behavior identification and anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Time Series Data Prediction Using CNN-BiLSTM based Attention-KAN Model
abstract: Time series refers to a sequence of data points arranged in chronological order, typically used to represent the trend of a variable over time. These data points can be continuous, such as hourly temperature records, or discrete, such as annual demographic statistics. Precise time series prediction plays a pivotal role in many areas, for instance, the domain of natural language processing. However, achieving precise predictions for time series data remains challenging. The methods encompass traditional machine learning algorithms, such as Random Forests (RF), as well as recent advancements in deep learning, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), along with various improvements of these neural networks. While these approaches have achieved favorable results in practical time series forecasting applications, they still exhibit some limitations. This paper proposes a hybrid network to improve the accuracy of time series training and prediction. The network is based on one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1DCNN), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), dual-head attention mechanisms, and the novel Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN). The model is subsequently applied to the preprocessing, training, and testing of stock price trends as a time series. Comparative analysis with existing CNN-LSTM time series prediction models demonstrates that the proposed CNN-LSTM-KAN hybrid approach achieves improvements in fitting degree, RMSE, R2, and accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhancing UAV Coverage Path Planning via Deep Reinforcement learning with Intrinsic Curiosity
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are widely used in various fields due to their agility and versatility, but their limited energy supply necessitates efficient Coverage Path Planning (CPP). Traditional CPP methods are effective in structured environments but often fall short in more complex scenarios. This paper proposes a novel approach integrating advanced reinforcement learning techniques to enhance UAV path planning. Our method combines Double Deep Q-Networks (DDQN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to improve decision-making and temporal information processing capabilities. Additionally, we incorporate an Intrinsic Curiosity Module (ICM) to drive exploration and Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) to focus on high-value experiences, accelerating learning and enhancing performance. The proposed framework demonstrates superior coverage efficiency and adaptability in simulations, achieving higher coverage ratios and reduced redundant paths compared to traditional methods. These innovations provide a robust and flexible solution for autonomous UAV navigation, offering a solid foundation for future research in CPP optimization.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Clustering Method for Maximizing Energy Efficiency in C-V2X Metaverse
abstract: The Metaverse can leverage intelligent traffic management technology to simulate the Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (C-V2X) environment, integrating closely with the Internet of Vehicles due to its advanced connectivity and real-time data processing capabilities. These features make it possible to create a smart transportation system that closely mirrors the real world. Dynamic clustering is an effective network management method for handling the large number of mobile vehicles within the Metaverse, particularly in emergency scenarios where base stations (BSs) may fail. However, frequent changes in network topology due to high-speed vehicles result in unstable clusters and low communication efficiency. In this study, a dynamic clustering algorithm based on motion vector similarity (DA-MVS) is proposed for constructing stable clusters, and an adaptive adjustment clusters strategy is presented based on the change rate of vehicle numbers to improve energy efficiency (EE). Furthermore, we propose an elite chaotic perturbed sparrow search algorithm (ECPSSA) to optimize the EE of the C-V2X. Compared to the multiple baseline algorithm, the successful transmission rate can be improved by up to 76.9%, and the EE is enhanced by 20.97%.

articleTitle: SCDet: Scale-aware and Context-rich Feature Fusion Network for Traffic Sign Detection
abstract: With the rise of deep learning technology, traffic sign detection has made great progress. However, due to the diversity and complexity of the collected high-resolution images, detecting small, multi-scale, and easily obscured traffic signs in real-world scenarios still presents a persistent challenge. Aiming at this problem, a new traffic sign detection network, Scale-aware and Context-rich Traffic Sign Detection Network (SCDet) is proposed, which learns scale-aware and context-rich features. Specifically, the network constructs a backbone network Multi-Scale Deep Residual Network(MSNet) firstly, and we replace the ordinary convolution in the backbone with a dilated convolution module, where different sensory fields acquired by different layers help to acquire multi-scale contextual information, thus facilitating the detection of multi-scale objects in traffic signs. Secondly, to suppress the effect of scale variation, we replace the nearest neighbour interpolation in Feature Pyramid Network(FPN) with Content-Aware ReAssembly of Features(CARAFE), which performs multi-scale fusion based on scale-aware and context-rich representation. Moreover, to solve the problem of data imbalance between different classes, a method called configurable dynamic data expansion is proposed. Our approach has been extensively evaluated on two public traffic sign datasets through extensive experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority over several state-of-the-art approaches.

articleTitle: Personalized Differential Privacy Federated Learning Model for Internet of Vehicles
abstract: To solve the issue of the differential privacy protection mechanism in federated learning (FL) for Internet of Vehicles (IoV), which only focuses on fixed privacy budget allocation methods and ignores the dynamic allocation of privacy budgets based on the risk of user data privacy leakage, this paper proposes a personalized differential privacy federated learning model based on privacy metrics. In each round of federated training, vehicle nodes simulate membership inference attacks to measure the performance of the attack model using confidence metrics. The attack results are then transformed into privacy risk scores, quantifying the degree of privacy leakage of the training nodes. Subsequently, the vehicle nodes establish a multilevel privacy budget allocation method, allowing users to adjust the magnitude of noise added to the model parameters based on the privacy risk level before uploading. This enables users to achieve dynamic protection during the federated learning training phase. Experimental results show that the personalized differential privacy algorithm based on privacy metrics improves the accuracy of the model compared to the method of uniformly setting the privacy budget.

articleTitle: Elevating Vision Transformer Performance: The KAN-VIT Model for Image Recognition
abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative image recognition model called KAN-VIT, which applies the Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) architecture to the Vision Transformer (VIT), replacing the traditional multilayer perceptron (MLP) layers and the MLP head at the output. KANs are neural networks based on the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, which introduces learnable activation functions between nodes, parameterized by spline functions, thereby providing higher accuracy and interpretability. Based on this, the VIT model was improved by replacing the original MLP layers with KANs, and experiments were conducted on the CIFAR-10, Oxford Flowers, and MNIST datasets. The results show that the improved model has demonstrated superior performance on the test datasets. We also analyzed the interpretability of KANs, and the results show that the improved model not only has improved performance but also has advantages in the visualization and interpretability of the model.

articleTitle: A Residual Graph Convolutional Network Algorithm Based on Unfolded WMMSE for Power Allocation
abstract: Optimal power allocation is pivotal for enhancing network capacity and performance in wireless networks. To tackle the challenges posed by the high computational complexity of traditional algorithms and the limited interpretability and generalization of deep learning-based methods, inspired by the principles of deep unfolding and graph neural networks (GNNs), we propose a novel weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) unfolding-based residual graph convolutional network architecture (UWMMSE-RGCN). Specifically, our method unfolds the WMMSE algorithm, maintaining the iterative structure of WMMSE, and utilize GNNs to learn the key iterative variables of WMMSE to approximate the complex computational steps of the iterative variables. The methodology aims to capitalize on domain knowledge while achieve exceptional performance and computational efficiency. Additionally, we have developed a residual graph convolutional network (RGCN) by integrating residual connection into the GNNs. This design promotes the integration of features across diverse neighborhood scopes of nodes, thereby bolstering the architecture’s generalization performance. Theoretical analysis confirms the permutation equivariance of our method, which ensures its generalization to different network topologies. Experiments validate that the proposed unfolded architecture surpasses other deep unfolding algorithms in terms of performance and generalization. It demonstrates potential for scalability to larger network sizes and adaptability to diverse channel conditions.

articleTitle: Using Blockchain and Proxy Re-Encryption to Achieve the Anonymously and Reliable Data Secure Sharing
abstract: In the process of multi-party data transactions, there are multiple challenges including ownership confirmation, transaction supervision, and privacy protection. The current researches mainly focus on relevant security protocols and access control methods. However, existing technologies are not well suited to meet the critical needs of security and efficiency in large-scale data trading markets. Therefore, this paper introduces revocable ring signatures, proxy re-encryption, and one-time address techniques to design an anonymous Controllable data security transaction scheme that protects user privacy while securing the system and still provides dynamic control of data access. In terms of secure transactions, this scheme can control the time overhead of the data encryption and decryption phases within 6 ms and 3 ms respectively, and not insensitive to the size of the transaction data plaintext. When the number of ring members reaches 50, the longest time-consuming transaction request stage also runs within 180 ms, demonstrating strong usability in various scenarios. Security analysis and performance experiments show that this scheme can securely and efficiently solve the problems of data sharing.

articleTitle: An Intelligence Energy Consumption Model based on CNN-LSTM Neural Network in the Data Centers*
abstract: Constructing an accurate energy consumption model can obtain server energy consumption in real-time and optimize data center energy consumption for resource providers. Considering the “low precision problem” of the current server energy consumption model, a real-time server energy-consumption prediction method combining the “Spearman correlation coefficient” and CNN-LSTM neural network is proposed. Under four different workloads, the “Spearman correlation coefficient” method selects the characteristic parameters strongly correlated with energy consumption as model input. The CNN-LSTM neural network is leveraged to construct the server energy consumption model. Many experiments have been conducted using real datasets to verify the effectiveness of the proposed model. The test data indicates that, in contrast to the CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) model, LSTM (Long and Short Term Memory Network) model, and MLP (Multi-layer Perceptron) model, the mean absolute error and root mean square error of the CNNLSTM model are reduced by 1.1 and 1.5, respectively. In addition, the CNN-LSTM model has higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Cost and QoS-Aware Service Migration in Vehicular Edge Computing Networks with Limited Backhaul Capacity
abstract: Vehicular edge computing (VEC) is a key enabler for providing low-latency vehicular service, by deploying the services at the edge servers associated with wireless nodes distributed in vehicle networks. Due to limited coverage of wireless nodes and high vehicle mobility, vehicular services need to be adaptively migrated over the backhaul network to follow the vehicles. Given an ever-increasing amount of vehicles served by finite backhaul bandwidth, the backhaul network can become the bottleneck for timely service migration. However, few studies on service migration considered optimizing the utilization of backhaul network bandwidth to alleviate such bottleneck. In this study, we focus on the service migration problem in VECenabled small cell networks with distributed wireless backhaul. Specifically, we formulate the service migration in VEC networks as an optimization problem with the objective of minimizing the migration cost while guaranteeing the desired quality of service (QoS), taking into account the limited time, bandwidth resource, and computation capacity. We develop an efficient service migration algorithm, called OMELET, which dynamically makes service migration decisions based on Lyapunov technique via jointly optimizing migration decision, path selection and rate allocation. Simulation results validate that OMELET can achieve a more effective trade-off between migration cost and QoS guarantee compared with the state-of-the-art service migration schemes.

articleTitle: Verifiable, Access-Controllable, and Privacy-Preserving Multidimensional Data Aggregation based on Blockchain in Smart Grids
abstract: With the development of the smart grids, terminal devices collect fine-grained sensitive data from users and achieve personalized functions. A large amount of data is sent to the control center to meet the needs of electric power departments (EPDs) for conducting big data analysis, optimizing energy usage efficiency, and real-time pricing. However, in smart grids, safe-guarding user privacy confronts significant challenges, including unclear permission management that allows any EPD to access all data. To address these issues, we propose a blockchain-based multidimensional data aggregation scheme for data privacy protection and access control in smart grids. With modified Paillier cryptosystem, a multidimensional data aggregation scheme is proposed using superincreasing sequences. The access control of EPDs is achieved with attribute-based encryption (ABE). The requests of EPDs are recorded by the blockchain. Security analysis shows that multiple attacks can be resisted by the proposal. A comprehensive performance evaluation of the scheme is also conducted to prove its feasibility.

articleTitle: An Edu-Metaverse Service Platform and its Experiments on Physical Education Class in PKU
abstract: In the digital era, it is the only way for high-quality education to integrate the new generation of information technology with traditional education, promote the Digital transformation of education, and build a networked, digital, personalized, lifelong education system. This paper firstly introduces the concepts with Metaverse and its involvement toward Web3.0 as well as Generative AI. Then come with an Edu-Metaverse Service and its impact on the future education. Edu-Metaverse service would effectively support the “student-centered” education model, and drive profound changes in education scenes, education content, roles and responsibilities, teaching evaluation and other aspects. Finally, a pilot practice combine Edu-Metaverse Service platform with Physical Education in Peking University was introduced and some issues were discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Text Classification for Judicial Texts via Dual Graph and Label Feature Fusion
abstract: The legal judgement prediction (LJP) of judicial texts represents a multi-label text classification (MLTC) problem, which in turn involves three distinct tasks: the prediction of charges, legal articles, and terms of penalty. Nevertheless, extant multi-label text classification models tend to eschew the consideration of multiple correlations and semantic information between labels when predicting judicial texts, which may result in the loss of pertinent information. Furthermore, these models do not take full advantage of the local and overall information of the labels in the process of selecting appropriate labels for the text using the multi-head attention mechanism. To address these issues, we propose a new model, BGFLFF, which explores label correlation and semantics among the three tasks by employing Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and multi-head attention mechanisms. In particular, we propose a Bi-Graph Fusion GCN (BGF-GCN), which fuses the co-occurrence matrix of labels with the cosine similarity matrix, thereby fully exploiting the multiple correlations between labels. Furthermore, prior to embedding the tags, the interpretations of the labels are obtained via Google in order to enhance the semantic information between the labels. To further reinforce the interconnections between labels and text and more effectively comprehend the interrelationships between the three tasks, we propose a Multi-Head Label Feature Fusion Attentional Mechanism (MH-LFFAtt), which assigns distinct weights to the pertinent label information in the text by fusing the local and overall features of the labels. The experimental results demonstrate that the F1 score exhibits an improvement of up to ${2. 2 8 \%}$ and a minimum of ${1. 2 9 \%}$ across the various tasks of the two datasets. This evidence substantiates the assertion that BGFLFF outperforms the existing baseline model.

articleTitle: A Label-focused Transformer for Generating Illness-aware Medical Reports
abstract: Automatically generating radiology reports from X-rays holds great potential for simplifying medical processes, minimizing misdiagnosis, and enhancing patient care. Although current studies have enhanced report clarity through advanced computer vision and language generation models, they often fail to capture the subtleties of diseasespecific manifestations, such as the presence and severity of conditions ranging from cardiomegaly to pneumonia, and from pleural effusions to fractures. Furthermore, label imbalance in radiographic datasets can lead to oversight of rare diseases. This paper builds upon the Memory-boosted Transformer model and introduces a specific label-focused radiology method, along with an imbalanced label correct reward. Through this approach, the generated diagnostic text is much closer to the original diagnostic reports. Additionally, the method’s effectiveness is evaluated against current techniques across two public datasets (IU X-Ray and MIMICCXR), showcasing improved clinical accuracy for both frequent and rare conditions without compromising report readability.

articleTitle: Dynamic Segmentation Enhanced Asynchronous Non-linear Federated Learning for Fault Diagnosis Using Incremental Aggregation Mechanism
abstract: To address the challenges of nonlinearity in edge raw data and the absence of real-time feedback in distributed heterogeneous fault diagnosis, we propose a dynamic segmentation enhanced asynchronous federated learning method (FedDSA) utilizing an incremental aggregation mechanism. This methodology incorporates a meta-learning-driven strategy during the segmentation of edge groups (EGs), facilitating dynamic self-organized segmentation across multiple EGs. During the prototype aggregation among EGs, a particle filtering algorithm is integrated to accommodate nonlinear data, thereby enabling asynchronous global prototype aggregation and constructing an adaptive asynchronous incremental aggregation mechanism.
