Ultimately, a hybrid asynchronous federated learning framework based on segmentation across multiple EGs is established. Within the framework, a global prototype generator (GPG) is trained in the cloud, leveraging embedded fault feature prototype representations. Finally, a federated fault diagnosis platform is designed and implemented, with its effectiveness validated through extensive experimental evaluations.

articleTitle: MAPPO based Single-hop Task Offloading with Dynamic Vehicle Prediction in RSU-assisted IoV
abstract: In the realm of Internet of Vehicles (IoV), Roadside Units (RSUs) play a vital role due to their advanced sensing and computing capabilities. They support Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) by enabling real-time data processing and reducing latency and energy consumption. Given the large volume of data and the limited computing capacity of RSUs, tasks are often offloaded to other nodes, such as the cloud, other RSUs, or vehicles. However, due to the environment dynamic caused by vehicle mobility, the set of neighboring nodes for each RSU frequently changes, and variations in neighboring nodes are not perceived timely. In such cases, RSUs need to predict changes in neighboring nodes to ensure effective task offloading. Moreover, since each RSU can only perceive the surrounding environment, it is difficult for a single node to make optimal offloading decisions for each task independently. To address these issues, this paper proposes a distributed task offloading scheme that incorporates vehicle trajectory prediction. First, each RSU uses the vehicle trajectories predicted by the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model to determine neighboring vehicles and update the set of neighboring nodes. Then, to enable each RSU to select a suitable computing node and minimize computation delay and energy consumption for the task, we adopt a distributed approach where each RSU independently makes offloading decisions based on local observations. To achieve this goal, we establish a 01 mathematical model and transform it into a Markov Decision Process (MDP). Subsequently, we propose a solution based on Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO). Through extensive simulation experiments, we demonstrate that the scheme effectively reduces both long-term average processing delay and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Deployment and Offloading Optimization for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network with Improved Differential Evolution Algorithm
abstract: The development of the Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) represents a significant advancement in satellite Internet technology, primarily because it facilitates the provision of pervasive networking solutions for the Internet of Things (IoT). Central to minimizing energy consumption in this context is the strategic deployment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and the efficient offloading of computational tasks. This is due to the fact that the quality of communication between UAVs and ground-based mobile devices is a crucial determinant of both communication latency and energy usage. This study presents an in-depth exploration of a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) framework within a SAGIN context, in which multiple UAVs serve as edge computing servers, thereby accelerating computational services to terrestrial devices. In parallel, Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are leveraged to provide cloud computing services. We introduce a Dual-layer nested joint optimization technique fortified by an improved differential evolution. The outer layer of the algorithm employs a phased differential evolution technique to optimize the positioning of UAVs. Simultaneously, the inner layer adopts a greedy approach to optimize the offloading ratio for computational tasks. The effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed method are substantiated through extensive numerical simulations. Comparative analysis with existing benchmark techniques demonstrates a significant reduction in the energy consumption of the system, underscoring the potential of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Hyperdimensional Computing Empowered Federated Foundation Model over Wireless Networks for Metaverse
abstract: The Metaverse, a burgeoning collective virtual space merging augmented reality and persistent virtual worlds, necessitates advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and communication technologies to support immersive and interactive experiences. Federated learning (FL) has emerged as a promising technique for collaboratively training AI models while preserving data privacy. However, FL faces challenges such as high communication overhead and substantial computational demands, particularly for neural network (NN) models. To address these issues, we propose an integrated federated split learning and hyperdimensional computing (FSL-HDC) framework for emerging foundation models. This novel approach reduces communication costs, computation load, and privacy risks, making it particularly suitable for resource-constrained edge devices in the Metaverse, ensuring real-time responsive interactions. Additionally, we introduce an optimization algorithm that concurrently optimizes transmission power and bandwidth to minimize the maximum transmission time among all users to the server. The simulation results based on the MNIST dataset indicate that FSL-HDC achieves an accuracy rate of approximately 87.5%, which is slightly lower than that of FL-HDC. However, FSL-HDC exhibits a significantly faster convergence speed, approximately 3.733x that of FSL-NN, and demonstrates robustness to non-IID data distributions. Moreover, our proposed optimization algorithm can reduce the maximum transmission time by up to 64% compared with the baseline.

articleTitle: Quadruped Robot Mastering Obstacle Avoidance: Integrating Perception and Decision-making
abstract: Quadruped robots play a critical role in navigating complex environments, where effective perception and obstacle avoidance are paramount. Despite advancements in reinforcement learning for motion control, current research has inadequately addressed the combined challenges of traversable and non-traversable obstacles, lack of ability to combine obstacle avoidance and terrain adaptation. This paper proposes a novel motion control framework for quadruped robots that integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to unify the modeling of both obstacle types, overcoming the limitations of existing methods. Our framework introduces a generalized joint obstacle avoidance strategy, which merges laser sensing and proprioception, to enhance the robot’s perception and navigation capabilities in diverse environments. Experimental results, conducted in both simulated and real-world terrains, demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods in obstacle avoidance performance, underscoring its potential for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Prototype Guided Personalized Federated Intrusion Detection System
abstract: Preventing network attacks and protecting user privacy are consistently hot research topics in the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing fields. Recent advancements in Federated Learning (FL) have shown promise in addressing these challenges. FL allows various clients to collaboratively build an intrusion detection system (IDS) without sharing their private data. However, most existing methods train a single intrusion detection model for all clients and assume that the training and test data distribution are identical, leading to unsatisfactory detection accuracy and generalization abilities in practice. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a prototype-guided personalized FL approach named PG-FedIDS. We propose two novel mechanisms within this method. Firstly, we utilize class prototypes as auxiliary information carriers to generate personalized models for each client, rather than generating a single global model as in previous works. Secondly, we propose a prototype-guided ensemble learning strategy, which can leverage the global knowledge in prototypes to enhance detection accuracy and generalization abilities for each client. We conduct extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets with different evaluation test settings. The results demonstrate that our PG-FedIDS achieves promising detection accuracy and consistently outperforms other FL baselines.

articleTitle: Innovative Sentiment Analysis of Mobile App Review Texts Based on MHA-MLP-Mixer
abstract: The current landscape of the mobile application market unfolds as a rich and diverse tapestry, with developers struggling to meet user demands and distinguish themselves amidst fierce competition; users confront a vast array of applications, each with unique features, posing challenges in accurately aligning with their actual needs. The star rating system, a commonly used evaluation tool in the industry, lacks in-depth interpretation of user comments, leaving developers unable to discern specific user needs and users deprived of nuanced reference information. Despite its crucial role as a key tool for deciphering emotional information in user comments, sentiment analysis technology still grapples with challenges such as its limited capability in extracting emotional features from a singular perspective and inadequate modeling of complex emotional interactions. Hence, this paper introduces a novel deep learning model, the MHA-MLP-Mixer model, specifically designed for sentiment analysis of mobile application review texts. Its innovation lies in integrating local and global text information, focusing on multi-perspective sentiment cues using a multi-head attention mechanism, and modeling deep sentiment interactions through MLP-Mixer. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that the precision, recall, and F1 score of the model all exceed $\mathbf{8 5 \%}$, surpassing the analysis results of other models. This framework contributes to fostering the development of the mobile application market and enhancing user experience.

articleTitle: SAR and Optical Satellite Image Matching Incorporating Category-Supervised Semantic Features*
abstract: The matching of SAR and optical satellite images is a crucial method for addressing the challenge of geolocalization in scenarios where real-time access to optical images is constrained (e.g., darkness, rain, fog, glare, etc.). To enhance the generalization capability of SAR-optical image matching, particularly under varying viewpoints (rotation), this paper presents an augmented Superpoint network architecture. This architecture incorporates semantic segmentation feature representation to facilitate a priori semantic description and to integrate it with the original network’s feature descriptors. This integration is achieved by introducing self-attention and cross-attention layers, which enhance the feature vectors. The experiments demonstrate that, compared to the original architecture, the model reinforces the relationship for commonality matching and significantly increases the number of correctly matched points. Compared with other deep learning methods, including CMMNet and LoFTR, the matching scheme presented in this paper is less time-consuming and more robust with anti-rotation capability.

Author Keywords: Cross modality remote sensing image matching

articleTitle: An Online Learning Prediction System for MOOCs Using Deep Learning Approaches
abstract: Using Internet, artificial intelligence and other technologies, online learning such as MOOCs provides us with new learning platforms and methods. In the paper, a transformer-based model for online learning prediction in MOOCs using deep learning approaches, namely ONLPSformer, is proposed. The model transforming the learner’s data to a sequential form and extracts feature information from students’ learning behavior using transformer-based mechanism model with their behavioral changes in online learning. After extracting feature information, the previous learning behavior data are combined to predict the students’ learning behavior and their learning effect. To verify the performances of the model, many experiments are conducted using the MOOCCubeX dataset. The experimental results show that the model achieved better effectiveness in learning prediction, compared with the traditional methods. The values of RMSE and MAE of the proposed method are 0.159 and 0.102, respectively, which are the smallest among the three models.

articleTitle: LiteATNet: Predicting APT Attack Using Transformer Model With MITRE ATT&CK Framework
abstract: With the increasing convergence of IT and OT environments in the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), attacks originating in IT systems are increasingly affecting OT assets, making network security in IIoT more critical than ever. Traditional intrusion detection systems often exhibit delays and struggle to effectively prevent advanced persistent threats (APTs). Therefore, understanding and predicting an attacker’s strategies is essential. However, existing attack prediction methods face challenges, such as dependence on specific network structures and the lack of standardized attack modeling. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Transformer-based lightweight attack prediction model, LiteATNet, which leverages the MITRE ATT&CK framework to model APT attacks in a standardized manner and predict attacker behavior at the level of specific techniques, independent of network structures. We also construct a dataset based on real APT attack cases. Experimental results demonstrate that our model effectively predicts attacker behavior and delivers competitive performance in multi-step intrusion scenarios.

articleTitle: Tailored Temperature for Student in Knowledge Distillation
abstract: In knowledge distillation, the temperature controls the shape of the model’s prediction probability distribution, thereby influencing the transfer of knowledge from the teacher. Most knowledge distillation methods simply fix the temperature, while a few studies employ a dynamic temperature improperly, both of which constrain the further progress of the distilled student model. In this paper, to address this issue, we present a method dubbed TTSD to distill with the temperature tailored for the student, which achieves label smoothing effectively according to the student’s performance. The tailored temperature consists of two parts: a learnable temperature (LT) and an adaptive temperature (AT), each functioning at different stages of student development (junior and senior). LT learns alongside the junior to find the optimal temperature, whereas in the senior stage, AT compensates for LT’s deficiencies through adaptation. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-100 ImageNet-2012, and Describable Textures Dataset (DTD) demonstrate that TTSD can effectively improve existing knowledge distillation frameworks.

articleTitle: Distributed Data Synthesis under Local Differential Privacy
abstract: Local Differential Privacy (LDP) has emerged as a cornerstone for safeguarding privacy in data analysis, enabling robust statistical inference without the need for a trusted intermediary. However, current LDP methods often lack scalability and applicability beyond specific tasks. In response, we propose a novel approach for locally differentially private data synthesis. Our method extracts representative marginals from user data to construct synthetic datasets that maintain statistical fidelity while adhering to differential privacy constraints. A primary challenge lies in selecting meaningful marginals and minimizing noise in LDP mechanisms tailored to domain size of each marginal. To tackle this, we employ a sliding overlapping window technique to effectively capture low-degree marginals that encapsulate critical dataset attributes. Furthermore, we adaptively utilize categorical frequency oracles (CFOs) to estimate marginal frequencies based on their respective domain sizes, thereby reducing noise levels and maintain data utility. Empirical evaluations on real-world datasets, including Twitter and Adult datasets, underscore the efficacy of our approach in preserving data utility across a spectrum of fundamental statistical tasks.

articleTitle: A Supply Chain Digital Twins Framework with Generative Knowledge Graph
abstract: With the explosive development of Artificial intelligence generated content(AIGC), generative AI technology has gradually been applied to supply chain optimization and management. However, current research lacks guiding principles and general framework for the application of generative AI in supply chain system optimization and management. To address this issue, this paper designs the supply chain digital twins framework with generative knowledge graph(SCDT-GKG), based on digital twin technology.Firstly, a foundational architecture for supply chain digital twins is proposed based on a five-dimensional model. Secondly, on this foundational architecture, a generative knowledge graph module is introduced to construct SCDT-GKG. Lastly, a general usage guide is provided, detailing the application processes in supply chain scenarios, thereby offering guidance for the construction and use of SCDT-GKG.This research effectively addresses the challenges of applying generative knowledge graph in supply chain systems and the issue of insufficient data. It also aids in achieving real-time collaborative optimization of supply chain system, paving the way for new method.

articleTitle: Guardians of Discourse: Evaluating LLMs on Multilingual Offensive Language Detection
abstract: Identifying offensive language is essential for maintaining safety and sustainability in the social media era. Though large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated encouraging potential in social media analytics, they lack thorough evaluation when in offensive language detection, particularly in multilingual environments. We for the first time evaluate multilingual offensive language detection of LLMs in three languages: English, Spanish, and German with three LLMs, GPT-3.5, Flan-T5, and Mistral, in both monolingual and multilingual settings. We further examine the impact of different prompt languages and augmented translation data for the task in non-English contexts. Furthermore, we discuss the impact of the inherent bias in LLMs and the datasets in the mispredictions related to sensitive topics.

articleTitle: Efficient Resource Allocation in Vehicular Networks Using Embedding-Enhanced MAPPO
abstract: With the swift advancement of automotive technology, the need for efficient allocation of resources in V2V (vehicle-to-vehicle) communications has grown significantly. However, the dynamic nature of channels in vehicular networks introduces considerable uncertainty in resource allocation. This research presents a novel approach to addressing these challenges by utilizing multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL). By leveraging shared resource blocks (RBs) for V2V and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications, our approach minimizes interference with V2I links and ensures optimal V2V performance. Unlike traditional methods that select actions sequentially, our approach treats every V2V link as an agent and simultaneously determines all agents’ actions to improve coordination and efficiency. To accelerate the training of the multi-agent critic network, we integrate an embedding module to simplify and compress the network input dimensions. Through the use of our embedding multi-agent proximal policy optimization (E-MAPPO) algorithm, the agents collaboratively optimize their transmission strategies to efficiently share spectrum with V2I links. Simulation results show that our method greatly minimizes interference with V2I links while meeting the stringent latency and reliability requirements of V 2 V communications, surpassing baseline approaches.

articleTitle: Context-Prompt-Align: An Architecture For Few Posts Based Social Bots Detection
abstract: In today’s opinion-driven world of social media, detecting social bots is crucial. However, current methods often rely on complex, deep models that present deployment challenges and computational burdens. In our paper, we propose a three-step approach: context, prompt, and align. Context involves applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to parse and comprehend usergenerated content, thereby gaining a nuanced understanding of social interactions. Prompt strategically utilizes LLMs with InContext Learning to distill a concise yet impactful set of user posts. These curated posts are transformed into User Personas, capturing the core behaviors and characteristics of social users. Align employs Graph NeuralNetworks (GNNs) to structure these User Personas within a heterogeneous social network graph. Our method achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods, utilizing just five user posts and constructing heterogeneous social network graphs. Furthermore, our lightweight approach minimizes noise in data features and reduces computational burdens, achieving effectiveness comparable to larger models even with smaller parameter settings. Through three experimental scenarios, we have validated the effectiveness and efficiency of our method, confirming the indispensable role of each module. The open-source code will be released at https://github.com/logpum/Context-Prompt-Align.

articleTitle: Advancing Haul Truck Safety: A Deep Neural Network-Based Driver Assistance System for Blind Spot Detection
abstract: The utilization of haul trucks within the mining industry presents a myriad of safety challenges, primarily due to their considerable size. Haul trucks serve as indispensable assets in large-scale construction projects, owing to their unparalleled capacity for transporting heavy loads. Tailored specifically for such rigorous tasks, these trucks are restricted to traversing non-crowded roads to uphold safety standards. Nonetheless, their sheer size and design contribute to numerous blind spots, rendering them challenging to operate. In this study, we address the issue of blind spots in haul trucks by proposing a cutting-edge machine vision system. Our innovative approach integrates machine vision technology with advanced Deep Neural Network (DNN) algorithms to detect objects within the truck’s blind spots and promptly alert the driver in real time. Leveraging a comprehensive dataset of images, the DNN is trained to identify objects of varying sizes and shapes accurately. To facilitate seamless monitoring, our system incorporates a visual display unit installed in the truck’s cab, offering the driver a real-time panoramic view of the surroundings. Initial testing conducted in controlled laboratory settings yielded promising results, with the DNN algorithm demonstrating high accuracy in object detection. To validate our concept, we opted to employ a standard car as a surrogate for the haul truck. Equipped with four strategically positioned cameras providing a 360 -degree field of view, we scaled down the truck’s dimensions to match those of a car. Utilizing the D455 Intel RealSense camera, we precisely measure the distances of detected objects and issue alerts to the driver within a 4 -meter range via a built-in buzzer. Our system is further fortified with the inclusion of the Jetson Orin Nano developer kit. Real-world testing conducted in a moving vehicle showcased the effectiveness of our system, garnering favorable results. Our endeavor underscores a significant step towards enhancing safety and operational efficiency in haul truck operations through innovative machine vision solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of a Glass Detection System Based on Context and Edge Attention Using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: The reflective and refractive properties of transparent glass, combined with its interactions with other objects, introduce challenges for the semantic segmentation of transparent glass scenes. Although existing methods utilize Fully Convolutional Networks (FCN) for segmentation, these models possess large parameter sizes, leading to low feature utilization, wasteful memory consumption, and intensive computational resources. Moreover, these models easy to lose the edge information specifically in transparent object scenes. In the paper, a glass detection system based on context and edge attention using deep learning methods are proposed. Firstly, the contextual information and edge attention are combined. The contextual information enhances the semantic understanding of transparent objects and the edge attention highlights the edge features of transparent objects. Secondly, the edge feature group module and edge attention module to effectively capture various boundary details and attain precise segmentation. Thirdly, the image context information and resolution are decreased by implementing the Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) and dense connectivity module, and the model complexity and parameter count are decreased. The experimental results validate the effectiveness of the method with reductions in both Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Balanced Error Rate (BER) to 0.068 and 4.41%, respectively. Additionally, Pixel Accuracy (PA) and Intersection over Union (IOU) demonstrated improvements to 92.51% and 89.64%, respectively.

articleTitle: EIMViT: A Model Integrating EEG Microstates and Deep Learning Methods for Depression Recognition
abstract: EEG microstates, which are stable electrophysiological states, can reflect the activity levels and connectivity patterns of specific brain regions, and they are considered potential biomarkers for depression. EEG microstates can reveal brain mechanisms, but the classification accuracy of depression recognition studies based on EEG microstates is low. In contrast, deep learning models have high accuracy but fail to reveal brain mechanisms. Therefore, we propose a model combining deep learning methods with EEG microstates, named EEGbased integrating microstates and Vision Transformer Network (EIMViT). This model takes EEG data as input into threedimensional convolutional neural network (3DCNN) module and Vision Transformer (ViT) module to extract local and global spatial features of the EEG data. Subsequently, the extracted spatial features are fused with the microstate temporal parameters to identify depression. The experimental results demonstrate that the EIMViT model achieved a recognition accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6 . 5 8 \%}$ on the MODMA dataset. Furthermore, statistical analysis of microstate temporal parameter results and ablative experiments confirmed strong correlations between microstate D and depression. The EEG source localization results indicated changes in the activation areas of each microstate in the depression group, potentially reflecting alterations in brain activity patterns among individuals with depression.

articleTitle: Overview of the Comprehensive Evaluation of Large Language Models
abstract: In recent years, the rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has attracted increasing interest from artificial intelligence researchers, and many large language models have emerged at home and abroad. These models have demonstrated amazing abilities in specific fields and have become important tools in the field of natural language processing. With the widespread promotion of large language models in research and daily application, it is increasingly important to conduct comprehensive testing on large language models. However, there is currently no clear methodology or unified technical standards for the comprehensive evaluation of large language models. In view of this, this paper will focus on the comprehensive evaluation of large language models, review the existing mainstream evaluation methods and standards. And based on this, the paper will explore the comprehensive assessment of large language models in various aspects, including intelligence, reliability, security, robustness, resource consumption, and social norms. This paper aims to provide a valuable reference for large language model researchers and developers and to promote the development and application of large language models.

articleTitle: A Speed-and-Performance Balancing Lightweight Network for Real-time Semantic Segmentation
abstract: In recent years, semantic segmentation has been able to achieve great segmentation performance, but it suffers from a large number of parameters and high computational expenses, making the model more complex and unfriendly to edge devices. The current lightweight semantic segmentation methods continue to face challenges with optimizing efficiency and maintaining accuracy. In order to better balance accuracy and performance, this research offers a lightweight bidirectional network for real-time semantic segmentation. First, a new spatial branching module was presented to minimize model parameters and computing costs while still incorporating channel and geographical calibration procedures. Second, there is a simple atrous spatial pyramid pooling module that increases the convolution kernel’s sense field while reducing computational cost and resolution. Finally, to enhance the model’s performance, a double-branch feature fusion module was created to merge low dimension and high dimension semantic features. Comparing our method against the baseline, we achieve a 1.4% improvement in mIoU and a $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ improvement in FPS on the Cityscapes test set. In the meantime, our method uses 32% fewer FLOPs and 34% fewer parameters.

articleTitle: USwin-HDRI: High Dynamic Range Imaging in Dynamic Scenes Combining Unet and Transformer
abstract: High Dynamic Range Imaging (HDRI) is crucial for capturing scenes with a wide range of luminance levels. Traditional methods often struggle with dynamic scenes due to issues like camera shake and object motion, leading to artifacts in the resultant images. To address these challenges, this paper presents a novel method for High Dynamic Range Imaging (HDRI) in dynamic scenes, called USwin-HDRI, which integrates UNet and Transformer technologies to address imaging challenges. The proposed network architecture includes an encoder, feature alignment subnet, feature enhancement subnet, decoder, and loss function design and implementation. By utilizing gamma correction, deformable convolutions, and the Swin Transformer, our method effectively aligns features, enhancing image consistency and detail preservation. Experimental results demonstrate that USwin-HDRI excels in reducing ghosting and maintaining image clarity compared to several traditional exposure fusion algorithms, showing superior performance in metrics such as PSNR and SSIM. Both subjective and objective analyses confirm the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Research on Rapid Metaverse Generation Technology of Industrial Tools for Intelligent Manufacturing Training Based on Industrial Metaverse
abstract: Industrial Metaverse plays an increasingly important role in Intelligent Manufacturing Training, improving the user immersion as well as reducing the cost and risks in training. As essential factor in live manufacturing, industrial tools like welding torch or hammer are frequently used but lack of rapid generation and convenient interaction in Industrial Metaverse. The NeuS algorithm based Metaverse Generation of industrial tools is researched, which combines the Self-Attention module to effectively distinguish simple industrial tools from the confusing factory background full of industrial equipment. Moreover, parallel processing of the generation tasks is proposed to improve the rapidity. The application of Rapid Metaverse Generation is finally demonstrated in the industrial metaverse of the intelligent manufacturing training through the homemade industrial tools dataset.

articleTitle: The Impact of Mobile Device Design on the Development of Mobile Gaming
abstract: The design of mobile devices has significantly impacted the development of mobile gaming, leading to profound changes in the gaming experience. This paper analyzes the evolution from early physical-key mobile phones to modern touchscreen smartphones, examining the influence of mobile device design on the development of mobile gaming. It also outlines the design principles for mobile games. The research findings indicate that as mobile device design has evolved, game development has progressively adapted to and capitalized on new interfaces and interaction forms. However, given that mobile phones are primarily communication tools, game design should prioritize the functionality of the phone before considering gaming features. The conclusion emphasizes that to enhance user experience, mobile game design should innovate in operational modes while ensuring that the communication functionality is preserved, thereby also meeting users’ demands for portability and convenience.

articleTitle: A Crowd Counting Method Based on Connected Field Image Generation of CSI Phase Difference
abstract: In response to the current low efficiency of CSI-based crowd-counting technology and the methods overly focus on debugging neural networks or mining more significant feature extraction methods, making the models complex and unstable in changing environments, the novel crowd-counting method named PhiC-Field is proposed in this paper, which is based on a cross-phase difference image generation technique. Firstly, the multi-antenna CSI subcarrier data is compressed and projected onto an orthogonal sampling field plane in pixel form. Secondly, by performing multi-point calculations, a blurred image reflecting the relationship between the number of people and the CSI subcarrier is obtained while preserving all subcarrier information without complex data preprocessing. This article proposes a neural network adapted to Phic-Field, and experiments in various experimental environments have shown that the accuracy of the model is higher than other methods.

articleTitle: Refined Reciprocally Convex Inequality for Less Conservative Stability Analysis of Systems with Interval Delay
abstract: This paper investigates problems related to the stability of time-varying delay systems using three new inequality lemmas. A constrained matrix inequality lemma and an unconstrained one, both of which concern high-order reciprocally convex combination, are proposed for analyzing asymptotic stability of the delayed system for networked control. A necessary and sufficient condition lemma is also established to ensure the negative definiteness of high-order matrix polynomials. A novel augmented Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional (LKF) with a third-order matrix polynomial on the interval delay is constructed to generate quartic matrix polynomials. The proven lemmas are exploited for the time derivative of LKF to expound delay-dependent stability criteria with reduced conservatism. Finally, a numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the raised criteria.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Gaussian and Student’s t Fusion for Distributed Target Tracking
abstract: In this paper, the heterogeneous fusion of the Kalman and Student’s t filters is considered in the context of distributed filter fusion for target tracking. This problem is involved in a multi-sensor tracking scenario where each sensor runs either a Kalman or Student’s t filter and they cooperate with each other via fusing the posterior density in a peer-to-peer fashion. This type of heterogeneous fusion has never been investigated before without closed-form solution. What is more, these sensors/filters are inherently correlated with each other to an unknown degree which raises a significant challenge for robust fusion. To address these challenges, both the arithmetic and geometric average fusion approaches are extended based on the appreciated moment matching strategies, in order to maintain the Gaussian or Student’s $\boldsymbol{t}$ distribution of the local posterior. The effectiveness and robustness of the proposed methods are verified through simulations which have demonstrated the superiority of arithmetic average fusion method over covariance intersection fusion and augmented measurement fusion.

articleTitle: Personalized Multi-Behavior Sequential Recommendation with Temporal-Aware Contrastive Learning and Self-Attention
abstract: Sequential recommendation (SR) is designed to capture sequential patterns and a user’s dynamic preferences from their historical interactions. Traditional sequential recommendation only considers a single behavior type of users, but in actual recommendation scenarios, users tend to produce multiple types of behaviors (e.g., page view, Add-to-favorite, purchase), so multi-behavior sequential recommendation (MBSR) is proposed. This paper aims to address the challenges posed by MBSR. First, users exhibit diverse and dynamic multi-behavior patterns due to different personal habits. Second, there are complex synergies between different behavior types and between behaviors and projects. In addition, existing MBSR methods do not fully consider the influence of time context. To address these challenges, we propose a Personalized Multi-Behavior Sequential Recommendation Framework (PMB) with Temporal-Aware Contrastive Learning and Self-Attention. Specifically, PMB first developed a personalized behavior awareness generator at the presentation layer to extract dynamic discriminant behavior patterns, then improved the self-attention mechanism through Sequential behavior aware collaborative extractor, and finally used time perception contrast learning. Used to model and learn vertical temporal proximity to project interactions between users. Finally, we conducted experiments on four benchmark datasets, demonstrating the effectiveness of PMB by significantly improving recommendation performance compared to various baseline models.

articleTitle: A Blind Driving System Leveraging Multimodal Feedback
abstract: Driving poses a significant challenge for blind and visually impaired (BVI) individuals, due to the loss of vision. Fortunately, the metaverse presents a promising platform where BVI individuals can experience independent driving just like sighted individuals. In order to assist such individuals in driving in the metaverse, we have devised a blind driving system that leverages multimodal feedback. We utilized stereo headphones and vibration motors to convey necessary information, including current and predicted vehicle states (i.e., speed, position, and direction) during driving, through sound, voice, and vibration feedback. Meanwhile, in order to improve the user-friendliness, we reduced the user’s information burden by data combination and compression. With the help of the multimodal feedback, BVI drivers could intuitively perceive the position and direction of the vehicle, thereby improving their driving experience. To evaluate the effectiveness of the system, we designed virtual scenarios to simulate a real driving environment, and we further devised two tasks: lane-keeping and lane-changing. We conducted user studies where sighted individuals wearing blindfolds were involved in the two tasks. The results suggest that our system demonstrates a beneficial effect in assisting BVI individuals in driving. Users could keep the vehicle in the center area of the lane for over ninety percent of driving time, and completed a lane-changing task with a high success rate. This study provides a potential solution for blind driving for BVI people by employing multimodal feedback.

articleTitle: Behavior Cognition Association Analysis with Heterogeneous Multimodal Causal Discovery
abstract: Describing the association between external behavior and internal cognition is significant for revealing the pathogenesis of cognitive diseases (e.g., dementia). Existing causal discovery methods perform well on homogeneous data, but struggle to handle heterogeneous multimodal data, due to the differences in data structure, distribution, and representation. Therefore, we propose a Heterogeneous Multimodal Causal Discovery method for Behavior Cognition Association Analysis (HMCD-BCA). This method employs Convolutional Auto-Encoder Network to extract features of heterogeneous multimodal data and map the multimodal data to a unified feature space. Based on consistent features, classical causal discovery algorithms are used to calculate causal associations between behavioral data and cognitive data. We validate our method on both simulated dataset and real behavior-cognition bimodal dataset. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in inferring causal associations between behavior and cognition.

articleTitle: Computation Pre-Offloading for MEC-Enabled Vehicular Networks via Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Task offloading is of paramount importance to efficiently orchestrate vehicular wireless networks, necessitating the availability of information regarding the current network status and computational resources. However, due to the mobility of the vehicles and the limited computational resources for performing task offloading in near-real-time, such schemes may require high latency, thus, become even infeasible. To address this issue, in this paper, we present a Trajectory Prediction-based Pre-offloading Decision (TPPD) algorithm for analyzing the historical trajectories of vehicles to predict their future coordinates, thereby allowing for computational resource allocation in advance. We first utilize the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network model to predict each vehicle’s movement trajectory. Then, based on the task requirements and the predicted trajectories, we devise a dynamic resource allocation algorithm using a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) that enables the edge server to minimize task processing delay, while ensuring effective utilization of the available computational resources. Our simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showcasing that, as compared with traditional real-time task offloading strategies, the proposed TPPD algorithm significantly reduces task processing delay while improving resource utilization.

articleTitle: A Priced Oblivious Transfer Scheme with Time Constraints for Mobile Edge Computing
abstract: The development of mobile edge computing has significantly influenced the popularity and adoption of products, including smart phones, smart appliances, smart wearable devices, etc. As consumers interact with websites or APPs, they provide their consumption data to service providers. Subsequently, service providers analyze consumer behavior with the help of smart data driven modeling (SDDM) so that they can offer more personalized and suitable products to consumers. However, this process raises concerns about user or group privacy and the potential leakage of sensitive information to the SDDM. Consequently, the primary objective of this paper is to ensure that the SDDM can analyze the users’ preferences effectively without knowing the privacy of the group members. A membership privacy group signature protocol with time constraints is proposed to guarantee the member has the authority to access APPs with valid signature periods. In addition, The proposed protocol protects the privacy of the user who joins in or leaves the group and time privacy. In addition, a priced oblivious transfer protocol is designed to protect the selection of members without exposing their privacy. The security and performance indicate that the proposed protocol can be instantiated in mobile edge computing with high security and efficiency.

articleTitle: Treasure Maps and Special Effects: The digital twin offering to threat actors
abstract: This paper considers the offering made to threat actors by the deployment of digital twins around Operational Technology (OT), IoT and Smart City environments. In the context of a model for threat actor types it explores misuse cases that may be possible given an available or compromised digital twin. We present a proposed methodology for red teaming a digital twin’s deployment that reduces risk whilst preserving utility. The common consultancy recommendation that security equivalence must be established is challenged given that a digital twin often represents a physical or cyber-physical system, with wider physical security and societal threats being identified.

articleTitle: DiagnoCare: A Diagnostic Analysis System for Electronic Medical Records Combining Medical Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model
abstract: With the rapid development of healthcare technologies and the increasing demand for intelligent diagnostic systems, we present a novel approach that combines medical knowledge graphs and Large Language Models (LLMs) for enhanced Electronic Medical Record (EMR) analysis and condition warning. Our system integrates structured medical knowledge with advanced text analysis capabilities to accurately interpret and process complex EMR data. By leveraging LLMs and prompt learning, the system provides personalized examination suggestions, diagnostic analyses, and disease warnings. Experimental results on real-world datasets, including the MIMIC III database and anonymized hospital records from Fujian Province, China, demonstrate the system’s efficacy in delivering precise and actionable insights. Case studies further illustrate the system’s practical value and usability, highlighting its potential to significantly improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. This research offers substantial implications for the advancement of intelligent EMR systems and personalized healthcare.

articleTitle: Question answering over temporal knowledge graphs based on hierarchical semantic extraction
abstract: Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering (TKGQA) aims to address problems with temporal constraints using a Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG). Existing models often overlook the structural information within problems, making it challenging to effectively manage complex temporal issues. To overcome these challenges, we propose the HSTQA model, which employs a hierarchical semantic extraction strategy to precisely capture semantic and implicit temporal information in queries. A multi-granularity fusion technique enhances the model’s capability to tackle problems with varying temporal granularities. Additionally, HSTQA incorporates graph convolutional networks to efficiently identify and integrate implicit temporal features and relational patterns. Extensive testing on the MultiTQ dataset shows that HSTQA improves Hits@1 by $\mathbf{1 0. 8 \%}$ compared to traditional methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing multi-granularity temporal problems and enhancing complex temporal reasoning.

articleTitle: VisionPlay: An Interactive Ball Game Using Computer Vision and Augmented-reality Overlay
abstract: This paper looks at how an integrated of technologies can be used for an enhancement of interactive gaming experience in digital sports. A prototype interactive ball game called ‘VisionPlay’ developed in our study offers a natural interactive experience with tennis balls using computer vision and augmented-reality (AR) overlay. We aim to provide a lightweight and cost-effective solution to achieve high tracking accuracy for the ball and precision for the real-time interaction with virtual game content overlaid in the physical environment. We describe some of the design decisions and technical challenges overcome in the development of our interactive game. This paper employs the Intersection-over-Union (IoU) method as the evaluation metric to validate the detection and tracking accuracy of our system, by following up with the qualitative analysis with questionnaires to evaluate the system’s performance and user perception. The IoU analysis demonstrates high accuracy and stability of object detection under different environmental conditions. The user study reveals significant improvement in participants’ exercise motivation and entertainment experience. The innovative form of interaction, enabled by real-time capturing of physical movements through the camera, provides an unparalleled degree of immersion and involvement.

articleTitle: BNKG: BERT-based Non-sampling Knowledge Graph Enhanced Recommendation
abstract: The topology of the knowledge graph (KG) encompasses rich semantic associations between entities and items, typically serving as auxiliary information to enhance the quality of recommendations. However, existing research faces two major challenges: data sparsity and the difficulty of mining the latent semantics of items. The performance of recommendations heavily relies on a high-quality KG, yet the long-tail distribution of entities results in semantic sparsity in KG-enhanced item embeddings. In the real world, user behavior patterns are complex and diverse, and ignoring potential user-item interactions leads to an inaccurate characterization of user behavior. To address these issues, a BERT-based non-sampling knowledge graph enhanced recommendation (BNKG) model was proposed. This model aims to mitigate the long-tail problem in recommender systems (RS) and mine the deep semantics between items. By leveraging the bidirectional encoder and feature extractor of a pre-trained model to semantically segment the relations in the KG, relation aggregation knowledge graphs (RAKG) were constructed. A knowledge aggregation mechanism was designed for each RAKG to integrate neighbor knowledge into item representations. By combining the KG with the user-item bipartite graph, a nonsampling strategy based on node centrality was adopted to learn user representations. Empirical results on two benchmark datasets indicate that the BNKG model achieves significant improvements compared to current advanced methods.

articleTitle: RaftFed: An Efficient Federated Learning Framework for Vehicular Crowd Intelligence
abstract: Vehicular crowd intelligence (VCI) is an emerging research field. Facilitated by state-of-the-art vehicular ad-hoc networks and artificial intelligence, various VCI applications come to place, e.g., collaborative sensing, positioning, and mapping. The collaborative property of VCI applications generally requires data to be shared among participants, thus forming network-wide intelligence. How to fulfill this process without compromising data privacy remains a challenging issue. Although federated learning (FL) is a promising tool to solve the problem, adapting conventional FL frameworks to VCI is nontrivial. First, the centralized model aggregation is unreliable in VCI because of the existence of stragglers with unfavorable channel conditions. Second, existing FL schemes are vulnerable to NonIID data, which is intensified by the data heterogeneity in VCI. Third, the dynamic nature of vehicular networks necessitates robust handling of nodes frequently opting in and out. This paper proposes a novel dual-layer federated learning framework called RaftFed to facilitate efficiently privacy-preserving VCI. By integrating with heartbeat and cache mechanisms, RaftFed is endowed with dynamic and asynchronous capabilities. The experimental results also show that RaftFed performs better than baselines regarding communication overhead, model accuracy, and model convergence.

articleTitle: The Prediction Error Bound in Urban Crime: Temporal Predictability
abstract: Predicting when and where crime occurs is essential and a significant task to support preventive policing. This subsequently has important outcomes for economic benefits, urban planning and human safety—predictability, which is a theoretical bound for the prediction of performance in human behavior based on limited data. Current approaches to predictability in human behavior usually measure prediction accuracy which is aimed at classification issues such as the next location of prediction and the lack of measurement for regression problems. To further research in this area, this study proposes a new method based on differential entropy to compute the prediction error as a form of mean square error to derive the minimum level of error referred to as temporal predictability. Special emphasis is placed on investigating the sensitivity of the predictability methods with regard to changing the data lengths. The method was evaluated using public crime datasets from four cities (Washington DC, Denver, New York, and Vancouver) collected between 2016 and 2022. The results from the study support the hypothesis of correlation between the minimum amount of data and the level of temporal predictability, which can guide the prediction of the regression issue.

articleTitle: AI and Personal Data in the Metaverse: A Risk Assessment
abstract: Artificial Intelligence, in combination with other Metaverse technologies such as AR/VR/MR, can create realistic virtual worlds and engaging experiences. Body worn sensors allow human movements, reactions, and even emotions to be recognised by AI models. This enables a user’s behaviour in the real world to be relayed to their avatar in the Metaverse automatically. The collection and processing of such personal data is a cornerstone of Metaverse development. However, security, privacy, and safety are common concerns amongst users, and protections must be built into the Metaverse’s architecture to ensure that individuals and their privacy are kept safe. Policies, regulations, and procedures are needed to enact user protection, privacy, and security. Current academic literature on AI use in the Metaverse reviews various AI techniques and maps them to opportunities, but the associated risks and threats are not analysed. Conversely, surveys on the use of biometric data within AI systems are not specific to the Metaverse and the rich sources of information associated with cyber-physical environments. This paper aims to deepen the conversations around personal data in the Metaverse and expose the risks associated with AI processing.

articleTitle: TL-Fuser: Layout-Sensitive Scene Generation for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Recent advances in generating realistic images from image captions have enabled the synthesis of traffic scenes from textual descriptions. However, scene synthesis for autonomous driving is more challenging as the spatial relationship of objects in the traffic scene is important for decision making, and existing solutions fail in positional representation. To address this problem, in this paper we propose TL-Fuser, a novel framework for layout-sensitive scene generation under the guidance of textual description and layout constrains. In TL-Fuser, we propose a multimodal fusion approach that allows precise control over the position of objects in an image by integrating descriptive language with bounding box information. To enhance the consistency and fidelity of both semantics and layout in the generated images, a multi-scale attention mechanism is proposed for feature fusion. We conduct extensive experiments on the open-domain MSCOCO and COCO-Traffic datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that TL-Fuser outperforms GAN-based solutions for image synthesis, and shows superior performance in positional information representation against diffusion-based models and even visual large language models. This implies that TL-Fuser can be used to synthesize traffic scenes for the efficient testings of autonomous driving systems.

articleTitle: IFVONet: Integrating Inter-Frame Variation and Occlusion Awareness for 3D Hand Mesh Reconstruction
abstract: Reconstructing 3D hand meshes from video files is significantly challenging due to objects in the video often occluding the hand during manipulation. These occlusions can greatly reduce the quality of information extracted from the obscured regions and decrease temporal hand coherence over time. Existing approaches focus primarily on global occlusion regions but overlook temporal hand coherence, which limits their performance. Herein, we propose a novel framework called IFVONet, designed to improve 3D hand mesh reconstruction by effectively capturing inter-frame variations and improving the recovery of global occlusions. IFVONet comprises three key components: (1) Pixel-Domain Variation Module for identifying inter-frame variations across adjacent frames, enhancing temporal hand coherence. (2) Enhanced Global Occlusion Recovery Module for integrating hand information into global occlusion representation, thereby improving the accuracy of occlusion feature recovery. (3) Hand Regression Module for dynamically aggregating hand information from inter-frame variations and globally recovered occlusion features into comprehensive hand representations, ultimately leading to enhanced 3D hand reconstruction. Extensive experiments on the HO3D-v2 and HO3D-v3 datasets demonstrate that our proposed IFVONet achieves state-of-the-art performance on both 3D hand mesh reconstruction and pose estimation.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Digital Human Identity Attribute Synthesis
abstract: In the 21st century, the digitization of the economy and society has profoundly impacted various sectors worldwide, including healthcare, transportation, education, and entertainment. Concurrently, technological advancements have significantly reduced the costs associated with data collection, storage, and analysis. Electronic data, particularly digital identity attribute information, plays a crucial role in personalized recommendations and medical diagnostics, thereby significantly influencing individuals’ quality of life. However, stringent regulations such as the Personal Information Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) impose strict limitations on the sharing of digital identity information, which adversely affects the effectiveness of data sharing.To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel digital identity attribute generation system leveraging deep neural networks. This system innovatively generates the text and image components of identity information using Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) and Stable Diffusion Models (SDM), respectively. Our experimental results demonstrate that this system can produce high-quality multimodal digital identity attribute information in real-world applications. This work not only facilitates data sharing in sensitive domains while adhering to regulatory and privacy constraints but also significantly contributes to the advancement of the digital industry by enhancing the reliability and applicability of digital identity generation techniques.

articleTitle: HiCrowd: Hierarchical Multi-hop Crowdsourcing Delivery by Leveraging the Crowd of Taxi
abstract: Delivery by the crowd has become an alternative to the traditional delivery services thanks to the advances in ubiquitous computing, where abundant taxi data can be collected from mobile devices and infrastructures. To cater to this trend, the goal of this paper is to exploit potential and occupied taxi rides for logistics services so as to improve transportation efficiency. This is formulated as a city-wide multi-hop package routing problem composed of two sub-problems, where a package is delivered from one interchange station to another (package dispatching problem) by exploiting users’ daily commuting pattern (taxi ride matching problem). The previous works solve this two-level of reasoning in a separate and empirical manner. Therefore, we propose HiCrowd, a Hierarchical multi-hop Crowdsourcing delivery scheme for the co-design of these two sub-problems, comprising a high-level dispatching policy and a low-level goal-conditioned taxi selection policy. The major technical challenge we tackle is to optimize these policies collaboratively. Based on the insight of hierarchical reinforcement learning, the interchange station output of high-level policy is set as a series of subgoals, and the low-level policy aims to reach those subgoals, allowing for control and learning concurrently at two levels. Finally, we conduct extensive numerical studies using the real-world ride dataset in Chengdu to confirm the superiority of our model compared with some crowdsourcing baselines in terms of package delivery time, taxi detour, and service quality of passengers.

articleTitle: CERG-KBQA: Advancing KBQA-Systems through Classification, Enumeration, Ranking, and Generation Strategies
abstract: Knowledge Base Question Answering (KBQA) systems are critical for retrieving accurate information from structured data in response to natural language queries. Existing approaches, however, often fall short in coverage and generalization, especially in compositional and zero-shot situations. To mitigate these issues, we introduce CERG-KBQA, a novel framework that employs classification, enumeration, ranking, and generation strategies to enhance logical form candidate coverage and system generalization. We provide a suite of diverse logical form templates designed to accommodate various question types, effectively improving the coverage of logical form candidates. To enhance generalization capability, shuffled candidate augmentation is proposed to prevent positional bias and promote a more equitable consideration of candidates. Our framework is thoroughly tested on the GRAILQA and WEBQSP datasets, demonstrating significant improvements over baseline models, particularly in compositional generalization. With an F1 score of 77.0 on GRAILQA and 78.4 on WEBQSP, CERG-KBQA’s robust performance solidifies its effectiveness across diverse KBQA scenarios, providing a versatile solution for complex KBQA tasks.

articleTitle: NESpMV: NEON-Enhanced SpMV Algorithm for NUMA Architectures
abstract: Iterative methods are used to solve large-scale, sparse linear equations to approximate the exact solutions in various real-world applications, such as CG, GMRES, SOR, Jacobi and so on. Sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV), the primary computational step, usually must be performed thousands of times in the iterative solution. However, the complexity of the underlying hardware architectures and the sparse characteristics of sparse matrices lead to unbalanced computational loads and memory access bottlenecks, which makes it challenging to accelerate the performance of SpMV. ARMv8-A is a high-performance computing processor architecture launched by ARM. It provides the Non-Uniform Memory Access (NUMA) architecture, multiple cores, and SIMD instructions to improve parallel float-precision computing capabilities. This paper introduces a novel compression sparse row (NeCSR) format that leverages the NEON technique, which is an ARM Advanced SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) extension. NEON facilitates parallel processing of data, allowing for efficient handling of operations on multiple data points simultaneously. By applying NEON in the context of sparse matrix storage, the NeCSR format enhances data locality and computational performance by grouping data with similar characteristics into the same processing units. For example, 4 float data, named a vector pair, can be stored simultaneously in the 128 -bit vector register. This paper calculates the vector pair with the smallest unit in subsequent calculations instead of simply performing computations on nonzero elements. Correspondingly, this paper designs a NUMAaware distribution strategy to address the issue of cross-node memory access during the computation process and ensure that threads on each node only access local memory on the current node. We select 13 data sets from SuitSparse and test the performance of NESpMV on the Kunpeng 920 processor. The experimental results show that NESpMV gains a performance improvement of $59.5 \%$ compared with PETSc.

articleTitle: Toward Automated End-to-End Workflow Deployment In Dynamic Large-Scale Data Center Network With Multi-Vendor Devices
abstract: Complex data center network providers have long been characterized by their closed and proprietary nature. A programmatic approach allows for the dynamic management of network entities that can simplify and streamline the deployment, configuration, and management processes while building the foundational tools towards an open standards Software Defined Networking (SDN). The introduction of a new automated model into the data center network world immensely enhances programmability. As increasingly complicated multivendor networks emerge, the need for a new automation model becomes even more critical. A dynamic workflow provides an avenue for the engineering teams to automate the multi-vendor device onboarding process, without having to rely on manual configuration and provisioning, thus reducing the time and effort for the heterogeneous network entities. This paper expands this vision, describing some of the motivating use cases in more detail, delineating our proposed architecture and implementation, chronicling our progress to date, and outlining future plans.

articleTitle: The Revolution in 3D Animation Film Production Process Under Artificial Intelligence Technology
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology has made breakthrough progress in the field of 3D animation film production, especially since 2022 with the rise of generative AI, which has brought a completely new look to the animation field. This article provides a literature review of current technologies and systematically summarizes some of the most important technological developments and case studies in the 3D animation field between 2021 and 2024, summarizing the impact of AI technology on the industrialized process of 3D animation film production. We systematically reviewed relevant literature and industry reports, focusing on in-depth research from perspectives such as AI-generated video content technology, AI-generated 3D animation, the role of AI in 3D reconstruction, and AI-driven character animation. In this study, we summarize the advantages that AI technology can bring to the film and television industry and design a universally applicable AI-driven industrialized process for film and television production. This process, combined with current successful film and television cases and cutting-edge technologies, can provide multiple possibilities for the use of AI assistants in the film and television industry.

articleTitle: Not Just Imitation: Enhancing Role-Playing Through Retrieve Fine-Tuned Collaborative Large Language Model
abstract: In this paper, we focus on enhancing the credibility and personalization of large language models in role-playing scenarios, aiming to facilitate natural and believable humancomputer interaction. Current dialogue systems often fall short in accurately portraying character styles, leading to issues of role illusion. To address this, we introduce an innovative method, the Retrieve Fine-Tuned Collaborative Large Language Model (RFTC-LLM), which employs a two-stage strategy combining fine-tuning with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). By employing instruction-based fine-tuning, the model is directed to learn the character’s expression style and preferences, and the use of a role-specific knowledge graph aids in constraining responses to ensure relevance and avoid misleading answers. This approach effectively resolves the confusion surrounding role-specific knowledge, thereby boosting the credibility and authenticity of the dialogue system. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our method across multiple role-playing dialogue datasets, particularly in significantly reducing instances of role illusion.

articleTitle: A Multi-prototype Fusion approach for Few-shot Relation Extraction
abstract: Enhanced prototype networks have shown commendable performance in few-shot relation extraction tasks. However, existing methods fail to make reasonable use of additional information and overlook the potential of query information to optimize relational prototypes. This results in a diminished ability to represent certain relational prototypes. Drawing inspiration from the human learning process, this study proposes a Multi-Prototype Fusion (MPF) approach for few-shot relation extraction. The method integrates additional information through an attention mechanism, which mitigates the problem of missing relational information caused by the addition approach. In addition, the model introduces a dynamic interaction using query instances that are directly involved in the training of relational prototypes. This approach not only optimizes the relational prototypes but also trains the model’s discriminative ability, thereby enhancing its cognitive ability for the task. Experimental results show that our model improved the average accuracy of the four tasks on the FewRel dataset by ${2 . 0 6 \%}$ compared to a strong neural baseline.

articleTitle: CAPter: Controllable Data Privacy Enhancement for Deep Learning Inference Services
abstract: The deep learning’s outstanding performance and high overhead facilitate the popular intelligent web service, i.e., deep learning inference service (DLIS). However, DLISes require users to send their personal data to the remote server, which raises a severe risk of data privacy compromise. Some works have been proposed to mitigate this problem, but they all preset a determined data protection goal, e.g., finding a single sweet point that balances privacy and utility. The preset protecting goal neglects the protection needs of different users. In this paper, we propose, CAPter, a controllable data privacy enhancement solution for DLISes to meet users’ different protection needs in practical DLIS usage. It takes as input the user data and enhancement level and enhances the data in a controllable data information reduction way. CAPter works without any prior knowledge of the private attributes. Comprehensive experiments that CAPter can effectively prevent the secondary inference attack and reconstruction attack by sacrificing 0.01 to 0.02 in accuracy and outperforms the baseline.

articleTitle: Autonomous Planning for On-Board Adaptive Remote Sensing Transmission
abstract: The enormous increase of in-orbit satellites, exemplified by mega constellations like Starlink, highlights the scarcity of on-board resources in Earth-imaging satellites, which struggle to meet the high demand and transmit large volume of remote sensing images generated due to limited computing hardware, battery capacity, and available time windows. In addition, the limited downlink bandwidth also makes the real-time transmission of high-resolution remote sensing images to the ground challenging. In this paper, an adaptive planning method is proposed for resolution allocation of image transmission, which considers both image content and dynamic downlink capacity. Aiming at onboard autonomy, regions of interest (ROIs) are first extracted accurately in a high speed by utilizing multi-scale hybrid saliency mapping in combination with semantic refinement. In order to adapt to the dynamics of downlink bandwidth, the nonRoIs are proactively downsampled by optimizing the trade-off between data volume and the real-time prediction of transmission speed. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide efficient remote sensing image transmission, significantly reducing the redundant data and alleviating the transmission pressure to ground stations within the constraints of limited on-board environments.

articleTitle: A Scalable and Timely Data Auditing Scheme for Metaverse
abstract: The metaverse is a new trend in virtual reality applications, and data storage and management commonly rely on distributed storage systems. The integrity of the stored data has become a key concern in the metaverse. Furthermore, the scalability of data storage is a significant characteristic of the metaverse. Therefore, it is essential to provide a scalable data auditing approach for distributed outsourcing storage systems. However, the existing data auditing schemes do not fully consider the timeliness of auditing, which is a shred of important evidence for users to ensure the storage status. In this paper, we propose a scalable data auditing scheme with timeliness, which supports scalable data storage and timestamp updates. By leveraging the blockchain infrastructure, our scheme ensures the fairness and transparency of the data auditing process in a distributed storage system. To achieve efficiency in scalable data auditing, our scheme uses pseudo-indexed linked lists by ordinary arrays to store the relevant information needed for data auditing, which can effectively support resource-constrained blockchain for on-chain auditing. Finally, we analyze the computational cost, communication overhead, and storage overhead of the scheme theoretically, verify the correctness of the scheme and compare the efficiency of the key algorithms experimentally.

articleTitle: Evaluating and Bridging the Effectiveness of Privacy Desensitization Algorithms of Different Principles Based on Information Loss
abstract: In response to the rise of various privacy desensitization algorithms, evaluating their actual desensitization effectiveness is essential. However, there is a lack of a unified evaluation metric to assess these algorithms which are based on different principles. In this paper, we propose an approach to evaluate the effectiveness of various privacy desensitization algorithms and to link them together based on information loss. Specifically, we outline a framework that encompasses the data collection, desensitization, and assessment processes, followed by calculating information loss using conditional total correlation as a metric of desensitization effectiveness. Using anonymity algorithms based on generalization and differential privacy algorithms based on perturbation as case studies, we conducted our experiments on Adult dataset, analyzing the impact of different desensitization algorithms, as well as varying parameter settings of the same algorithm on the desensitization effectiveness. The findings indicate that our information loss metric aligns with intrinsic metrics within algorithms of the same principle. In addition, it provides an approach to map parameters among desensitization algorithms of different principles.

articleTitle: Multi-View Decoupling Framework for Emotion Recognition in Conversations
abstract: Emotion Recognition in Conversations (ERC) has always been a highly focused research topic in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI). The emotions of dialogues are not only dependent on the current discourse, but are also influenced by the context. Although recent studies have put forward various methods to address the issue, they are still insufficient to capture emotion shifts and context dependencies in conversations, leading to limited accuracy in emotion classification. To address this challenge, we propose an innovative emotion recognition framework, Multi-View Emotion Recognition Framework(MVERF), based on Multi-View Encoder and Decoupled Contrastive Learning. Specifically, an optimistic perspective encoder and a pessimistic perspective encoder are designed to independently capture optimistic and pessimistic emotions respectively, to ensure that both perspectives’ emotions are preserved and complementary. The unified emotion representation, as well as context embedding in dialogues, is then fed into a multi-head attention mechanism to capture multi-layered information, allowing for a better understanding of context and enhancing the accuracy in identifying emotion shifts. Decoupled contrastive Learning is exploited to avoid mutual interference between positive and negative samples, ensuring the purity and differentiation of emotion representation. In addition, a momentum contrast mechanism is raised to maintain a dynamic sample queue and to increase the number and diversity of negative samples. Extensive experimental results indicate that our proposed model exhibits excellent performance on the ERC task.

articleTitle: SKSP: Selected Kernel Spatial Pattern Analysis in Euclidean and Hilbert Space for Decoding Motor Imagery
abstract: Brain-computer Interface (BCI) has promising prospects as the most active research direction in the fields of brain science and artificial intelligence. The Common Spatial Pattern (CSP) algorithm has attracted extensive attention and has been demonstrated to be effective for Motor Imagery (MI) tasks. However, CSP is limited to capturing complex nonlinear characteristics under its linear assumption. Many variants of CSP cannot deal with multiple relationships simultaneously. This paper proposes a Selected Kernel Spatial Pattern (SKSP) algorithm for human behavior recognition. Electroencephalogram (EEG) signals are projected onto a high-dimensional Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space (RKHS) by the selected kernel function, where the nonlinear relationship is transformed into a linear one. This approach exploits wavelet transform and CSP patterns to compute the energy spectrum and differential entropy of data in RKHS to represent EEG patterns of brain activities. In addition, a multi-view module was proposed to strengthen pattern representations, which employs mutual information maximization to select the optimal sliding window in both frequency and time domains. The experiments are conducted on the BCI Competition IV-2a dataset. The four classes’ classification accuracy reaches 92% in subject seven. The proposed method outperforms the best state-of-the-art classification method by 4% in average subject accuracy.

articleTitle: Data Sinks Deployment for Backbone-Assisted Real-Time PD-NOMA Networks based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Real-time performance is one of the most vital metrics in Backbone-assisted Power-Domain Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Wireless Networks(BA-PDNOMAWNs) for Industrial Internet of Things applications. Since the relative geographic relationship between data sinks and wireless sensors affects real-time performance greatly, setting reasonable locations for data sinks is thus a feasible way to achieve high real-time performance for the scenarios where wireless sensors are not mobile. In this paper, we model the problem of finding the optimal locations for given sinks in BA-PDNOMAWNs so as to minimize uplink transmission latency. To find a low-complexity algorithm, we first formalize the problem as a Markov Decision Process, and then propose a reinforcement learning algorithm based on the classic Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient, where its reward function is designed elaborately to accelerate convergences. Experimental results show that multiple data sinks in the BAPDNOMAWNs can reduce uplink transmission latency by $2.2 \times$ compared to that with a single data sink. Additionally, compared to the classic Simulated Annealing optimization algorithm and the other siting algorithms, such as Clustering Center and Grid Partitioning in BA-PDNOMAWNs, our proposed algorithm can even reduce the uplink transmission delay by $2 \times$, thus achieving better real-time performance.

articleTitle: Heterophilic Graph Representation Learning Based on Multi-Order Information Extraction and High and Low Pass Filters
abstract: Real-world networks can be divided into homophilic and heterophilic graphs. Significantly, many nodes tend to be heterophilic in a homophilic graph. Graph representation learning in heterophilic graphs has attracted considerable significance in recent years as it breaks the homophily assumption and achieves higher-quality graph embeddings.
